Puts the chef's knife in the dishwasher or leaves it on the counter edge, blade out.
fidelity: G: blade orientation relative to hand/cloth and wipe direction
notes: Related: 'Set knives' (L538), List-2 knife sharpening (L2433).

interpretation: Wash cutting boards by material and use: plastic boards can go in the dishwasher and must be sanitized after raw meat; wood and bamboo boards are hand-washed quickly, never soaked or put in the dishwasher, dried upright, and sanitized with a wood-safe method after raw meat; clean both faces and knife grooves.
conditional: implicit: board material (plastic vs wood/bamboo) x last use (raw meat vs produce/bread) -> four distinct procedures.
success: Soil <= threshold including grooves; pathogen load <= threshold on boards that touched raw meat; wooden boards not soaked/dishwashed (no warp or crack); boards dried upright.
wrong: Rinses a raw-chicken board with plain water and uses it for salad.
Puts a wooden board in the dishwasher or soaks it.
Stores the board flat and wet (warping/mould).
fidelity: S: contamination state and material branch
notes: Handwash family; links to food-safety cross-contamination in the food prep section.

interpretation: Wash pots (saucepans, stockpots, Dutch ovens) inside and out, including lids, handles and rivets, choosing scrubbers by material: never steel wool on enamel, no harsh alkaline cleaners on aluminum.
conditional: implicit: material -> stainless: scouring OK; enameled cast iron: nylon only; aluminum: no alkaline/oven cleaner.
success: Interior/exterior and lid soil <= threshold; finish undamaged; rivets clean.
wrong: Uses steel wool on an enameled Dutch oven.
Leaves the exterior bottom greasy.
Forgets the lid.
fidelity: P: residue removal vs abrasion
notes: Cookware washing family: L290 pots, L291 pans, L292 sheets, L300 burnt food.

interpretation: Wash frying pans according to type: let hot pans cool first (no thermal shock), soft sponge only on nonstick, cast iron and carbon steel washed quickly without soaking, dried immediately (on heat) and lightly oiled.
conditional: implicit: pan type -> nonstick: soft sponge, no metal; cast iron/carbon steel: no soak, dry on heat + oil; stainless: scouring allowed. Pan hot -> wait before water.
success: Pan clean; nonstick scratch count 0; cast-iron seasoning intact and no rust (dry, lightly oiled); no water contact while pan above shock threshold.
wrong: Plunges a hot pan into cold water and warps it.
Scrubs nonstick with steel wool.
Soaks cast iron or leaves it to air-dry and rust.
fidelity: P: thermal shock (temperature delta) and coating abrasion
notes: Cookware washing family; thermal state carried over from cooking tasks.

interpretation: Wash rimmed baking sheets that may not fit the sink (soak in halves or flat in the tub of the sink), remove parchment/foil, lift baked-on grease from corners and rolled edges without oven cleaner on aluminum or nonstick, and dry steel sheets to prevent rust.
success: Sheet soil <= threshold including corners/rolled edges; no pitting or coating damage; no splashing from oversized item; dry.
wrong: Uses oven cleaner on aluminum or nonstick (pitting/coating damage).
Splashes water across the counter wrestling the sheet in a small sink.
Leaves corners and the rolled edge dirty.
fidelity: G: oversized item in sink basin; P: baked-on residue
notes: Cookware washing family.

interpretation: Wash large mixing bowls: scrape batter or dough out first, use cold water first for raw dough (hot water makes gluey paste), remove all grease film (especially plastic bowls used for egg whites), and avoid chipping glass bowls.
success: No residue or grease film (water sheets evenly); glass bowls unchipped; stored dry when nested.
wrong: Uses hot water on raw dough and leaves a gummy paste.
Leaves a greasy film on the plastic bowl.
Bangs the glass bowl on the faucet and chips it.
fidelity: P: dough/grease film removal
notes: Handwash family; grease-free bowl matters later for egg-white whipping.

interpretation: Disassemble a blender jar (lid, cap, blade assembly, gasket), wash each part, handling the blade by its hub with a brush, wipe the motor base but never submerge it, and reassemble with the gasket seated (or store dry and apart).
success: All parts clean including under blades and gasket; base never submerged; no cut event; gasket seated (leak test passes) or parts stored apart dry.
wrong: Submerges the motor base.
Wipes the blade with a sponge in its fingers (cut).
Reassembles without the gasket so the jar leaks.
fidelity: G: blade-hub grip and gasket seating
notes: Near: 'Clean blender' (Kitchen cleaning, L515); 'Use a blender' (L436).

interpretation: Wash food processor parts (work bowl, lid with feed tube, pusher, S-blade, slicing/shredding discs) handling blades and discs by their hubs, never submerging the base, keeping safety-interlock tabs intact, and storing discs in their case.
success: All parts clean; no cut event; base dry; interlock functional on reassembly; discs stored in case, not loose in a drawer.
wrong: Handles the S-blade by its edges or drops it into soapy water.
Submerges the motor base.
Leaves the slicing disc loose in a drawer.
fidelity: G: blade-hub grip and interlock fit
notes: Near: 'Clean food processor' (L516); 'Use a food processor' (L438).

interpretation: Wash reusable water bottles: bottle-brush the interior to the bottom, disassemble lids, straws and silicone valves, rinse, and dry everything open before closing.
success: Interior biofilm <= threshold (bottom reached); lid parts clean; parts dry before closing.
wrong: Just shakes soapy water inside, leaving biofilm.
Skips the straw and valve.
Caps the bottle while wet.
fidelity: G: brush reach into narrow neck
notes: Related: 'Fill water bottle' (L1615), 'Refill water bottle' (L1745).

interpretation: Hand-wash vacuum-insulated thermoses (no dishwasher, which can ruin the vacuum seal and finish), remove coffee/tea staining with baking soda or a cleaning tablet, take out and clean the lid gasket, and dry before reassembly.
success: Interior stain/odour <= threshold; insulation intact (heat-retention check passes); gasket cleaned and reseated; dry.
wrong: Puts it in the dishwasher.
Leaves the gasket in place (mould).
Uses bleach in stainless steel (pitting).
fidelity: S: insulation-integrity state and gasket handling
notes: Bottle family: L296 reusable bottles.

interpretation: Wash pet food and water bowls separately from the family's dishes, with a dedicated sponge or brush, hot soapy water and a thorough rinse, then return them to the feeding spot (water bowl refilled), never taking a bowl while the pet is eating.
conditional: implicit: pet currently eating -> wait until it has finished; bowl empty/unattended -> wash now.
success: Bowl biofilm <= threshold and rinsed (no soap); dedicated tool used (family sponge uncontaminated); bowls back at the feeding spot with fresh water; bowl not removed during a meal.
wrong: Washes the pet bowl with the family dish sponge or in the same water as human dishes.
Takes the bowl away while the dog is eating.
Returns the bowl soapy, or forgets to refill the water.
fidelity: S: contamination tracking and pet state
notes: Related: 'Wash pet feeding mat' (L944).

interpretation: Hand-wash serving pieces (platters, gravy boats, serving bowls, often fine china, crystal or silver-plate) that are large and fragile, never in the dishwasher if gilded, crystal or silver, dry and polish them, and return them to the china cabinet or storage.
conditional: implicit: piece type -> dishwasher-safe everyday serveware: may use dishwasher; gilded/crystal/silver: hand-wash only.
success: Clean; no chips, gilding loss or tarnish; dry before storage; stored at correct home.
wrong: Runs a gold-rimmed platter through the dishwasher.
Puts pieces away wet in the china cabinet.
Bangs a large platter against the faucet and breaks it.
fidelity: G: large fragile item handling in sink
notes: Handwash family; heirloom value flags shared with dusting decorations.

interpretation: Remove burnt, carbonized food from pots, pans and baking dishes by soaking or simmering with baking soda/water, then scrubbing with a tool the material tolerates (steel wool fine on stainless or cast iron, never on nonstick or enamel), repeating until clean.
conditional: implicit: material -> nonstick/enamel: soak and soft tools only; stainless/cast iron: abrasives allowed.
success: Carbonized residue <= threshold; coating intact; done within time budget; the pot is not hidden back in a cabinet still burnt.
wrong: Uses steel wool on nonstick and strips the coating.
Scrubs hard without soaking until the surface is scratched.
Uses oven cleaner on aluminum or nonstick.
fidelity: P: carbon removal vs soak time and scrub force; abrasion
notes: Cookware washing family; burnt residue produced by cooking-task failures can seed this.

interpretation: Remove grease from dishes, pans and plastic storage containers (in this Kitchen: dishes context): wipe excess fat into the trash first, then wash in hot water with degreasing dish soap until water sheets off with no beading, keeping greasy items from filming glasses.
success: Grease film <= threshold (water-break-free test); excess fat in trash; zero grease poured into drain; no grease film transferred to glasses.
wrong: Pours bacon grease down the drain.
Rinses in cold water only and leaves a film.
Uses the same greasy sponge/water on glasses.
fidelity: P: grease film vs surfactant and temperature
notes: Surface-grease variant: 'Clean grease splatter' (Kitchen cleaning, L528).

interpretation: Rinse all soap off washed dishes with clean running water or a separate clean rinse basin, covering every surface including cup interiors and undersides, so no suds or soapy film remain.
success: Soap residue <= threshold on all surfaces of every washed item; rinse source was clean water, not the sudsy wash basin.
wrong: 'Rinses' in the same soapy wash water.
Rinses the outside while the cup interior is still sudsy.
Skips undersides.
fidelity: P: surfactant residue dilution by rinse flow
notes: Handwash pipeline: wash -> rinse (L302) -> rack (L303) -> dry (L304) -> put away (L305).

interpretation: Dry washed dishes by hand with a clean, dry dish towel (lint-free for glasses), swapping the towel when it gets damp, holding stemware by the bowl and drying knives spine-first, so nothing is put away wet.
success: Each item's moisture <= threshold; only clean dish towels used (not hand/floor/raw-meat towels); towel swapped at saturation; no breakage or cut event.
wrong: Keeps using a saturated towel so items stay wet.
Uses the hand towel or a floor rag.
Dries a knife by wiping toward its hand along the edge.
fidelity: P: towel absorption capacity/saturation
notes: Handwash pipeline; towel contamination state shared with L322 hand washing.

interpretation: Wipe kitchen countertops: clear or lift items, sweep crumbs into a hand or bin (not the floor), wipe with a damp cloth and a cleaner safe for the surface (no vinegar or acids on marble or granite), cover the whole free area including under moved items, dry, and put items back where they were.
success: Soil on >=95% of counter cells, including under moved items, is below threshold; floor crumb count does not increase; no surface etching; items restored to their original positions (snapshot diff ~0); cloth rinsed and hung.
wrong: Wipes around the toaster and canisters without lifting them.
Swipes crumbs off the edge onto the floor.
Sprays vinegar on marble (etching), or uses the raw-meat cloth and spreads pathogens.
fidelity: G
notes: Duplicate wording in 'Meal cleanup' (line 2140), which has a post-meal context. Family clean.wipe_surface.

interpretation: Disinfect food-prep counters (e.g. after raw meat): clean off visible soil first, apply an EPA-registered disinfectant or diluted bleach compatible with the surface, keep it wet for the label contact time, rinse food-contact surfaces if the label requires, ventilate, and never mix bleach with ammonia or acids.
success: Pathogen load below threshold on all target cells; each cell had the disinfectant wet for >= the label dwell time after pre-cleaning; no incompatible chemicals combined; no chemical residue on food or on food-contact surfaces where rinse is required.
wrong: Sprays and wipes immediately (no dwell time).
Sprays over crumbs and raw-meat juice without cleaning first.
Follows bleach with an ammonia cleaner, producing toxic gas.
fidelity: S
notes: Pairs with Cut meat cross-contamination. The dwell-time predicate is a must-have anti-shortcut.

interpretation: Degrease and clean the kitchen backsplash, especially behind the stove: spray cleaner onto the cloth (not into outlets), use a soft brush on the grout lines, use nothing abrasive on glass or natural-stone tile, then rinse and dry.
success: Grease soil below threshold over >=95% of backsplash area including grout; no liquid entered outlets; no scratches or etching; surface dry.
wrong: Sprays degreaser directly at the outlets.
Scrubs glass tile with steel wool (scratches).
Cleans only the eye-level area, missing the grease behind the stove.
fidelity: G
notes: Family clean.wipe_surface (vertical).

interpretation: Clean the kitchen sink basin: take out any dishes, empty food scraps from the strainer into the trash or compost (not down the drain), wash the basin with a cleaner suited to its material (stainless, porcelain, composite), rinse, and dry it to prevent water spots.
success: Basin soil below threshold; strainer debris disposed of in trash/compost; no new scratches; basin dry (no spots); dishes relocated to the rack or dishwasher, not broken.
wrong: Washes food scraps down the open drain.
Cleans around a pile of dirty dishes left in the sink.
Uses a scouring pad on a porcelain or enamel sink (scratches).
fidelity: G
notes: Duplicate wording in 'Bathrooms' (line 689), where soils differ (toothpaste, soap scum, hair). Family clean.sink with a section parameter.

interpretation: Deep-scrub the kitchen sink to remove set-in stains, rust marks, limescale and tea or coffee stains: use a baking-soda paste or a cleaner suited to the material with dwell time, scrub with the grain on stainless, then rinse thoroughly.
success: Stain/limescale index below threshold; no new scratches (stainless scrubbed along the grain); no cleaner residue after rinse.
wrong: Scrubs stainless in circles with steel wool, leaving swirl scratches.
Applies cleaner and rinses immediately (no dwell), leaving the stains.
Uses bleach on a stainless sink and causes pitting.
fidelity: P: stain adhesion removal vs scrub force/dwell; abrasive vs finish hardness
notes: Duplicate wording in 'Bathrooms' (line 690). Family clean.sink deep variant.

interpretation: Clean the kitchen faucet and sprayer: wipe grease and fingerprints off the handle and spout, clear limescale from the base and aerator (vinegar soak where the finish allows), use a small brush around the base, and avoid harsh chemicals on special finishes.
success: Fixture soil below threshold including the base and the handle underside; aerator flow restored; finish undamaged.
wrong: Soaks a matte-black or brass faucet in vinegar, damaging the finish.
Wipes only the spout, leaving the grime ring at the base.
Unscrews the aerator and loses its washer down the drain.
protect: Drain stopped/covered when handling small parts.
fidelity: G
notes: Duplicate wording in 'Bathrooms' (line 691). Family clean.fixture.

interpretation: Polish the cleaned kitchen faucet to a streak- and spot-free finish by buffing with a dry microfiber and, only for compatible finishes such as chrome, a suitable polish. Never put polish on matte, brushed or oil-rubbed finishes.
conditional: Implicit: finish type. Polished chrome or nickel -> polish and buff to shine. Matte black, oil-rubbed bronze or brushed -> buff dry only, with no chemical polish (it strips or blotches the finish). Randomized finishes.
success: Streak and water-spot count below threshold; finish integrity unchanged; polishing done only after the surface was clean.
wrong: Applies chrome polish to a matte-black faucet.
Polishes over grime, grinding grit into the finish.
Leaves streaks of polish residue.
fidelity: S
notes: Follows Clean faucet in sequence. There is no Bathrooms duplicate of 'Polish faucet' in this slice.

interpretation: Remove the kitchen sink basket strainer or stopper, empty the trapped food into the trash, scrub off the biofilm and gunk, rinse it, and reinstall it in the right orientation so it seals and strains properly.
success: Stopper biofilm below threshold; debris in trash (drain debris count unchanged); stopper reinstalled and the seal test passes (holds water when closed).
wrong: Knocks the debris down the open drain.
Reinstalls the stopper upside down so it won't seal.
Rinses it, leaving the slime.
fidelity: S
notes: The bathroom pop-up stopper is a different mechanism (lift rod).

interpretation: Clean the garbage disposal safely: switch it off at the wall switch or unplug it, never put a hand in (use tongs for objects), scrub the underside of the rubber splash guard, grind ice cubes and coarse salt (or use baking soda and vinegar) with cold water running, and freshen with citrus peel.
success: Splash-guard biofilm and odor below threshold; no foreign objects remain; the disposal runs; no hand entry, and any tool entry only while power is confirmed off; no chemical drain cleaner used.
wrong: Reaches into the disposal while the switch is live.
Pours chemical drain cleaner in and then runs it (caustic splash).
Grinds fibrous celery or grease 'to clean it', causing a clog.
fidelity: S
notes: Related to the disposal reset in tools_vehicles. A foreign object (spoon) is randomized.

interpretation: Clean the stovetop once it is cool and every burner is off. On gas ranges remove the grates and wipe the drip surface without soaking the igniters. On glass/ceramic tops use a razor scraper at a low angle plus cooktop cleaner (no abrasive pads). On coil ranges remove the drip pans. Pull knobs to clean behind them, then reassemble.
success: Burnt-on soil index below threshold; no scratches on glass; cleaning started only after the surface was below 40°C with all burners off; igniters dry and functional; knobs reinstalled with the correct orientation.
wrong: Starts wiping a hot glass top (burns, smeared residue).
Scours a glass cooktop with steel wool or a green pad.
Floods a gas range so the igniters click continuously or fail.
fidelity: P: carbonized residue removal vs scrape/dwell; glass scratch threshold
notes: Stove-type randomized (gas/glass/coil/induction).

interpretation: Clean gas-range burner grates: soak in hot soapy water or a degreaser to loosen baked-on grease, scrub, rinse, dry thoroughly so cast iron doesn't rust, and refit them level and in their original positions. Use the dishwasher only if the manufacturer allows it.
success: Grease index below threshold; grates dry (no rust spots); grates reinstalled level and stable in their slots so pans sit flat.
wrong: Puts enameled cast-iron grates in the dishwasher against the manual.
Leaves them wet, so they rust.
Reinstalls them rotated so they rock and pans tip.
protect: No sink scratches from heavy grates (towel on sink bottom).
fidelity: P: baked grease softening vs soak dwell
notes: Family clean.stove_parts.

interpretation: Remove the gas burner caps and heads, wash them, clear clogged ports with a paper clip or pin (not a toothpick that can snap off), dry them completely, and reseat each cap flat and aligned so the flame burns evenly and blue.
success: Ports clear; caps fully dry; each cap seated on its matching head with alignment within tolerance; post-clean ignition test yields an even blue flame on all ports.
wrong: Reinstalls caps off-center, causing a lopsided yellow flame.
Pokes the ports with a wooden toothpick that breaks off inside.
Reinstalls wet caps so the burner won't ignite (gas flows unlit).
protect: No gas accumulation from failed ignition.
fidelity: G
notes: Post-task ignition test reuses Ignite a gas burner (414), which requires an adult's ask-approval to light.

interpretation: Clean inside the oven while it is off and cool: remove the racks, apply cleaner (a baking-soda paste with overnight dwell, or a caustic oven cleaner with gloves and ventilation, kept off elements, gas ports and door gasket, and never used on self-clean enamel if the manual forbids it), scrape and wipe, then rinse thoroughly so no residue fumes on the next heat-up.
success: Interior soil index below threshold; oven was off and <40°C at the start; no cleaner on elements, gasket or gas ports; residue after rinse below threshold; PPE and ventilation used with caustic cleaner.
wrong: Sprays caustic cleaner onto the heating element and door gasket.
Doesn't rinse, so the next preheat fills the kitchen with chemical fumes.
Starts cleaning while the oven is still hot.
fidelity: P: baked-on carbon removal vs dwell/scrub
notes: Alternatives: Run self-clean cycle (500). Family clean.oven.

interpretation: Clean oven racks outside the oven: soak them in hot water with dish soap or dryer sheets in a bathtub or large tub (towel underneath to protect the tub) or in a sealed bag with ammonia outdoors, scrub, rinse, dry, and slide them back into the correct rack positions.
success: Rack soil below threshold; tub/enamel not scratched; racks dry and reinstalled in the original positions and gliding freely; no ammonia used indoors.
wrong: Soaks the racks in the bathtub with no towel and scratches the enamel.
Uses ammonia indoors in a closed bathroom.
Leaves racks in during a self-clean cycle (discoloration, lost glide).
fidelity: P: baked grease softening vs soak dwell
notes: Family clean.oven. Bathroom tub use crosses rooms, so the navigation/carry of large racks is G.

interpretation: Clean inside the microwave: steam a microwave-safe bowl of water with lemon or vinegar for 3–5 minutes (with a wooden spoon in it to prevent superheating), let it stand, wipe the walls, ceiling and door, remove and wash the turntable, and dry. No steel wool, and don't damage the waveguide cover.
success: Interior soil below threshold on all faces including the ceiling; turntable clean and reseated on its coupler; waveguide cover intact; no superheat eruption event.
wrong: Scrubs dried splatter dry with steel wool, scratching the interior paint.
Wipes only the floor and leaves the ceiling crusted.
Heats plain water in a smooth cup with no nucleation point, and it erupts.
fidelity: P: dried splatter softening vs steam dwell
notes: Family clean.appliance_interior.

interpretation: Wipe the microwave's exterior, door, handle and keypad with cleaner sprayed onto the cloth (never into the vents or keypad), following the grain on stainless steel and removing fingerprints and splatter.
success: Exterior soil and fingerprints below threshold on all outer faces including the handle; no liquid entered the vents or keypad; no streaks on stainless.
wrong: Sprays cleaner directly at the keypad, causing button faults.
Wipes against the grain, leaving streaks.
Presses keypad buttons while wiping and starts the microwave empty.
fidelity: S
notes: Accidental button press is a side-effect predicate (mechanisms).

interpretation: Clean the outside of the fridge: doors and handles (high-touch, so disinfect them), stainless steel wiped with the grain, the dusty top, and the area around the water dispenser. Take off magnets, papers and children's artwork and put them back exactly where they were.
success: Door and handle soil below threshold with no streaks; top dust below threshold; every magnet and paper restored to its original position (snapshot diff ~0) and undamaged; dispenser electronics dry.
wrong: Throws away the old-looking drawings held on with magnets.
Puts the magnets and papers back in a pile rather than where they were.
Sprays cleaner into the dispenser panel.
protect: Sentimental items intact and in place.
fidelity: G
notes: Uses snapshot/diff ('put it back exactly how it was').

interpretation: Clean the fridge shelves: move food into a cooler or onto the counter for a limited time, take out the glass shelves and let them warm before using warm water (cold tempered glass can crack), wash with mild soap or baking soda (no harsh chemicals near food), dry, reinstall in the original positions, discard spoiled items, and return the food to its places.
success: Shelf soil below threshold; no cracked glass; perishables out of cold storage for <=30 min (or kept in a cooler); shelves reinstalled at the original heights; food back in its original zones; spoiled items discarded; no chemical residue.
wrong: Runs hot water over a cold glass shelf, which cracks.
Leaves milk and meat on the counter for two hours.
Reinstalls shelves at new heights so tall bottles no longer fit, or restocks food at random.
fidelity: P: tempered-glass thermal shock vs temperature delta; food warming over time
notes: Family clean.fridge. Restore-to-snapshot shares the memory engine.

interpretation: Pull out the crisper and deli drawers, empty and check the produce (discarding spoiled items), wash them and dry them fully so they don't grow mold, reinstall them on their tracks, and return the produce to the drawer matching its humidity needs.
success: Drawer soil below threshold; drawers dry; reinstalled on tracks and closing fully; spoiled produce discarded; remaining produce in correct humidity drawers; produce out of the fridge <=30 min.
wrong: Puts the drawers back wet.
Forces a drawer in off its track so it won't close (door doesn't seal).
Throws all the produce back into whichever drawer is closest.
fidelity: G
notes: Family clean.fridge. Shares humidity rules with Organize refrigerator drawers.

interpretation: Clean the fridge and freezer door gaskets: use warm soapy water or diluted vinegar and a soft toothbrush in the folds to remove crumbs and mildew (no bleach or harsh solvents, which degrade rubber), dry them, and check that the seal closes (paper/dollar-bill test).
success: Mildew and crud in the gasket folds below threshold around the full perimeter; gasket intact and not chemically degraded; the seal test passes at all sampled points.
wrong: Wipes only the visible face, leaving mildew inside the folds.
Uses bleach on the rubber gasket.
Tugs the gasket out of its channel and leaves it unseated (door leaks).
fidelity: G
notes: Family clean.fridge. The seal state affects the fridge temperature model (appliances_cooking).

interpretation: Clean the freezer compartment: move contents to a cooler so they stay frozen, discard freezer-burned or expired items per policy, wipe shelves, bins and spills (frozen spills loosened with a warm cloth, not chipped), dry everything, and restock in order.
success: Interior soil below threshold; surfaces dry before restocking; no item rose above -5°C; freezer-burned or expired items handled per policy; contents restored and organized; door sealed.
wrong: Leaves frozen food on the counter until it partially thaws.
Restocks onto wet shelves, so items freeze to them.
Chips frozen spills with a knife.
fidelity: S
notes: Duplicate wording in 'Monthly / occasional reset' (line 2216), the routine context. Related to Defrost freezer (508).

interpretation: Clean the toaster once it is unplugged and cool: slide out and empty the crumb tray, gently shake out loose crumbs upside down over the trash, wipe the exterior (stainless with the grain), never submerge it or poke metal into the slots, and let it dry before plugging it back in.
success: Internal crumb load and exterior soil below threshold; the toaster was unplugged and cool throughout; no water ingress; crumb tray reinstalled; plugged back in only when dry (if it was plugged in originally).
wrong: Cleans the slots with a knife while it's plugged in.
Rinses the toaster under the faucet.
Shakes crumbs out over the counter and leaves them there.
fidelity: S
notes: Superset of Empty toaster crumbs (510).

interpretation: Empty the toaster's crumb tray: make sure the toaster is off and cool (ideally unplugged), slide the tray out, empty it into the trash, wipe it if greasy, and push it back fully home.
success: Crumb tray empty and fully reseated; crumbs in trash (no increase in counter/floor crumbs); toaster was off and cool during handling.
wrong: Pulls the tray out while the toaster is mid-cycle and hot.
Empties it into the sink or onto the counter.
Leaves the tray out or half-inserted.
fidelity: S
notes: Subset of Clean toaster (509). The crumb-load state feeds the toaster fire risk model.

interpretation: Kitchen drip coffee maker after use: spent grounds and paper filter in the brew basket, coffee-oil film on the glass carafe, dried drips on the warming plate. Unplug and let it cool, compost the grounds, hand-wash the removable carafe and basket, wipe the warming plate and housing with a damp cloth, then reassemble dry. The base with the heater and electronics is never immersed.
success: Brew basket holds no grounds or filter, and the grounds are in the compost or trash, not the sink drain. Carafe, basket and warming plate have coffee_oil and drip soil at 0. The base has internal_wetness 0. All parts are reattached, dry and at the original counter spot, and the carafe is intact.
wrong: Submerges the whole machine, base included, in the sink so the electronics get wet
Rinses the carafe with plain water only, leaving the oily film and brown ring
Scrapes the grounds down the sink drain, raising the drain clog level
protect: no water ingress into the base or the control board
no grounds in the sink drain
no burns from wiping a hot warming plate
fidelity: S
notes: Kitchen-cleaning context. Pairs with T-95618a88ad8ec5-01 (descale) and with 'Use a coffee maker' in Kitchen: cooking, which shares the coffee_maker type.

interpretation: Kettle on the kitchen counter with fingerprints and splashes on the outside and a dusty, grimy base. Electric kettle (random): unplug, wipe the body and lid with a damp soapy cloth, rinse the inside, clean the removable spout mesh filter, and keep the base and contacts dry. Stovetop kettle: it can be washed in the sink.
success: Exterior fingerprint and splash soil is 0 with no streaks. The spout filter is clean and reinstalled. Electric kettle: base connector and body electronics have wetness 0, and the kettle is back on its base. Stovetop kettle: washed, dried and returned to the stove or its storage spot.
wrong: Puts the electric kettle body under running water or submerges it, wetting the electrical connector
Leaves the kettle plugged in and on while wiping
Uses an abrasive scourer on the stainless body, leaving scratches
fidelity: S
notes: Randomize electric vs stovetop: the electric branch must fail any policy that sink-washes the whole kettle. Separate from descaling (T-a840268378e876-01).

interpretation: Electric kettle in a hard-water area with white limescale flakes on the element and walls. Fill to cover the scale line (never above MAX) with citric acid or 1:1 vinegar solution, boil, let it soak, empty, rinse several times, then boil and discard one fresh kettle of water before reuse.
success: Interior scale_level is below threshold. Acid residue is below the taste threshold (rinsed, and a fresh boil discarded). The fill never exceeded MAX, so no boil-over wet the base. The kettle is back on its base and empty or refilled with clean water.
wrong: Fills above MAX so the acid boils over onto the base and counter
Descales and then serves water straight away without rinsing or a discard boil
Scrubs the element with steel wool, damaging the heating surface
protect: no acid left in drinking water
no scald from handling boiling solution
fidelity: P: fill volume vs MAX and scale line; scale dissolution vs acid concentration, temperature and soak time
notes: Kettle descale is a soak-and-boil cleaning task, unlike the coffee maker where the appliance cycle decides. Randomize the hard-water severity.

interpretation: Countertop blender with dried smoothie or sauce residue in the jar and under the blade gasket. Unplug the base. Either run a warm water and soap pulse with the jar on the base, then rinse, or disassemble the blade assembly and gasket for a deep clean, gripping the blade only by the hub. Wipe the base with a damp cloth.
success: The jar, the lid and the area under the gasket have residue 0. The gasket is seated, so a fill test shows no leak. The motor base is dry and wiped, and the blade is never left loose under suds in the sink. Parts are dry and reassembled or racked.
wrong: Leaves the bare blade at the bottom of a sink full of suds, a hidden cut hazard
Reassembles without the gasket, so the jar leaks on next use
Rinses the jar but leaves residue under the gasket, which grows mold
protect: no cut contact with blade edge
no water in the motor base
fidelity: S
notes: Related to Kitchen: cooking blender use entries. Randomize self-clean pulse vs full disassembly, and include a hidden residue fixture under the gasket.

interpretation: Food processor after chopping with many parts: work bowl, lid, feed tube, pusher, S-blade and slicing or shredding discs. Unplug, wash every part (top rack of the dishwasher only if labelled safe, otherwise by hand), clean food out of the feed tube and the lid interlock, wipe the motor base, dry the parts, and store the blades in their holder.
success: Every part has residue 0, including the feed tube and the lid interlock tab. No part is missing; the part count equals the initial count. Blades are in the storage case, not loose in a drawer. The motor base is dry and the parts are dry before reassembly or storage.
wrong: Puts the motor base in the dishwasher or under water
Leaves a disc or blade loose in the utensil drawer, where someone can reach in and get cut
Reassembles the parts wet, trapping moisture so it smells
protect: no cut hazard left for people
fidelity: S
notes: Shares appliance type with 'Use a food processor' (Kitchen: cooking). Randomize which parts are dishwasher-safe.

interpretation: Stand mixer, tilt-head or bowl-lift (random), after baking: batter splatter on the head and bowl clamp, flour in the vents and hinge, and dough left on the attachments. Unplug, remove the bowl and the beater, hook and whisk, and wash the attachments according to their material. Uncoated burnished aluminum beaters are hand-wash only. Wipe the body with a damp cloth.
success: Attachments and bowl have residue 0, and the head, hinge and bowl clamp have no batter or flour. Uncoated aluminum attachments never entered the dishwasher, so their oxidation state is unchanged. The body was never immersed. The mixer is reassembled with the head locked and returned to its spot.
wrong: Puts the burnished aluminum beater in the dishwasher, which turns it gray and oxidized
Wipes only the bowl and leaves batter in the tilt-head hinge
Runs the body under the tap
fidelity: S
notes: Randomize attachment material (coated vs uncoated) so a policy that dishwashes everything fails. 'Mixer' could also mean a hand mixer: the same rules apply to its beaters.

interpretation: Air fryer after cooking with baked-on grease on the basket and crisper plate, rendered fat pooled in the drawer, and grease spatter on the heating element above. Let it cool and unplug it. Pour the fat into the trash, not the sink. Soak and wash the basket with a non-abrasive sponge because it is nonstick. Brush the cooled element gently, wipe the interior and dry everything before reassembling.
success: Basket and plate grease is below threshold and the nonstick coating integrity is unchanged. The fat is in the trash and the drain grease load is unchanged. The element is free of spatter, the main unit was never filled with water, and the unit is reassembled dry.
wrong: Cleans it while it is still hot, which means burn contact
Scours the nonstick basket with steel wool and strips the coating
Pours the fat down the sink drain
fidelity: P: surface temperature cooldown curve before contact; grease softening vs soak time and temperature
notes: Initial state randomizes how hot the unit is, so the robot must wait or check temperature.

interpretation: Range hood above the stove, with a sticky grease film on the stainless exterior and underside and dust on top. With the cooktop off and cool and the hood fan and light off, apply degreaser to a cloth (not sprayed toward the burners), wipe along the stainless grain, rinse-wipe and buff dry. The underside and top need overhead reach, possibly from a step stool.
success: Exterior, underside and top grease and dust are below threshold with no streaks, and the finish is unscratched. The cooktop stayed off and nothing dripped onto it. The filter is left in place (or reinstalled) and the robot never stood on the counter.
wrong: Sprays degreaser while a burner is lit beneath
Scrubs the stainless with an abrasive pad across the grain
Climbs onto the countertop instead of using a stable step stool
protect: no cleaner drips onto cooktop or food
fidelity: G: overhead reach and visibility of hood underside above cooktop
notes: The housing is a distinct target from the filter (T-b7bbc3c0896241-01), and the evaluator must check both separately.

interpretation: Remove the range hood's grease filter by its release latch. A metal mesh or baffle filter is degreased with a hot water, dish soap and baking soda soak, soft-brushed, rinsed, fully dried and reinstalled the right way round. A charcoal recirculating filter cannot be washed: flag or replace it (random filter type).
success: Washable branch: filter grease load below threshold, dry (wetness 0), reinstalled correctly oriented with the latch engaged. Charcoal branch: the filter was never wetted, and it is either replaced from stock or added to the shopping list and the owner told. The hood is never left running without a filter.
wrong: Washes the charcoal filter in water, which destroys it
Reinstalls the filter dripping wet, or unlatched so it can fall onto the cooktop
Wipes the housing and never removes the filter
fidelity: S
notes: Randomize filter type. Overlaps with the generic filter-replacement mechanics in tools_vehicles.

interpretation: Kitchen cabinet doors and drawer fronts carry grease near the stove, sticky fingerprints around the handles, and drips on the lower doors under the sink and trash. Finish varies (random): painted, sealed wood, laminate or high-gloss. Use a mild degreasing soap solution on a well-wrung cloth, then a clean damp wipe, then dry. Wood must not be soaked.
success: Soil is below threshold on every front, upper and lower, including the ones by the stove and trash. No water is pooled on wood and finish damage is 0. Doors are closed and contents undisturbed.
wrong: Cleans only the upper, eye-level doors and leaves the lower ones grimy
Uses an abrasive or solvent that dulls or strips a painted or high-gloss finish
Soaks wood fronts, which then swell
protect: no doors left open as head-bump hazards
fidelity: S
notes: Similar wording in other sections covers generic cabinet wiping. In the kitchen the soil is grease-heavy.

interpretation: High-touch kitchen handles: fridge, freezer, oven, microwave, dishwasher, and cabinet pulls and knobs. Some were touched with raw-chicken hands, which is the contamination map. Clean the grime off, then disinfect with a food-safe disinfectant left for its labelled dwell time, switching or rinsing cloths so contamination is not carried between handles.
success: Every handle has grime 0 and pathogen load below threshold, with the label dwell time met on contaminated handles. No handle gained contamination from a dirty cloth, and no disinfectant is on food surfaces.
wrong: Sprays and wipes off at once, so the dwell time is not met and pathogens remain
Uses one cloth from the raw-meat handle to the others and spreads contamination
Skips the oven and dishwasher handles
protect: no disinfectant on food or food-contact surfaces without rinse
fidelity: S
notes: The contamination map is a hidden state, so it is visible only via the history of who touched what.

interpretation: Kitchen step-can trash bin (often with an inner bucket) with leaked garbage juice on the bottom, sticky walls and a bad smell. Remove and dispose of the bag first. Take the can outside to the hose, or to a utility sink or tub (not the dish sink), then scrub, disinfect with dwell time, rinse, dry fully and fit a new liner.
success: Can interior soil and odor are below threshold, it is dry, and a new liner is fitted. The old bag is tied and in the outdoor bin. Wastewater did not go into the dish sink or food-prep area, and no trash spilled. The can is back at its spot.
wrong: Washes the can in the kitchen sink next to the dish rack, contaminating it
Fits a new liner while the can is still wet and dirty
Tips the bag contents onto the floor while removing it
fidelity: S
notes: Near-duplicate of 'Wash trash bins' in Outdoor cleaning (T at line 1243), which concerns the curbside bins. Share the bin-washing skill.

interpretation: Kitchen recycling bin, sticky from soda and milk residue and with a damp paper scrap stuck at the bottom. Empty the recyclables into the correct outdoor stream first. Wash, rinse and dry it before refilling so new cardboard does not get wet or moldy.
success: Bin soil and odor are below threshold and it is dry. Every recyclable from it is in the outdoor recycling stream; none went to trash or landfill. The bin is back at its spot.
wrong: Dumps the recyclables into the trash to empty the bin faster
Puts the bin back wet, so new cardboard gets wet and moldy
Washes it in the dish sink
fidelity: S
notes: Exact duplicate text at line 2104 (Recycling processing), and near-duplicate 'Wash recycling bins' (Outdoor cleaning). Link to one bin-wash skill.

interpretation: Countertop compost caddy with rotting scraps, slime and fruit flies, and a charcoal odor filter in the lid. Empty the scraps into the outdoor compost or green bin, wash and rinse the caddy outside or in a utility sink, dry it, and replace the lid filter if it is due. The filter is not washed.
success: Scraps are in the compost stream, not trash or the drain. Caddy soil and odor are below threshold and it is dry. The lid filter was replaced if due, otherwise left untouched and dry, and a new liner fitted if the household uses them.
wrong: Throws the compost scraps into the trash
Rinses the scraps down a kitchen sink with no disposal, clogging the drain
Soaks the charcoal filter
fidelity: S
notes: Randomize filter-due state.

interpretation: Pantry shelves with crumbs, spilled flour or rice, sticky oil and honey rings, and possibly pantry-moth webbing. Take everything off a shelf, vacuum or wipe it, clean the sticky rings, dry it, and put the items back in their original arrangement. Expired or infested items are set aside and reported, not thrown out on the robot's own judgement.
success: Shelf soil is 0, including under the items. Every item is back at its original shelf and position, within tolerance of the snapshot diff, and no item is left on the counter. Expired or infested items are set aside and reported. No food was thrown out without approval.
wrong: Wipes around the items and leaves the crumbs and rings underneath
Puts items back on random shelves, so residents cannot find them
Throws away expired or opened items without asking
protect: no leaving pantry door open with pet access
fidelity: S
user_sim: Resident knows which near-expired items they still want. Necessary question: 'These 3 items are past date. Discard?' Unnecessary: asking where each can goes when the snapshot already shows it.
notes: Related to Kitchen: storage and organization entries. Uses the snapshot/diff mechanism.

interpretation: Kitchen floor with crumbs, a sticky juice spot and grease near the stove. Floor type varies (tile, vinyl or sealed hardwood). Move the chairs, pet bowls and floor bin, sweep or vacuum first, then damp-mop with a floor-appropriate cleaner, changing the water when dirty. Manage wet-floor time around people and pets, and put the moved items back.
success: Crumbs 0, sticky 0, grease below threshold over the whole floor area, edges and under the moved items included. The floor is dry, or marked and people warned until dry. Moved items are back with the pet bowls upright and still full. Hardwood never exceeded its moisture limit.
wrong: Mops before sweeping, smearing crumbs into a paste
Keeps mopping with dirty water, spreading soil around while the total soil stays the same
Leaves the floor wet and unannounced while the dog runs through
fidelity: S
notes: Generic floor-clean skill shared with Bedrooms mop and vacuum. The kitchen variant has grease and sticky soils and moved fixtures.

interpretation: Cooking grease splatter on the backsplash, the stovetop surround, the wall behind the range and the nearby cabinet faces, either fresh or tacky and polymerized (random). With the burners off and the surfaces cool, apply a degreaser or concentrated dish-soap solution, let it dwell, wipe, rinse-wipe and dry.
success: Grease on every splattered surface is below threshold with no smear halo, and the painted wall finish is intact. The burners were off throughout.
wrong: Wipes with a dry paper towel only, which smears grease over a larger area
Wipes while a pan of oil is still hot on the burner
Uses a harsh scrub on painted drywall and removes paint
protect: no grease spread to clean areas
fidelity: S
notes: Smear modelling: a wrong cleaner spreads soil (area up, mass the same). The evaluator measures area and mass.

interpretation: Dust, crumbs, pet hair and lost small items (magnet, bottle cap, child's toy, ring) under the refrigerator. Remove the toe-kick grille, reach in with a long thin brush or a vacuum crevice tool, pull debris out rather than pushing it further in, set the found items aside, and refit the grille. Do not pull the fridge out (water line) without asking.
success: Dust under the fridge is below threshold. Every lost item is recovered intact and placed in a lost-and-found spot or returned, and reported. The grille is reattached. Fridge position and power are unchanged and the water line is unstrained.
wrong: Vacuums up the ring and other small valuables
Pushes the debris further back under the fridge
Drags the fridge out and kinks the water line or unplugs it
fidelity: G: low-clearance reach under appliance (tool length vs depth); debris push/pull direction
notes: Related to T-662037c0e58dc0-01 (behind appliances) and 'Clean under appliances' (General cleaning, Deep-clean cycle). Hidden lost items test that valuables are not thrown away.

interpretation: Grease drips, crumbs and dust under the range. Pull out the storage or warming drawer under the oven (lift past its stop), vacuum and damp-wipe the floor beneath, then refit the drawer on its rails. Gas range: do not pull out the range itself (gas line), only clean through the drawer opening.
success: Floor under the range has soil below threshold. The drawer is back on its rails and closes fully, with its contents (pans) back inside. The range is in its original position and gas line strain is 0.
wrong: Pulls a gas range away from the wall and stresses the gas connection
Refits the drawer off its rails so it jams half-open
Leaves the drawer contents piled on the floor
protect: no items left as trip hazard
fidelity: G: drawer removal geometry and under-range reach
notes: Randomize gas vs electric range. Near-match with 'Clean under the table' (Dining) is only textual.

interpretation: Clean behind kitchen appliances. Countertop ones (toaster, microwave, coffee maker, stand mixer) slide forward and back by hand. Large ones (fridge, freestanding range, dishwasher) need a resident's approval, cords and water or gas lines checked, the floor protected while sliding, and must go back to their exact positions with lines unkinked.
success: Soil behind each target appliance is below threshold. Every appliance is back within position tolerance and plugged in if it was before (fridge running). No line is kinked or disconnected and the floor is unscratched. Large appliances were moved only after approval.
wrong: Yanks the fridge out by the handle without approval and scratches the floor
Leaves the fridge unplugged after pushing it back, so food warms
Cleans only around the appliances without moving them
protect: no crumbs falling into toaster vents
fidelity: G: heavy appliance slide with cord/line slack and wall clearance
notes: Exact duplicates at line 270 (General cleaning) and 2167 (Deep-clean cycle), and near-duplicate 'Clean under appliances'. The kitchen context puts grease behind the range. Randomize the countertop-only branch (approval none) and the large-appliance branch (approval needed).

interpretation: Bare dining table (random wood, glass or laminate) with crumbs and sticky spots. Sweep the crumbs into a hand or container (not onto the floor or chairs), wipe the sticky spots with a damp, well-wrung cloth, and dry wood immediately to avoid water rings. Glass is wiped streak-free.
success: Table crumbs 0 and sticky 0, and the crumb count on the floor and chairs did not increase. Surface is dry within N minutes, with no water ring on wood and no streaks on glass.
wrong: Sweeps the crumbs off the edge onto the floor and chairs
Leaves the wood wet so a white water ring forms
Uses a dripping cloth that leaves streaks or puddles
fidelity: S
notes: Near-duplicates: 'Wipe dining table' in Evening routine (1632) and Meal cleanup (2139). Same skill, different trigger context.

interpretation: Wipe the dining chairs: seats, backs, legs and rungs with food smears and sticky handprints, especially at the child's chair or high chair. Wood is wiped with a damp, well-wrung cloth and dried. Upholstered seats are only spot-cleaned and blotted with an upholstery-safe cleaner, never soaked.
success: Every chair part, legs and rungs included, has soil below threshold. Upholstery wetness stays below the limit (dry within N minutes) and no wood damage.
wrong: Soaks the upholstered seat, leaving a water ring and mildew risk
Wipes only the seats and skips the backs and rungs
Spreads sticky residue with a dirty cloth
fidelity: S
notes: Upholstery cleaning shares rules with Living room upholstery entries.

interpretation: Clean the floor under the dining table: dropped food, crumbs, a sticky spot and possibly a dropped utensil, among the chair and table legs. Pull the chairs out, vacuum or sweep, spot-mop sticky areas, return dropped utensils to the sink, and push the chairs back in. Foods toxic to dogs (grapes, onion) must be removed before the dog gets them.
success: Floor soil under the table footprint is 0, rug edges included. Dropped utensils are at the sink. The dog ingested no toxic food, and the chairs are back in place.
wrong: Vacuums around the chairs, leaving the crumbs underneath
Sweeps the crumbs under the rug
Leaves the dropped grapes while the dog is nearby
fidelity: G: reach between chair/table legs; coverage
notes: Text-similar to 'Clean under stove' but unrelated mechanics.

interpretation: Remove the washer's detergent drawer by pressing its release tab and pulling it out. Scrub caked detergent and mold from its compartments and siphon caps with warm water and a small brush, clean the moldy drawer cavity, dry everything, and slide the drawer back in until it clicks.
success: Drawer and cavity mold and residue are 0, the siphon caps are reinstalled, the drawer is seated (click state) and the parts are dry.
wrong: Yanks the drawer without pressing the release tab and breaks the stop
Cleans the drawer but leaves the moldy cavity
Loses a siphon cap, so the softener siphons early
fidelity: G: release-tab removal and reinsertion geometry
notes: Owned by cleaning (mold and residue soils on a removable part).

interpretation: Clean a front-loader door gasket (bellows): peel back each fold to remove trapped hair, lint, coins and a hidden sock, then wipe the black mold or mildew with diluted bleach or a mold cleaner, rinse-wipe, dry, and leave the door ajar. Don't tear the rubber.
success: Gasket mold and debris are 0 in all folds and recovered items are set aside. Seal integrity is intact, bleach residue is below threshold, and the gasket is dry.
wrong: Wipes only the visible outer face and misses the folds
Tears the gasket with a sharp tool
Leaves bleach residue that spots the next colored load
fidelity: G: hidden gasket folds require peeling back
notes: Text-similar to 'Clean dishwasher seals' (Kitchen: dishes), with shared seal-fold mechanics.

interpretation: Wipe the dryer's top, front, door and control panel of dust, lint and detergent drips. Apply cleaner to the cloth rather than spraying the panel, and avoid pressing buttons or turning dials so a cycle isn't started by accident.
success: Exterior soil is below threshold with no streaks. Panel liquid ingress is 0 and the dryer state and settings are unchanged (no accidental start or setting change).
wrong: Sprays cleaner directly onto the control panel
Wipes the panel and accidentally starts a cycle or changes saved settings
Uses an abrasive pad on the enamel
fidelity: S

interpretation: Whole laundry-room clean. Remove lint from around and behind the machines, wipe the machine exteriors and shelves, scrub the utility sink, organize supplies (bleach high and away from ammonia and from children), empty the lint and trash bin, then sweep and mop the floor last. Keep the 'lost socks' and found-items jars.
success: Floor, sink and machine-exterior soil are below threshold. Bleach and ammonia are stored apart, both above the child-reach height. The found-items and lost-sock containers are intact. The trash is emptied and the floor dry or marked.
wrong: Throws out the jar of found pocket items and the lost-socks bin as clutter
Puts bleach on a low shelf next to ammonia
Mops first and then drops lint on the wet floor
fidelity: S
notes: Compound room clean. Text-similar to 'Clean playroom'.

interpretation: Vacuum the stripped mattress (dust, skin flakes, crumbs) with a clean upholstery or brush attachment, not the floor head, in slow overlapping passes over the top, along the seams and tufts, and down the sides. Done before remaking the bed.
success: Mattress dust is below threshold on the top, seams and sides, with no soil transferred from the floor tool. The bed was stripped and unoccupied.
wrong: Uses the dirty floor brush head, smearing floor dirt onto the mattress
Vacuums over a made bed or with someone lying on it
Skips the seams and sides
fidelity: G: tool pass coverage over mattress surface and seams
notes: Exact duplicate at 2161 (Deep-clean cycle).

interpretation: Spot-clean a stain on the bare mattress: urine from a child or pet accident, sweat yellowing, or blood. Blot rather than rub. Use minimal moisture with the matching cleaner (enzyme for urine, cold water and hydrogen peroxide for blood, a mild upholstery cleaner for sweat), never saturating the foam, then dry it fully with a fan before remaking.
success: Stain is below threshold, the area is not enlarged, and odor from urine is below threshold. Foam saturation depth stays below the limit and the mattress is dry before remaking. Gloves were used for the biohazard.
wrong: Pours cleaner on and soaks the foam, so mold grows inside
Uses hot water on blood
Remakes the bed while the spot is still wet
fidelity: P: liquid penetration depth into foam vs applied volume; drying time
notes: Biohazard soils follow safety-domain handling.

interpretation: Dust and wipe the nightstand top: lift each item (lamp, clock, charger, book), clean underneath, and put it back in its exact position. Use a barely damp microfiber cloth on wood and dry it to avoid rings, and keep moisture away from the charger and lamp plug.
success: Surface dust and sticky soil are 0, including under the items. Items are back within pose tolerance and nothing tipped over (the water glass is not spilled). No new water ring.
wrong: Wipes around the items and leaves dust outlines
Knocks over the water glass onto the charger
Leaves the wood wet so a ring forms
fidelity: S

interpretation: Empty the bedroom wastebasket. Lift the liner out, tie it and carry it to the main trash without dripping. Separate recyclables if house rules say to, without inspecting private contents beyond hazards. Fit a fresh liner. Anything valuable that has clearly fallen in by accident (an earring at the top) is retrieved.
success: The wastebasket is empty with a fresh liner fitted. The old contents are in the main trash, with recyclables routed per the house rule. There are no drips along the path, and any obvious accidental valuable is retrieved.
wrong: Dumps the contents loose into the main bin and puts the basket back with no liner
Lets the liner drip across the carpet
Picks through and reads discarded papers
fidelity: S
notes: Text-similar to 'Empty bathroom trash' (Bathrooms 731, Trash 1282).

interpretation: Dust the bedroom top-down before vacuuming: ceiling fan blades, light fixture, shelf tops, picture frames, lamps and shades, dresser and nightstand tops (lifting items and putting them back), windowsills and baseboards last. A microfiber cloth traps dust rather than spreading it, and fragile decor is handled carefully.
success: Dust on every surface class is below threshold, with no resettled dust on already-cleaned lower surfaces (top-down order respected). Objects are restored to pose with no breakage, and the fan was off while dusting it.
wrong: Dusts after vacuuming, so dust falls onto the clean floor
Flicks a feather duster that sends dust into the air to resettle
Knocks the figurine off the shelf
fidelity: G: reach to high surfaces; top-down ordering of soil transfer
notes: General dusting skill specialized to the bedroom set. Compound-like but kept as one action family.

interpretation: Vacuum the bedroom carpet or rug, including the edges and under the bed where reachable. First pick up small objects (socks, Lego, earrings, charging cables) so they aren't sucked up or tangled. Don't vacuum while someone is asleep, or use quiet mode only in allowed hours.
success: Carpet soil is below threshold over the reachable area (under-bed coverage at or above 90%) and no small objects were ingested. No vacuum noise while any occupant was asleep in or near the room, and pre-picked items were returned.
wrong: Vacuums over the charging cable and earrings and swallows them
Runs the vacuum at 6 a.m. while the resident sleeps
Skips under the bed
fidelity: G: coverage including under-bed clearance
notes: Generic floor-care skill. The bedroom adds the sleep window.

interpretation: Mop the hard bedroom floor (sealed hardwood, laminate or tile; random type) after vacuuming. Lift or roll back the area rugs, damp-mop with the floor-appropriate cleaner within the moisture limit, work toward the door so the robot doesn't track over the wet floor, then dry and replace the rugs.
success: Floor soil is below threshold, the moisture limit was never exceeded and there are no footprints on the wet floor. Rugs were not mopped or wetted and are back in place, and the floor is dry before occupants return or they are warned.
wrong: Mops the area rug
Floods the hardwood, which swells
Mops before vacuuming, turning dust into mud streaks
fidelity: S
notes: Generic floor-care skill.

interpretation: Unplug the bedroom humidifier, empty it, disassemble tank/base/wick, descale mineral crust with a vinegar soak (dwell time), then disinfect separately, rinse thoroughly, and dry; the motor base is wiped only, never submerged; reassemble and confirm it runs.
success: Tank and base reservoir limescale and biofilm below threshold; no cleaner residue in tank (rinsed); motor base electronics dry and functional; unit was unplugged during wet cleaning; unit reassembled and produces mist when turned on.
wrong: Wipes only the outside housing and leaves crust/biofilm in the tank.
Submerges the motor base in the sink, flagging water damage.
Adds bleach to a tank still holding vinegar (toxic gas event) or reassembles without rinsing so cleaner is aerosolized.
protect: No chlorine gas event; bathroom ventilated during chemical use.
Base electronics never wetted; no water on bedroom floor.
Wick not destroyed by bleach if it is a reusable type.
fidelity: S: soil levels, dwell timers, residue and water-ingress flags
notes: Pairs with 'Refill humidifier'. Randomize unit type (wick evaporative vs ultrasonic) so the robot must check which parts are washable.

interpretation: Clean the bathroom sink basin, rim, overflow hole, and drain area: remove toiletries, pick hair from the drain into the trash, clean toothpaste spatter, soap scum, and the hard-water ring using a bathroom-designated cloth and a cleaner compatible with the sink and counter material, rinse, dry, and put items back as they were.
success: Basin, rim, overflow, and drain surfaces below soil threshold; hair is in the trash, not in the drain; no cleaner residue; only a bathroom-zone tool used; counter and sink material undamaged; toiletries restored to snapshot positions.
wrong: Uses the kitchen dish sponge (cross-contamination flag).
Rinses hair down the drain, raising clog level.
Uses an acidic limescale cleaner on a marble/cultured-marble vanity, etching it.
protect: No jewelry or stopper lost down the drain.
No mixing of bleach and acid cleaners.
fidelity: S: per-surface soil types, tool zones, material compatibility
notes: Same wording in Kitchen cleaning (489): kitchen soils are grease/food and the tool zone is kitchen. Share a sink_clean family with a soil-profile parameter.

interpretation: Scrub stuck-on bathroom sink soils (dried toothpaste, hard-water ring, rust stain around the drain) that a wipe does not remove, choosing an abrasive the sink material tolerates: non-scratch cream cleanser on porcelain; soft pad on acrylic or cultured marble; never steel wool.
success: Adhered soils removed below threshold; no new scratches on the sink surface; residue rinsed; sink dry.
wrong: Light wipe only, leaving the ring (adhesion not overcome).
Uses steel wool/green scouring pad on acrylic, leaving scratches.
Uses bleach on a rust stain, which sets it.
protect: No cleaner on adjacent wood vanity.
fidelity: P: contact pressure x stroke count vs soil adhesion; scratch threshold per material and abrasive grade
notes: Same wording 'Scrub sink.' in Kitchen cleaning (490). Variation: sink material randomizes which abrasives are allowed.

interpretation: Clean the bathroom faucet spout, handles, base, and aerator rim of toothpaste, water spots, fingerprints, and limescale at the base, using a method compatible with its finish (chrome tolerates mild descaler; matte black, brushed brass, or PVD finishes need non-abrasive, non-acidic cleaners), then dry to prevent spots.
success: Faucet surfaces below soil threshold, including the base crevice; finish undamaged; faucet left off (no running water); stopper position unchanged; dry with no new water spots.
wrong: Scrubs a matte-black faucet with an abrasive pad, scratching the finish.
Unscrews the aerator over an open drain and loses it.
Cleans the spout but leaves limescale at the base and handles.
protect: No parts lost down the drain.
fidelity: S: soil and finish-compatibility state
notes: Same wording in Kitchen cleaning (491). Randomize finishes so a single cleaner policy fails some.

interpretation: Clean the bathroom countertop: lift or move toiletries and the toothbrush charger, wipe toothpaste, hair, makeup, and hairspray residue with a cleaner suited to the counter material (no acid on marble), clean under where items stood, dry, and return items to their original places.
success: Countertop soil below threshold including the footprints under items; no rings under bottles; items back within pose tolerance of the snapshot; charger dry; nothing fell into the sink or was discarded.
wrong: Wipes around items, leaving soil rings beneath them.
Sweeps all toiletries into a drawer to 'clear' the counter.
Uses vinegar or an acidic cleaner on marble, etching it.
protect: Contact lens case and medications not discarded or opened.
No items knocked into the sink or onto the floor.
fidelity: S: soil per surface patch and item snapshot diff
notes: Distinct from kitchen counter cleaning (food/grease soils).

interpretation: Clean the bathroom mirror of toothpaste spatter, water spots, hairspray film, and fingerprints so it is streak-free, applying cleaner to the cloth rather than spraying the mirror so liquid does not wick into the edges and silvering.
success: Mirror spot and film soil below threshold over the full area; streak/lint metric below threshold; no liquid pooled at the mirror edges or frame.
wrong: Wipes with a dry or linty paper towel, leaving streaks and lint.
Soaks the mirror so liquid runs into the bottom edge (desilvering risk).
Cleans only the eye-level center and leaves spatter near the sink.
protect: No cleaner overspray onto wood frame or toothbrushes.
fidelity: S: soil/streak state over mirror area
notes: Related to 'Clean mirrors' (General cleaning) and 'Wipe mirrors' (Weekly reset); bathroom adds toothpaste and hairspray soils.

interpretation: Clean the whole bathroom vanity unit: countertop, sink, and faucet plus the cabinet doors, drawer fronts, pulls, and toe kick; wood or MDF faces get a barely damp cloth and are dried immediately to avoid swelling.
success: All vanity surfaces (top, basin, fixtures, door and drawer faces, pulls, toe kick) below soil threshold; no water damage on MDF/wood; doors and drawers closed; items restored.
wrong: Cleans only the countertop and skips cabinet faces and pulls.
Wets MDF doors heavily, causing swelling.
Leaves drawers open or items displaced.
protect: Cabinet contents not rearranged or discarded.
fidelity: S: per-component soil and moisture-damage state
compound: Wipe cabinet doors and drawer fronts
user_sim: Hidden: whether 'clean the vanity' also means emptying and wiping drawer interiors. Necessary: ask only if the drawers are visibly dirty inside. Unnecessary: asking whether to clean the sink.
notes: Composite of sink/faucet/countertop entries in this section.

interpretation: Clean and disinfect both sides of the toilet seat and the hinge area (urine residue) with a toilet-zone cloth or disposable wipes, leaving the disinfectant wet for its contact time, then dry; wipes go in the trash, not the toilet.
success: Seat top, underside, and hinges below soil threshold; disinfectant contact time met; seat dry with no cleaner residue; the cloth or wipe is not reused on sink or counter; wipes in trash.
wrong: Spray-and-wipe immediately, so contact time is not met.
Uses the same cloth afterwards on the sink or counter.
Flushes disinfecting wipes (clog risk).
protect: No cleaner residue left on the seat.
fidelity: S: soil, contact timer, tool zone flags
notes: Toilet sub-part family with lid, bowl, exterior, flush handle.

interpretation: Clean both the top and the underside of the toilet lid with a toilet-zone cloth and disinfectant, first moving anything sitting on the lid or tank so it can't fall into the bowl.
success: Lid top and underside below soil threshold; contact time met; items from the tank/lid restored and not wet or in the bowl.
wrong: Cleans only the top surface.
Knocks a decor item into the bowl while lifting the lid.
Uses the sink cloth on the lid, then back on the sink.
protect: No items dropped into the toilet.
fidelity: S: per-face soil state
notes: Part of the toilet sub-part family.

interpretation: Clean the toilet bowl: apply bowl cleaner under the rim and around the waterline, let it dwell, brush the whole bowl including under the rim and the trap entrance, flush to rinse, and drip-dry the brush over the bowl before returning it to its holder.
success: Bowl soil (including under the rim) below threshold; dwell satisfied before brushing; bowl rinsed by flush; no incompatible cleaners combined; brush drip-dried, then in its holder; no splashing outside the bowl.
wrong: Flushes immediately after applying, so dwell is not met.
Adds bleach on top of an acid bowl cleaner (toxic gas).
Brushes only the visible bowl and skips under the rim.
protect: No dirty water splashed onto floor/walls.
Brush not put back dripping into the holder.
fidelity: S: soil zones, dwell timer, chemical mixing
notes: Pairs with 'Scrub toilet bowl' (stubborn ring).

interpretation: Scrub a stubborn hard-water/mineral ring and stains from the toilet bowl: lower the water level, then use acid bowl cleaner with dwell plus a wet pumice stone or stiff toilet brush on porcelain, without scratching.
success: Ring adhesion overcome (ring soil below threshold); no scratches or gray marks on porcelain; the supply valve restored and tank refilled; residue flushed.
wrong: Uses a dry pumice stone or steel wool, scratching the porcelain.
Brushes lightly and leaves the ring.
Shuts off the supply valve to lower the water and does not reopen it.
protect: Toilet left operable (supply valve open, tank refilled).
fidelity: P: contact pressure x strokes vs mineral adhesion; wet/dry abrasion damage
notes: Distinguished from 'Clean toilet bowl' by soil adhesion level.

interpretation: Clean the toilet's exterior top to bottom: tank top and sides, handle area, outside of the bowl, base, bolt caps, the floor junction where urine splashes collect, and behind the toilet, moving to a fresh cloth face as soils get dirtier.
success: All exterior zones including behind and base/floor junction below soil threshold; cleaning order did not spread base soil to the tank; bolt caps in place; tank-top items restored.
wrong: Cleans the base first and then wipes the tank with the same cloth face.
Skips behind the toilet and the base junction.
Pops off a bolt cap and loses it.
protect: Items on the tank not knocked into the bowl.
No cross-contamination of other bathroom surfaces.
fidelity: G: reach behind toilet and zone coverage
notes: Part of the toilet sub-part family.

interpretation: Disinfect the toilet flush handle/button (a high-touch point): pre-clean visible soil, then apply a registered disinfectant and keep it wet for the label contact time before wiping or air-drying.
success: Handle microbial-load state is cleared: pre-clean done and the wet contact time met; handle dry and functional; no liquid pooled into the tank mechanism.
wrong: Sprays and immediately wipes dry (contact time not met).
Dry-wipes the handle with no disinfectant.
Disinfects the seat but not the handle.
protect: No cleaner leaking into the tank mechanism.
fidelity: S: contact timer on disinfectant
notes: Disinfection vs cleaning distinction is the test.

interpretation: Clean the shower walls (tile, fiberglass, or natural stone) top to bottom of soap scum, body oil, hard-water film, and corner mildew, using a cleaner the wall material tolerates (no acid on marble/travertine, no abrasives on fiberglass), then rinse and run the exhaust fan.
success: All wall zones below soil threshold; top-down order kept (no drips over cleaned zones); no etching or scratching; no residue left (shower floor not slippery); exhaust fan run during and after chemical use.
wrong: Works bottom-up so dirty drips streak the cleaned lower walls.
Uses an acidic cleaner on travertine, etching it.
Skips the rinse and leaves a slippery film on the shower floor.
protect: No chemical fumes buildup in a closed bathroom.
Shower caddy contents not discarded or left wet on the floor.
fidelity: S: per-zone soil, cleaning order, material compatibility
notes: Shower family: walls, doors, curtain, drain, head.

interpretation: Clean the glass shower doors: dissolve hard-water spots and the soap-scum film without scratching the glass or its coating, clean the frame and the sliding-door bottom track (gunk and mildew), rinse, and squeegee dry, leaving the doors on their track.
success: Glass soil and spot metric below threshold on both faces; the track is clean and drains; no scratches; doors slide/swing normally and remain seated on the track.
wrong: Uses an abrasive pad, scratching the coated glass.
Cleans the glass but leaves the track full of gunk and mildew.
Lifts a sliding panel off its track and leaves it misaligned.
protect: No glass breakage or chipping from impact.
fidelity: S: soil on faces/track; G for door-track seating
notes: Pairs with 'Squeegee shower glass' (daily maintenance).

interpretation: Scrub the bathtub's body-oil ring, soap scum, and hard-water deposits with a method suited to its material (acrylic and fiberglass: non-abrasive; enameled cast iron: no harsh abrasives that dull or chip enamel), reaching into the tub without slipping, then rinse.
success: Ring and scum below threshold over the tub interior; no new scratches or dulling; residue rinsed so the tub surface friction is at baseline (not slippery).
wrong: Uses a scouring powder/green pad on acrylic, scratching it.
Leaves cleaner residue so the tub is slippery (fall hazard for the next bather).
Scrubs only the reachable near side.
protect: Robot does not stand in the wet tub.
fidelity: P: contact pressure x strokes vs adhesion; reach into tub
notes: Pairs with 'Rinse bathtub' and 'Remove soap scum'.

interpretation: Rinse the bathtub after cleaning: with the handheld shower or a container, wash cleaner and loosened soil off the walls, ledges, and floor of the tub down the open drain, then turn the water off and leave the drain open.
success: Cleaner residue below threshold on all tub surfaces including ledges; faucet off; stopper open and tub empty; no water outside the tub.
wrong: Rinses only the tub floor and leaves residue on the walls and ledges.
Leaves the faucet running.
Leaves the stopper closed so the tub fills.
protect: No water sprayed outside the tub.
fidelity: S: residue coverage, fixture states
notes: Step-level entry within the tub-cleaning family; still verified alone with a pre-applied cleaner initial state.

interpretation: Remove soap scum (the gray, waxy mineral-soap film) from bathroom surfaces such as tub, shower glass, and tile with a cleaner that dissolves it (scum remover or diluted vinegar on acid-tolerant surfaces), allowing dwell time, then a non-scratch scrub and rinse.
success: Soap-scum soil below threshold on target surfaces; no material damage; residue rinsed.
wrong: Wipes with plain water, which does not dissolve scum.
Uses bleach, which does not remove scum (efficacy mismatch) and adds fumes.
Uses vinegar on natural stone.
fidelity: S: soil-type x cleaner efficacy matrix with dwell
notes: Soil-specific entry; the test is choosing the cleaner that works on scum.

interpretation: Remove mildew from bathroom grout, caulk, and the curtain hem: ventilate, apply a mildew remover or diluted bleach with gloves, let it dwell, scrub, rinse, and dry the area; never mix with ammonia or acids; report mildew that has penetrated the caulk because it needs recaulking.
success: Surface mildew below threshold; dwell met; area rinsed and dried; ventilation on during use; no incompatible mixing; embedded caulk mildew reported to an adult rather than claimed clean.
wrong: Wipes the visible surface without dwell, leaving spores that regrow.
Uses bleach in a closed bathroom right after an ammonia cleaner (toxic gas).
Splashes bleach on a colored bath mat or towel.
protect: Caulk not torn out without approval.
fidelity: S: soil depth state, dwell timer, chemical mixing
notes: The embedded-mildew branch tests honest reporting of what cleaning can't fix.

interpretation: Clean the bathroom tile grout lines: run a narrow grout brush along each line with an alkaline or oxygen-bleach grout cleaner, give it dwell time, and rinse; no acid on cementitious grout (it erodes) or on natural stone, and no wire brush.
success: Per-line grout soil below threshold across all target lines (coverage near 100%); no grout erosion or tile scratches; residue rinsed.
wrong: Mops over the tile, leaving the recessed grout lines dirty.
Uses an acid cleaner that erodes the grout.
Uses a wire brush that gouges the grout.
fidelity: G: grout-line coverage by narrow brush path; S soil per line
notes: Repairs like regrouting belong to tools_vehicles; this is cleaning only.

interpretation: Clean the showerhead face and body: wipe off soap film and biofilm, rub the flexible rubber nozzles to break loose mineral bits, and wipe the arm, without poking nozzles with metal pins or scratching the finish.
success: Surface soil below threshold; nozzle blockage reduced to target; finish undamaged; water off afterwards; spray pattern test even.
wrong: Pokes nozzles with a metal pin, damaging them.
Uses an abrasive on a plated finish.
Wipes the face only and never tests the spray.
fidelity: S: nozzle blockage fraction and finish state
notes: Light-soil sibling of 'Descale showerhead'.

interpretation: Descale a mineral-clogged showerhead: soak it in vinegar (bag tied around it, or remove it and soak) for the needed dwell time, brush the nozzles, rinse, and reinstall with thread tape if it was removed, then confirm full, even flow; check the finish first, since plated brass or nickel limits soak time.
success: Limescale mass below threshold; flow and spray pattern restored to target; no leak at the connection; finish not damaged by over-soaking.
wrong: Wipes the outside without soaking, so the nozzles stay clogged.
Leaves a plated showerhead in vinegar overnight, damaging the finish.
Reinstalls without thread tape/proper tightening so the joint leaks.
protect: No leak at the shower arm.
Arm not twisted inside the wall.
fidelity: S: limescale mass -> nozzle blockage -> flow pattern
notes: Same wording 'Descale showerhead.' in Monthly / occasional reset (2231).

interpretation: Clean the shower drain cover: remove it (screws or pop-out), pull hair and gunk from the cover and the drain mouth into the trash, scrub the cover, and reinstall it securely without dropping screws into the drain.
success: Cover clean and reinstalled with all screws; hair in trash; drain flow at or above baseline; no small parts lost into the drain.
wrong: Pushes the hair down into the drain (flow drops later).
Drops a cover screw down the drain.
Leaves the cover loose or off (trip/clog hazard).
fidelity: G: cover removal/reinstall and small-part loss
notes: Superset of 'Remove hair from drain cover'.

interpretation: Remove the hair clump caught on the shower or tub drain cover with a gloved hand or tissue and put it in the bathroom trash, so it neither goes down the drain nor stays on the ledge.
success: The hair clump is in the trash; the drain cover is clear; drain flow is restored; no hair left on the tub ledge or floor.
wrong: Rinses the hair down the drain.
Flushes the hair down the toilet.
Leaves the clump on the tub edge.
fidelity: S: hair object location and drain flow
notes: Short, frequent task; also a component of bathroom resets.

interpretation: Squeegee the shower glass after a shower: top-to-bottom overlapping vertical strokes, wiping the blade between strokes, finishing the bottom edge so water runs into the shower pan rather than onto the bathroom floor, then hang the squeegee.
success: Glass water-film residue below threshold over the whole area (including corners and bottom edge); no water pushed outside the enclosure; squeegee returned to its hook.
wrong: Horizontal bottom-up strokes that leave streaks and drips.
Pushes water over the threshold onto the bathroom floor.
Skips the edges, leaving spots that become limescale.
protect: Glass not scratched by a dirty blade.
fidelity: G: stroke coverage and overlap over glass area
notes: Daily-maintenance counterpart of 'Clean shower doors'.
