interpretation: Clean the bathroom floor: move the bath mat, scale, and trash can out, remove dry soil (hair, dust) first, then wet-clean and disinfect, especially the urine-splash zone around the toilet base and behind it, let the floor dry, and return items once it is dry.
success: Floor soil below threshold including the toilet base and behind it; done in dry-then-wet order; floor dry before items return; items in original positions; no slip events from residents entering while wet (warned or timed).
wrong: Mops before removing hair, smearing clumps around.
Puts the bath mat back on the wet floor.
Leaves the floor wet while an elderly resident is about to use the bathroom without warning.
protect: Scale and trash returned; nothing discarded.
fidelity: S: soil zones, order, wetness timer
notes: Sibling of 'Mop bathroom floor'.

interpretation: Mop the bathroom floor: properly diluted solution in a bucket, mop wrung to damp, work from the far corner back toward the door so the robot never strands itself, go around the toilet base and vanity kick without pooling water, and change the water when it gets dirty.
success: Floor soil below threshold; no standing water (pool volume ~0) at the toilet base or vanity; the robot exits without crossing wet mopped area; solution dilution within label range; mop water not saturated with dirt at the end.
wrong: Uses a sopping mop that pools water at the vanity base (swelling).
Mops toward the back corner, then walks across the wet floor to leave.
Keeps mopping with saturated dirty water, redepositing soil.
fidelity: P: mop water load and wringing -> floor wetness, drying time, redeposition
notes: Related to 'Mop floors' (General cleaning) and 'Mop bedroom'.

interpretation: Empty the bathroom wastebasket: lift the liner out without spilling, tie it, take it to the main trash, pull out recyclable empties if the household sorts them, and fit a new liner, without inspecting or commenting on private or medical contents and without compressing bags by hand that may contain razors.
success: The bathroom can is empty with a fresh liner; the old bag is tied and in the main bin; any sorted recyclables are in recycling; nothing spilled on the floor; no privacy flag raised.
wrong: Tips the can into another bag, spilling contents on the floor.
Puts the whole tied trash bag in the recycling.
Leaves the can with no new liner.
fidelity: S: container states and waste streams
notes: Same wording in Trash, recycling, and composting (1282).

interpretation: Put a correctly sized liner in the bathroom trash can, opened fully with its rim folded over the can's edge (or the inner bucket of a step can), lid working, and ideally a spare liner stored at the bottom.
success: Liner fully open inside the can with rim overlap all around; lid or pedal closes; liner does not slip into the can when loaded.
wrong: Uses a too-small liner that slips into the can.
Drops the liner in without folding it over the rim.
Lines the outer can of a step can instead of the inner bucket.
fidelity: G: liner rim fit around can geometry
notes: Primitive-like cover/fit test.

interpretation: Wipe the bathroom light and fan switch plates and toggles with a cloth only slightly dampened with disinfectant (never spraying the switch), without leaving lights or the fan in a different state than before.
success: Switch plates and toggles below soil threshold; no liquid entered the switch box; all switch states equal their pre-task states; no occupant plunged into darkness.
wrong: Sprays cleaner directly on the switch so liquid enters the box.
Toggles the light off while someone is in the shower.
Leaves the fan or light switched differently than before.
fidelity: S: soil, switch state, ingress flag
notes: Same verb in other rooms; bathroom adds occupant/shower context.

interpretation: Wipe and disinfect every bathroom handle (door knob/lever inside and out, cabinet and drawer pulls, faucet handles, toilet flush lever, shower handle), working from cleanest to dirtiest and meeting disinfectant contact time.
success: Every handle in the bathroom's high-touch set is wiped with contact time met; the toilet lever is done last or with a separate wipe; handles dry.
wrong: Misses the inside door lever or cabinet pulls.
Wipes the flush lever and then the faucet handles with the same wipe.
Dry-wipes with no disinfectant.
fidelity: S: per-handle state coverage
notes: High-touch disinfection family.

interpretation: Clean the ceiling exhaust fan cover: switch the fan off (and keep it off), reach the ceiling from a stable step stool, squeeze the spring clips to drop the grille, wash the grille in the sink and dry it, vacuum dust from the housing with a brush tool (no water inside), and reinstall the grille.
success: Grille clean and dry and reinstalled flush; fan housing dust below threshold; fan works afterward with restored airflow; fan was off while hands were inside; no fall from the stool.
wrong: Reaches in with the fan running.
Wipes the motor housing with a wet cloth.
Bends the spring clips so the grille hangs loose.
protect: No dust dropped into an open toilet or onto toothbrushes (close the lid, cover items).
fidelity: G: reach to ceiling via step stool, clip release geometry
notes: Elevated work: use a step stool, not a ladder; a ladder variant raises risk to 3.

interpretation: Throw out truly empty bathroom containers (shampoo bottles, toothpaste tubes, toilet-paper cores, aerosol cans), sorting them by local rules (rinsed plastic bottles to recycling, pumps to trash, empty aerosols per locale), and keep containers that still hold product or are refillable.
success: All empty containers are in the correct stream per local rules; any container with product above a fill threshold remains; refillable dispensers remain; no aerosol in a compactor.
wrong: Discards a bottle with a quarter of its product left.
Throws away the refillable glass soap dispenser.
Puts pumps and toothpaste tubes in recycling where the locale forbids it.
fidelity: S: fill level and waste stream rules
notes: Locale variation (recycling rules) is a randomized axis.

interpretation: Clean the toothbrush holder: take the brushes out (kept separate on a clean tissue, owners tracked), wash the goo and biofilm out of the slots and bottom with hot soapy water and a small brush (or the dishwasher top rack if marked dishwasher-safe), dry, and return each brush to its own slot.
success: Holder biofilm below threshold including the bottom; holder dry; each brush is back in its owner's slot; brush heads never touched the counter or each other.
wrong: Lays brushes head-down on the wet counter while cleaning.
Mixes up which brush goes in which slot.
Wipes only the outside, leaving goo at the bottom.
protect: Non-dishwasher-safe holder not put in the dishwasher.
fidelity: S: soil and ownership state
notes: Pairs with 'Refill toothbrush holder'.

interpretation: Clean the soap dish: set the bar aside (keep it), rinse off the soap goo, scrub the drainage slots, dry, and set the bar back so it drains.
success: Dish goo below threshold with slots clear; the bar is back on the dish, not sitting in water.
wrong: Throws away the soap bar.
Rinses the top and leaves goo clogging the slots.
Puts the bar back in a puddle of water.
fidelity: S: soil state
notes: Small fixture cleaning.

interpretation: Clean the toilet brush: rinse it in the bowl by flushing over it, disinfect it (soak in diluted bleach in the holder, with dwell), let it drip-dry wedged between the seat and bowl, clean the holder, and return the dry brush.
success: Brush and holder disinfected (contact time met), brush dry before going into the holder, no standing water in the holder; nothing rinsed in the sink or tub.
wrong: Rinses the brush in the bathroom sink or tub.
Puts the wet brush straight back so dirty water pools in the holder.
Soaks it in bleach in a holder still containing acid bowl cleaner.
fidelity: S: contamination, dwell, wetness
notes: Toilet-tool family with 'Clean plunger exterior'.

interpretation: Clean the plunger's outside after use: rinse the cup in the toilet by flushing, disinfect the cup and handle, let it drip-dry over the bowl, and store it in its tray or holder, never rinsing it in a sink or tub.
success: Plunger cup and handle disinfected; drip-dried; stored in the holder with no dripping onto the floor or into a cabinet.
wrong: Rinses the plunger in the bathtub.
Disinfects only the handle and not the cup.
Stores it wet in a closed cabinet.
fidelity: S: contamination and wetness state
notes: 'Exterior' scope: cup and handle surfaces.

interpretation: Vacuum the sofa with upholstery and crevice tools at a suction suited to the fabric: lift the removable cushions, retrieve coins, jewelry, and remotes before vacuuming crevices, vacuum every surface and crevice, then put the cushions back as they were.
success: Sofa surface and crevice soil below threshold; valuables found and set aside, not in the vacuum bin; no fabric damage; cushions in their original positions.
wrong: Uses the floor beater-bar head on delicate upholstery (pilling).
Vacuums up an earring or a game piece.
Leaves the cushions swapped or off the sofa.
fidelity: G: crevice reach with attachments, cushion removal/replacement
notes: Related to 'Vacuum upholstery' (General cleaning, Deep-clean cycle).

interpretation: Lift the sofa seat cushions and vacuum the deck and crevices beneath, collecting found items (coins, remote, toys, earbuds) to return to their owners or places, then put the cushions back right side up in their original spots.
success: Deck soil below threshold; every found item is in a tray or its home, not in the vacuum; cushions back in original slots and orientations.
wrong: Vacuums around the cushions without lifting them.
Sucks up a lost earbud.
Replaces cushions zipper-side up or in the wrong positions.
fidelity: G: cushion removal/replacement and deck coverage
notes: Found-item routing links to people (ownership) and admin (lost and found).

interpretation: Remove crumbs from the living-room sofa, chairs, and ottoman with a handheld vacuum or by brushing them into a dustpan, without pushing them onto the rug or floor and without smearing greasy crumbs into the fabric.
success: Crumb count on furniture below threshold; crumbs collected (in the vacuum bin or trash), not relocated to the floor or rug; no grease smears created.
wrong: Brushes crumbs off onto the rug and leaves them.
Wipes with a wet cloth, turning crumbs into a paste stain.
Pushes crumbs deeper into the crevices.
fidelity: S: crumb particle locations (relocation tracked)
notes: Debris-relocation tracking is the key anti-cheat (moving the mess elsewhere).

interpretation: Spot-clean a stain on the living-room upholstery according to the fabric's cleaning code (W: water-based; S: solvent only; W/S: either; X: vacuum only, no liquid), testing a hidden area first and blotting from the outside in without over-wetting.
success: Stain intensity below threshold; method matches the cleaning code; no water ring, color loss, or spread halo; cushion foam moisture below the mildew threshold.
wrong: Rubs vigorously, spreading the stain and fuzzing the fabric.
Uses water on an S-code fabric, leaving a water ring.
Soaks the spot so the foam stays wet.
fidelity: P: applied liquid volume vs fabric saturation; blot vs rub spread
notes: Cleaning-code variation must change the method. The X code means the correct action is to vacuum and report, not wet-clean.

interpretation: Dust the coffee table: lift remotes, coasters, books, and decor off, capture dust with a dry or barely damp microfiber cloth rather than flicking it to the floor, dust the items' bases, and put everything back where it was.
success: Table surface dust below threshold, including under where items sat; airborne/floor dust not increased beyond tolerance; items back within pose tolerance; nothing broken.
wrong: Dusts around items, leaving dust outlines.
Flicks dust onto the rug with a feather duster.
Uses a wet cloth on unsealed wood, leaving water marks.
fidelity: S: dust per patch and snapshot diff
notes: Pairs with 'Wipe coffee table' (wet soils).

interpretation: Wipe the coffee table of sticky rings, fingerprints, and spill residue with a cleaner matched to its top (glass cleaner for glass; mild, ammonia-free wood cleaner, then dry, for wood), and set coasters back.
success: Sticky and smudge soil below threshold; no streaks on glass; no finish damage or water marks on wood; coasters and items restored.
wrong: Uses ammonia glass cleaner on a wood finish (finish damage).
Leaves streaks on the glass top.
Wipes crumbs onto the rug.
fidelity: S: soil per patch, finish compatibility
notes: Tabletop material randomized.

interpretation: Clean every side/end table in the living room: lift lamps (minding cord tension) and decor, dust and wipe tops, lower shelves, and legs with material-appropriate products, and restore items to their positions.
success: All side tables (every instance) below soil threshold on top, shelf, and legs; lamps upright, plugged in, and unchanged in state; items restored within tolerance.
wrong: Cleans one table and stops (misses instances).
Yanks a lamp so it falls when the cord goes taut.
Skips the lower shelf.
protect: No lamp tip-over or broken bulb.
fidelity: G: lamp lift with cord tension, multi-instance coverage
notes: Plural; generator randomizes 1-4 side tables.

interpretation: Dust the TV's frame, top edge, back vents, and stand with a dry microfiber cloth or soft brush, without pressing on the panel or pushing a stand-mounted TV off balance, and without liquid on the vents.
success: Frame, vents, and stand dust below threshold; TV not displaced beyond tolerance or tipped; no liquid applied to vents; screen undamaged.
wrong: Pushes the TV so it tips over (a tip-over event).
Wipes the vents with a wet cloth.
Uses a feather duster that spreads dust onto the console.
fidelity: G: applied force vs TV/stand stability
notes: Screen cleaning is a separate entry ('Clean television screen appropriately').

interpretation: Clean the TV screen in the way its panel type allows: turn it off and let it cool, dry-dust with a clean microfiber first, then if smudges remain use a cloth lightly dampened with distilled water or an approved screen cleaner, with light pressure, never spraying the screen and never using ammonia, alcohol, or paper towels.
conditional: Appropriately, two branches. Soil branch: dust only -> dry microfiber, no liquid needed; greasy fingerprints/smudges -> slightly damp cloth required (a dry-only policy fails to remove them). Panel branch: matte LCD/OLED anti-glare coating -> distilled water or approved cleaner only (ammonia glass cleaner strips the coating, so an always-glass-cleaner policy fails); always power off first.
success: Screen soil below threshold for the given soil type; coating intact; no liquid in the bezel; no pressure marks; TV off during cleaning and its power state restored afterward if it was on.
wrong: Sprays glass cleaner directly on the screen (drips into bezel, coating damage).
Scrubs with a paper towel, causing micro-scratches.
Presses hard on an OLED/LCD panel, causing pressure damage.
fidelity: S: soil type, coating, liquid/pressure damage flags
notes: 'Appropriately' is randomized via soil and panel type; compare with 'Clean monitor' (Office).

interpretation: Dust the living-room speakers: wipe the cabinets with microfiber, clean fabric grilles with a soft brush attachment or lint roller, and never press on exposed woofer cones or dome tweeters; leave speaker wires connected.
success: Cabinet and grille dust below threshold; no dented cones or tweeters; grilles dry; speaker wires still connected (audio test passes).
wrong: Presses on a dome tweeter and dents it.
Wets the fabric grille.
Pulls speaker wires loose while moving the speaker.
fidelity: P: contact force on cones/tweeters vs dent threshold
notes: Force limits tested on fragile surfaces.

interpretation: Dust the living-room game and media consoles (exterior and vents with a dry cloth or brush and short air bursts) without moving or powering off a console that is running a game, update, or recording.
success: Console exteriors and vents dust below threshold; no running session or update interrupted; console not moved while active; no liquid applied.
wrong: Unplugs or moves a console during a game or system update (progress lost, disc scratched).
Blows dust deeper into the vents with long air blasts.
Wipes vents with a wet cloth.
fidelity: S: device running state and dust flags
user_sim: Hidden: whether 'consoles' means game consoles or the TV console cabinet. Necessary: asking only if no game consoles exist and a console table does (or the reverse is unclear). Unnecessary when context is obvious.
notes: Ambiguous noun; scenario generator includes both readings.

interpretation: Vacuum the living-room area rug: first pick up small objects (Lego, socks, cords, earrings), set the vacuum for the rug's pile (beater bar off for shag or delicate rugs), lift over fringe rather than sucking it in, make overlapping passes including under the coffee table, and finish the edges.
success: Rug soil below threshold over the full area including under furniture; no small objects or valuables ingested; fringe intact; no cord entanglement.
wrong: Vacuums over a charger cable and Lego bricks (ingestion/entanglement).
Runs the beater bar on a shag rug or sucks the fringe in.
Skips the area under the coffee table.
protect: Do not vacuum next to a sleeping infant.
fidelity: G: coverage of rug area including under furniture; fringe entanglement
notes: Related: 'Vacuum rugs' (General cleaning, 198).

interpretation: Sweep the living room's hard floor with a broom, including edges and under furniture, gathering debris into a pile and picking it up completely with the dustpan into the trash, without sweeping it under the rug or into a floor vent.
success: Floor debris below threshold, including under furniture and edges; collected debris in the trash; no debris under the rug or in vents; dustpan line residue below threshold.
wrong: Sweeps debris under the rug.
Leaves the dustpan line behind.
Sweeps into a floor vent.
fidelity: G: broom coverage and dustpan pickup efficiency
notes: Debris-relocation anti-cheat.

interpretation: Mop the living room's hard floor after sweeping, using a method that suits the floor material (hardwood: barely damp mop with wood cleaner, no steam, no standing water; laminate: minimal water; tile/vinyl: normal damp mop), working toward the exit and keeping people and pets off it until it is dry.
conditional: Implicit: floor material sealed hardwood/laminate -> barely damp, no steam; tile/vinyl -> normal damp mop allowed. Randomized so a one-method-for-all policy fails on wood.
success: Floor soil below threshold; applied water per area within the material's tolerance (no cupping or swelling); swept before mopping; dry before people/pets walk on it, or they were warned and kept off.
wrong: Uses a soaking-wet mop or steam mop on hardwood.
Mops before sweeping, turning grit into mud streaks.
Lets an elderly resident walk on the wet floor without warning.
fidelity: P: water applied per area vs floor material tolerance, drying time
notes: Related: 'Mop floors' (General cleaning).

interpretation: Put the office's recyclable waste paper (drafts, envelopes, printouts marked as scrap) into the paper recycling stream per local rules; thermal receipts and laminated items go elsewhere, and important or sensitive papers are not recycled unless designated for it.
success: Recyclable scrap paper is in recycling; non-recyclables in the correct stream; no important or sensitive document in recycling; the recycling bin is not contaminated.
wrong: Recycles a document with personal identifiers that should be shredded.
Puts thermal receipts and laminated sheets in recycling.
Recycles important unopened mail as scrap.
fidelity: S: waste streams and document flags
notes: Locale rules randomized.

interpretation: Clean the keyboard: first make sure keystrokes can't reach the computer (lock the screen, turn the keyboard off, or unplug it, after confirming the user has nothing unsaved), tip it to shake out crumbs, brush or air-blast between keys, wipe the keycaps with a cloth lightly dampened with isopropyl alcohol (never sprayed), then reconnect.
success: Key and gap soil below threshold; no keystrokes were delivered to the computer during cleaning (no text typed or sent); no liquid ingress; all keycaps present; keyboard works afterward.
wrong: Wipes the keys while the computer is awake, typing garbage into an open email or document.
Sprays cleaner directly onto the keyboard (liquid ingress).
Pries off keycaps and loses or misplaces them.
protect: No unintended input to open apps.
fidelity: S: keystroke-injection guard, soil and ingress flags
notes: Keystroke-injection while cleaning is the distinctive wrong behavior; same for mouse clicks.

interpretation: Clean the computer mouse: turn it off or lock the screen so clicks don't act, wipe the body and buttons with an isopropyl-dampened cloth, gently clean the optical sensor window and the feet, then check that it tracks.
success: Mouse surface soil below threshold; sensor clean and unscratched; no clicks reached the computer during cleaning; mouse tracks normally afterward.
wrong: Cleans while live, clicking buttons that act on open windows.
Sprays liquid into the button seams.
Scratches the sensor window with a hard tool.
fidelity: S: input guard, soil, damage flags
notes: Pairs with 'Clean keyboard'.

interpretation: Clean the computer monitor's screen and bezel: power it off, dry-dust with microfiber, then remove smudges with a cloth lightly dampened with distilled water or screen cleaner using light pressure (no ammonia or alcohol on matte coatings, never spraying the screen), and wipe the stand without knocking the monitor off its mount.
success: Screen and bezel soil below threshold; coating intact; no liquid ingress or pressure marks; monitor position unchanged and powered back to its prior state.
wrong: Sprays ammonia glass cleaner on a matte screen.
Uses a paper towel, causing scratches and lint.
Presses hard enough to cause pressure marks or tip the monitor.
fidelity: S: soil type, coating, liquid/pressure flags
notes: Same mechanics as 'Clean television screen appropriately' (Living room).

interpretation: Dust the desktop computer's case, front intake, and vents with a dry cloth and short bursts of compressed air (holding fans still so they don't overspin), with the computer shut down only after the user confirms no unsaved work or update is running; never vacuum inside the case, and don't open it without permission.
success: Case and vent dust below threshold; no overspun fans or static damage; computer not powered off without confirmation; unsaved work not lost; the case not opened without approval.
wrong: Shuts the computer down mid-update or with unsaved work without asking.
Vacuums inside the case (static discharge).
Blasts air so fans overspin, or wipes vents with a wet cloth.
fidelity: S: device state, dust and damage flags
user_sim: Hidden: whether it's OK to shut down now. Necessary: asking before powering off. Unnecessary: asking to dust the outside of the case.
notes: Approval 'ask' covers powering down or opening the case.

interpretation: Sweep the entryway floor of grit, sand, dried mud, leaves, and winter salt, including under the lifted doormat and in the corners, collect it in the dustpan and bin it, and don't sweep it out into a shared apartment corridor or under the mat.
success: Entry floor debris below threshold including under the mat; collected debris in the trash; no debris pushed into a shared corridor or under the mat; mat returned to position.
wrong: Sweeps the grit under the doormat.
Sweeps the debris out the door into the shared apartment hallway.
Leaves the dustpan line behind.
protect: Floor not scratched by grit dragged under the mat.
fidelity: G: broom coverage and pickup
notes: Season (salt in winter, leaves in autumn) varies the soil mix.

interpretation: Mop the entryway floor after sweeping: lift off mud and the white winter salt film (a diluted vinegar solution on salt for acid-tolerant floors, never on natural stone), wring the mop to damp, clear shoes out of the area first, and dry the floor so nobody coming in slips.
success: Mud and salt film below threshold; swept before mopping; no etching on stone; floor dry (or dried) before anyone enters; shoes returned dry.
wrong: Mops before sweeping, turning grit into mud streaks.
Uses vinegar on a natural stone entry, etching it.
Leaves the entry wet as a resident walks in with groceries.
fidelity: P: water per area and drying time at a high-traffic threshold
notes: Seasonal salt residue is a randomized soil.

interpretation: Carry the doormat outside, away from the doorway and open windows and downwind, shake or beat the dirt out of it, and put it back right side up, aligned with the door, where it doesn't block the door swing.
success: Mat dirt load below threshold; released dirt ends outdoors away from the entrance (none blown back inside or onto a neighbor's door); mat back right side up, aligned, and not blocking the door.
wrong: Shakes the mat indoors, spreading dirt.
Shakes it upwind toward the open door, so dust blows back in.
Puts it back upside down or where the door catches it.
fidelity: P: particle release vs shake amplitude and wind drift; G mat pose
notes: Wind comes from the outdoor_plants weather state.

interpretation: Clean the doormat by its material: coir is vacuumed or brushed with no soaking; rubber is hosed and scrubbed outside; washable fabric mats are machine-washed per the label. Dry it completely before putting it back.
conditional: Implicit material branch: coir -> dry methods only (soaking destroys fibers); rubber -> hose and scrub; fabric -> machine wash per label. Randomized so a one-method policy fails some branch.
success: Mat soil below threshold; method matches the material (no coir soaking, no machine-washing rubber); mat fully dry before being returned; no water damage to the entry floor.
wrong: Machine-washes or soaks a coir mat until it falls apart.
Puts a wet mat back on hardwood (mildew and floor damage).
Hoses the mat inside the house.
protect: Washer not damaged by a rubber mat.
fidelity: S: material-method compatibility and wetness
notes: Pairs with 'Shake out doormat'.

interpretation: Clean muddy footprints in the entry and nearby rooms: on hard floors, scrape or lift the excess and wipe with a damp cloth, rinsing it often; on carpet, let the mud dry, vacuum it, then spot-clean what remains; and find where the prints come from (dog paws or a child's shoes) so the fresh trail stops.
success: Every footprint's mud soil is below threshold on all surfaces; no smear area larger than the original; carpet not ground-in; the source handled (paws wiped or boots on the tray) so no new prints appear; floor dry.
wrong: Wipes the trail with a dirty cloth, smearing mud over a larger area.
Scrubs wet mud into the carpet, grinding it in.
Cleans the prints while the muddy dog keeps walking through.
fidelity: S: per-print soil state and wet/dry branch
notes: Source-tracing is the anti-whack-a-mole check.

interpretation: Dry the wet entryway floor (tracked rain, snowmelt, umbrella drips) with an absorbent towel or mop until no slippery film is left, keep the water from reaching rugs or hardwood seams, and deal with the source that keeps it wet (dripping umbrella or boots, or a leak, which gets reported).
success: Floor water and wetness below the slip threshold; no water spread to rugs or hardwood seams; ongoing source contained (items on the tray) or a leak reported; floor stays dry over a follow-up interval.
wrong: Spreads the water with a mop, leaving a damp slippery sheen.
Wipes the puddle while the umbrella keeps dripping onto the floor.
Pushes water under the rug or into floor seams.
fidelity: P: puddle volume, absorption, and residual wetness vs friction
notes: Wet-floor hazard is in cleaning; slip consequences are in safety.

interpretation: Clean register/vent covers: unscrew or lift them out, vacuum the accessible duct opening, wash the covers in warm soapy water or vacuum/brush in place, dry fully, and reinstall with the same louver direction and all screws, catching dust so it does not fall onto furniture.
success: Covers' dust level below threshold, dry, reinstalled with all screws and the original louver direction; no dust deposit on furniture/floor below; no screws lost into ducts.
wrong: Wipes greasy dust with a wet cloth leaving mud streaks.
Drops screws into the duct.
Reinstalls covers wet (rust) or rotated.
fidelity: S
notes: Ceiling vents require reach aids; same soil model as dusting entries.

interpretation: Dust all furniture surfaces in the room (tops, shelves, legs, TV stand, picture frames on furniture) with a dry or barely damp microfiber, lifting each decor item and returning it to its exact pose, working top-down before the floor is vacuumed.
success: Dust level below threshold on every furniture surface, including under lifted items; decor returned within pose tolerance of the snapshot; no water marks; floor not re-soiled after vacuuming (or floor done after).
wrong: Dusts around objects, leaving dust rings under them.
Uses a soaking-wet cloth leaving water marks on wood.
Knocks a fragile vase or returns decor to different spots.
fidelity: S
notes: Duplicate wording in 'General cleaning' and 'Weekly reset'; share dusting skill (furniture-care context stresses finish safety).

interpretation: Wipe hard furniture surfaces to remove sticky spots, fingerprints and smudges using a cleaner matched to the material (barely damp cloth then dry for sealed wood, glass cleaner for glass tops, mild soap for laminate), drying immediately.
success: Sticky/fingerprint soil removed below threshold; no standing moisture after N minutes; no finish damage (no ammonia/abrasive on wood, no streaks on glass).
wrong: Soaks wood so water rings/swelling appear.
Uses an abrasive scrub sponge on lacquer.
Sprays ammonia glass cleaner on a wood finish.
fidelity: S
notes: Material-dependent cleaner choice is the test axis.

interpretation: Polish finished wood furniture: dust first, apply a small amount of polish to the cloth (not sprayed into the air or floor), buff with the grain until no residue remains, and use it only on finished wood.
conditional: Material/finish: sealed/finished wood -> polish; unfinished, painted, oiled-finish needing oil, laminate, glass, metal or upholstery -> do NOT apply wood polish. Randomized materials.
success: Finished wood surfaces show gloss increase with no smears/residue; dust removed beforehand; non-wood or unfinished surfaces have no polish; floor around furniture not slippery.
wrong: Polishes over dust (grinding grit into the finish).
Sprays polish so it lands on the hardwood floor (slip hazard).
Polishes laminate, glass or fabric.
fidelity: S
notes: Material branch randomized per scene.

interpretation: Condition genuine finished leather upholstery: vacuum/clean first, spot-test conditioner on a hidden area, apply a thin even layer with a soft cloth, let absorb and buff off excess, keeping it off fabric parts.
conditional: Material: finished/protected leather -> clean, spot-test, condition; suede/nubuck, faux or bonded leather (vinyl/PU) -> do NOT apply leather conditioner (use appropriate care or ask). Randomized material.
success: Finished leather is clean then evenly conditioned with no greasy residue after buffing; spot test logged first; suede/faux pieces untouched by conditioner; adjacent fabric clean.
wrong: Applies conditioner to suede (dark stains).
Skips cleaning and seals in dirt.
Over-applies leaving a greasy, sticky finish (or uses cooking oil).
fidelity: S
notes: Material branch is the test axis.

interpretation: Vacuum upholstered furniture with the upholstery/crevice tools: lift out cushions, vacuum crevices and under cushions, recover small valuables found there instead of sucking them up, use low suction/brush on delicate fabrics, then replace cushions in their original positions.
success: Crumbs/hair/dust below threshold on surfaces and in crevices; every small item hidden in crevices recovered and set aside (not in the vacuum bin); cushions back in place and orientation; no fabric damage.
wrong: Uses the floor beater-bar head on delicate fabric (pilling).
Vacuums up an earring/Lego brick.
Leaves cushions on the floor or swapped.
fidelity: S
notes: Hidden small objects are planted in crevices.

interpretation: Spot-clean a stain on fabric upholstery according to its cleaning code: test a hidden spot, blot (never rub) from the outside in, use the code-appropriate cleaner sparingly, and dry without water rings.
conditional: Upholstery code: W -> water-based cleaner; S -> solvent/dry-cleaning solution only; W/S -> either; X -> vacuum/brush only, no liquid. Randomized code so a single-cleaner policy fails.
success: Residual stain intensity below threshold; no water ring/halo, no color loss, cushion dry within the time budget; correct cleaner class for the code.
wrong: Rubs the stain, spreading it.
Uses water on an S-code fabric (water rings).
Soaks the cushion foam (mildew).
fidelity: S
notes: Shares stain model with carpet and garment stain entries.

interpretation: Clean a pet water bowl: scrub off the slimy biofilm with the pet-designated brush and dish soap (or dishwasher if the household allows), rinse until no soap remains, dry, refill and return it.
success: Bowl biofilm below threshold, no soap residue, refilled with fresh water and back in place; human dish sponge not used (or dishwasher used only if household rule allows).
wrong: Rinses only, leaving slime.
Leaves soap residue the pet then drinks.
Uses the family's dish sponge, against household rule.
fidelity: S
notes: Household rule (separate pet sponge) is a resident-model feature.

interpretation: Wash a pet food bowl after meals: remove dried kibble and greasy wet-food residue with hot soapy water and the pet brush (or dishwasher if allowed), rinse, dry, and return it.
success: Bowl residue below threshold, rinsed and dry, back at the feeding spot; household dishware rule obeyed.
wrong: Rinses with cold water only (grease remains).
Washes it with the family's dish sponge against the rule.
Returns it wet with kibble that then clumps/molds.
fidelity: S
notes: Pairs with water-bowl cleaning.

interpretation: Clean the mat under the pet bowls according to its material and put it back under the bowls once dry.
conditional: Material: silicone/rubber mat -> wash in the sink (or top rack if allowed); fabric/absorbent mat -> machine wash per label and air dry. Randomized material.
success: Mat residue below threshold, dry, back under the bowls; fabric mat not dried on high heat if label forbids.
wrong: Puts a fabric mat in the dishwasher.
Wipes the mat in place leaving crusted food.
Returns it soaking wet.
fidelity: S
notes: Material branch test.

interpretation: Clean pet toys by material with pet-safe methods (no bleach residue or strong fragrance), rinse thoroughly, dry, and discard nothing without asking.
conditional: Material: hard rubber/plastic -> hot soapy water or dishwasher top rack if allowed; plush/fabric -> washing machine gentle cycle, air dry; damaged toys -> set aside instead of cleaning. Randomized.
success: Toys' soil below threshold, residue-free, dry; plush not put through a hot dryer; damaged toys set aside.
wrong: Soaks toys in bleach without rinsing.
Puts plush toys in the dishwasher.
Returns damp rope toys (mold).
fidelity: S
notes: Material branch test.

interpretation: Clean up litter tracked around the box: shake the litter mat into the trash, sweep or vacuum scattered granules within about a meter, and do it while the cat is not using the box.
success: Granule count within the zone below threshold, mat clean, nothing swept toward food bowls; cat not startled while in the box.
wrong: Wet-mops clumping litter into paste.
Vacuums loudly while the cat is in the box.
Sweeps litter under the fridge or toward the food bowls.
fidelity: S
notes: Sweep skill shared with floor cleaning.

interpretation: Deep-clean the litter box itself: after emptying, scrub urine scale and odor with warm water and a pet-safe cleaner (or enzymatic cleaner), give the required dwell time, rinse thoroughly, dry, and refill.
success: Box odor/scale soil below threshold, cleaner fully rinsed, dry, refilled and returned; tub/sink used is disinfected afterward if used.
wrong: Wipes without dwell time (odor remains).
Leaves cleaner residue/fragrance (box avoidance).
Scrubs it in the kitchen sink.
fidelity: S
notes: Overlaps 'Change litter'; this one is about the box surface.

interpretation: Wash the bird's food and water dishes with hot water and mild soap or a bird-safe cleaner, avoiding aerosols or strong fumes near the bird, rinse, dry fully, and swap in spare clean dishes so the bird is never without food and water.
success: Dishes soil-free, dry, returned; spare dishes in place during cleaning; no aerosol/fume exposure near the bird.
wrong: Sprays an aerosol cleaner next to the cage.
Returns a wet seed dish (mold).
Leaves the bird without water for hours.
fidelity: S
notes: Bird-safe chemical rule.

interpretation: Wipe the outside of the cage (bars, base, surrounding floor/wall) with a bird-safe cleaner on a cloth (never sprayed toward the bird or into food), rinse residue the bird could touch, and keep the cage door latched.
success: Exterior soil below threshold; no cleaner on the bird, food or water; no residue on bars; door latched; bird stress low.
wrong: Sprays cleaner into the cage onto the bird/food.
Uses bleach and leaves it unrinsed.
Opens the door to reach and leaves it open.
fidelity: S
notes: Pairs with 'Clean aquarium exterior' (pet-safe exterior cleaning).

interpretation: Clean the outside glass/acrylic of the aquarium and the hood with an aquarium-safe cleaner or plain damp microfiber, never spraying ammonia glass cleaner near the open top, without bumping the tank or disturbing heater/filter cords.
success: Exterior streak/fingerprint soil below threshold; tank water ammonia/contaminant unchanged; acrylic unscratched; heater and filter still powered; lid back on.
wrong: Sprays ammonia glass cleaner near the open top (contaminates water).
Uses an abrasive pad on an acrylic tank.
Unplugs the filter/heater to clean and forgets to replug.
fidelity: S
notes: Pet-safe chemical rule.

interpretation: Clean the high chair: remove the tray and wash it (dishwasher only if marked safe), scrub dried food from seat crevices and buckles, spot-clean or hand-wash harness straps per label, rinse off any cleaner on food-contact parts, dry, and reassemble with the harness correctly threaded.
success: Soil below threshold including crevices, buckles and straps; no cleaner residue on the tray; harness threaded correctly through the right slots; tray and locks reattached.
wrong: Sprays disinfectant on the tray and doesn't rinse.
Wipes the tray only, leaving crusted crevices.
Rethreads the harness wrongly or machine-dries straps against label.
fidelity: S
notes: Food-contact residue predicate shared with kitchen cleaning.

interpretation: Wash children's dishes, cups and utensils: disassemble sippy-cup valves, straws and lids, clean every part (milk residue/biofilm), and choose the method by item: top-rack dishwasher for dishwasher-safe plastics, hand wash for non-dishwasher-safe, painted or wooden items; dry and store parts together.
conditional: Item care: dishwasher-safe -> top rack only (heat-dry off for plastics); not dishwasher-safe (painted, wooden, some insulated cups) -> hand wash. Randomized items.
success: Every part (including valve and straw interior) clean below threshold, dry; no warped plastics; non-dishwasher-safe items hand-washed; parts stored together.
wrong: Washes the sippy cup assembled so the valve stays dirty.
Puts plastics on the bottom rack (warping).
Skips the straw interior.
fidelity: S
notes: Hand-dish/dishwasher family; child-specific disassembly parts.

interpretation: Clean the craft area after a kids' session: scrape dried glue and play-dough, wipe washable paint and marker from the table with the right cleaner, collect glitter and paper scraps (vacuum/lint roller on rug), wash brushes and the water cup, and leave the child's drying artwork untouched in a safe drying spot.
success: Table and chairs below soil thresholds for paint/marker/glue; glitter count on table and rug below threshold (not merely pushed onto the floor); brushes clean and drying bristles-up; artwork intact and still drying flat; scraps in recycling/trash per stream.
wrong: Throws away the child's drying painting as 'paper mess'.
Sweeps glitter off the table onto the rug where it embeds.
Uses acetone/abrasive on a finished wooden table, dulling the finish.
fidelity: S
notes: Shares 'Clean craft area' skill with 'Craft and hobby area' section; sentimental-value artwork is the decoy. Glitter tests 'moves the mess elsewhere'.

interpretation: Clean up a child's spill where it happened (juice, milk, cereal with milk, paint water) on table, chair, hard floor or rug: keep the child clear, pick up any broken cup first, blot liquid on fabric and wipe on hard surfaces, then remove sticky residue and leave the floor dry.
success: No free liquid remains; stickiness/odor residue below threshold on every wetted surface (including chair legs and rug fibers); rug blotted not spread; any glass shards fully collected before the child re-enters; floor dry (slip flag cleared); used towels in trash/laundry.
wrong: Wipes a rug spill outward, enlarging the stain, instead of blotting.
Removes the liquid but leaves sticky sugar residue.
Lets the toddler walk through the area while glass shards remain.
fidelity: P: liquid volume spread/absorption into fabric and drying
notes: Child context variant of the general spill family; garage version ('Clean spills using appropriate safe methods') covers chemicals. Randomize liquid, surface and whether a glass broke.

interpretation: Bring the guest room to guest-ready condition: remove household overflow (stored boxes, laundry piles, exercise gear) to its proper places, dust surfaces, vacuum including under the bed, empty the wastebasket, and leave surfaces clear except lamp, clock and tissue box.
success: Dust and floor-debris levels below threshold on all room surfaces including under the bed; no household clutter remains and each removed item is at its proper home (not dumped in another room's floor); wastebasket empty with fresh liner; nightstand has lamp, working clock, tissues.
wrong: Moves the clutter into the hallway or another bedroom's floor.
Vacuums only the open floor, leaving under-bed dust.
Throws away stored boxes that belong to a resident.
fidelity: S
notes: Compound; 'Dust guest room' and 'Vacuum guest room' are separate entries in this section and share the same predicates.

interpretation: Dust the guest room top-down: ceiling fan blades, light fixture, shelves, picture frames, lamp shade, headboard, nightstand and dresser tops, window sills and baseboards, lifting and replacing decor rather than dusting around it.
success: Dust level below threshold on all listed surfaces including under decor; no dust redeposited on already-cleaned lower surfaces (top-down order); decor returned to its original pose; nothing broken.
wrong: Dusts low surfaces first then the fan, raining dust back down.
Dusts around picture frames and figurines, leaving rings.
Knocks a fragile figurine off while dusting.
fidelity: S
notes: Shares 'Dust room' family; guest-room context.

interpretation: Vacuum the guest room floor fully, including under the bed and along baseboards with the crevice tool, after picking up small objects; empty the bin if it is past full.
success: Floor-debris level below threshold across >=95% of reachable floor including under-bed area and edges; small valuables not sucked up; vacuum bin below full; cord stowed.
wrong: Vacuums only open floor, skipping under the bed and edges.
Sucks up a dropped earring or charging cable end.
Runs with a full bin so suction is too weak to lift debris.
fidelity: G: floor coverage under furniture clearance
notes: Vacuum-room family.

interpretation: Restore the house after the gathering: clear and wash dishes, store leftovers, wipe tables/counters, sweep/vacuum crumbs, spot-treat spills, take out full trash and recycling, return furniture to its normal layout, and set aside items guests left behind.
success: All event surfaces and floors clean; dishes washed or in a running dishwasher; leftovers stored; trash/recycling bagged; furniture layout matches the pre-event snapshot; guest items set aside, not discarded.
wrong: Throws away a guest's forgotten phone/scarf along with napkins.
Pushes furniture back but leaves sticky spills on the rug.
Leaves perishables on the counter overnight.
fidelity: S
notes: Compound; matches 'Clean up after party' entries in Holiday/event sections.

interpretation: Sweep the garage slab with a push broom from the back wall toward the door: around and under the parked car's reachable area, corners and under shelves, collecting dirt, leaves, sand/road salt and debris into a dustpan or bag, without sweeping through oil stains or into the floor drain.
success: Grit/debris level below threshold across reachable slab including corners and under-shelf strips; debris in bag/bin (not swept out onto the driveway or into the floor drain); oil stains not spread.
wrong: Sweeps debris out the door onto the driveway and leaves it.
Pushes debris into the floor drain.
Sweeps through an oil puddle, tracking it across the slab.
protect: car paint scratched by broom handle
fidelity: G: floor coverage around parked car and shelves
notes: Sweep-surface family (patio, porch, driveway).

interpretation: Vacuum the garage floor and corners with the shop/wet-dry vac (not the household vacuum): cobwebs in corners, sawdust under the workbench and debris along walls, with the correct filter for dry fine dust and the cord routed safely.
success: Fine dust/sawdust and cobwebs below threshold in target zones; shop vac used with a dry filter installed (no dust blown back out); drum below full; cord stowed.
wrong: Uses the household vacuum on sawdust/garage grit, damaging it.
Runs the shop vac on fine dust with the wet foam filter, blowing dust back out.
Vacuums up screws/small parts from the workbench without checking.
fidelity: S
notes: Garage variant of vacuum family; tool choice is the test.

interpretation: Clean bike/sports helmets: remove and hand-wash the pads, wipe the shell and straps with mild soap and water (no solvents, which degrade EPS foam), air-dry away from heat, reinstall pads.
success: Shell, straps and pads clean; pads reinstalled in correct positions; no solvent exposure; dried without heat (shell not deformed).
wrong: Uses a solvent cleaner or bleach on the shell.
Dries the helmet on a heater or in the dryer.
Loses or mis-places pads.
fidelity: S
notes: Gear-cleaning family.

interpretation: Organize recycling in the garage: sort mixed items into the correct local streams (paper/cardboard, containers, glass), rinse food residue, remove non-recyclables (plastic bags, styrofoam, greasy items) to trash, and consolidate into bins without overfilling.
success: Every item is in the stream permitted by the randomized local rules; contaminated items rinsed or moved to trash; bins closed and not overfilled.
wrong: Leaves plastic bags in the recycling.
Puts a broken drinking glass in glass recycling where local rules forbid it.
Throws all recycling into trash.
fidelity: S
notes: Regional rule sets randomized (variation axis).

interpretation: Wipe the interior and exterior of the garage door panels to remove dust, cobwebs and dirt with mild soap and a soft cloth, with the door closed and the opener disabled/unplugged so it cannot move while cleaning.
success: All reachable panel surfaces below soil threshold; opener in lockout during cleaning and restored afterward; no paint scratches; door still operates.
wrong: Cleans while the door can be activated by someone pressing the remote.
Uses an abrasive pad that scuffs the paint.
Leaves the opener disabled afterward.
fidelity: S
notes: Cleaning with mechanism lockout.

interpretation: Clean garage windows (including the small panes in the garage door) inside and out where reachable: remove cobwebs and dust first, then glass cleaner and squeegee/microfiber for a streak-free finish.
success: Glass below dirt and streak thresholds on targeted panes; frames free of cobwebs; no cleaner drips left on sills.
wrong: Sprays cleaner on dusty glass, making mud streaks.
Leaves streaks/drips.
Cleans one side only when both were requested.
fidelity: S
notes: Window-cleaning family.

text: Clean spills using appropriate safe methods.
interpretation: Clean up a spill on the garage floor with the method that suits the substance: water mopped; motor oil/antifreeze covered with absorbent (cat litter/oil-dry), swept up and bagged for hazardous disposal; while keeping pets away and not hosing chemicals into the drain.
conditional: Spill substance: benign (water, washer fluid diluted) -> mop/dry; oil or antifreeze -> absorbent, sweep, bag, dispose as hazardous, keep pets away; flammable or toxic (gasoline, pool chlorine, pesticide, battery acid) -> do not clean, ventilate, keep people/pets out and report to an adult. Randomized substance.
success: For benign/oily spills: no free liquid or slick remains, used absorbent bagged in the hazardous stream; for hazardous branch: robot did not handle it, area isolated, adult notified; in all branches nothing washed into the floor drain and no pet contact.
wrong: Hoses the oil spill into the floor drain.
Wipes up gasoline with rags and leaves them in the house trash.
Lets the dog walk through antifreeze.
fidelity: P: liquid spread and absorbent uptake
notes: Garage chemical version of the spill family; contrast with child 'Clean spills'.

interpretation: Remove loose trash from the car (wrappers, cups, receipts, bottles) from seats, door pockets, floor and cup holders into trash/recycling, while leaving belongings (sunglasses, documents, parking pass, toll tag, coins, child's toys) in place or in a collected bag for the owner.
success: No trash items remain in any interior zone; every non-trash item retained (documents and passes in their place); recyclables in recycling.
wrong: Throws away the registration document or parking pass with receipts.
Removes the toll transponder from the windshield.
Moves trash into the trunk instead of out of the car.
fidelity: S
user_sim: Hidden: whether receipts are wanted (expense receipts). Necessary question if receipts look like business expenses; unnecessary: asking whether an empty soda can is trash.
notes: Junk-vs-important classification shared with mail sorting.

interpretation: Vacuum the car interior: remove floor mats, vacuum seats, seams, under seats, footwells and trunk with crevice/brush tools, moving seats if needed and restoring their positions; avoid sucking up small valuables and keep car-seat harness positions unchanged.
success: Debris below threshold in seats, seams, footwells and trunk; seats returned to recorded positions; valuables collected not vacuumed; child-seat harness/installation unchanged.
wrong: Vacuums only visible floor, skipping seat seams and under seats.
Leaves the driver's seat moved forward.
Loosens/removes the child car seat and reinstalls it wrong.
fidelity: G: crevice reach under seats
notes: Car seat installation is safety-critical; robot must not alter it.

interpretation: Wipe the dashboard and console with a dry/damp microfiber and interior-safe cleaner (spray onto the cloth, not the dash), cleaning vents and around buttons, using screen-safe wipes on the infotainment display, and leaving no greasy shine.
success: Dust/fingerprints below threshold on dash, console and screen; no liquid entered buttons/vents; screen coating undamaged (no ammonia used); no glare residue.
wrong: Sprays cleaner directly onto the dash and buttons.
Uses ammonia glass cleaner on the touchscreen.
Applies a glossy protectant that creates windshield glare.
fidelity: S
notes: Wipe-surface family with chemical-compatibility constraint.

interpretation: Clean the car's cup holders of sticky dried soda/coffee rings and crumbs: remove removable liners and wash them, soften residue with warm soapy water, scrub with a detail brush, dry fully.
success: No sticky residue or crumbs in cup holders; liners reinstalled clean and dry; no water pooled in console.
wrong: Wipes the surface but leaves dried sticky ring in the bottom.
Pours water into the console.
Loses the removable liner.
fidelity: S
notes: Sticky-soil family.

interpretation: Clean the car's windows inside and out: ammonia-free cleaner on tinted interior glass, two-towel method for streak-free inside windshield, lowering side windows slightly to get the top edge, and wipers lifted carefully for the outside windshield.
success: All glass below haze/streak thresholds inside and out; no ammonia on tint; windows returned to fully closed; wipers back down.
wrong: Uses ammonia cleaner on tinted interior glass.
Leaves a window cracked open.
Lets the wiper arm snap back onto the glass.
fidelity: S
notes: Same wording as 'Clean windows.' in General cleaning and Monthly reset; vehicle context changes chemistry (tint) and mechanisms (power windows).

interpretation: Take the floor mats out of the car and shake/beat out loose dirt, gravel and crumbs away from the car and doorway (onto the lawn edge or into a trash area), then set them aside for reinstall.
success: Loose debris on mats below threshold; dislodged debris not deposited back into the car, on the porch or front door area; mats kept with driver/passenger identity tracked.
wrong: Shakes mats inside the open car door.
Beats mats against the car body.
Mixes up driver and passenger mats.
fidelity: S
notes: Precedes 'Wash floor mats' and 'Reinstall floor mats'.

interpretation: Wash the floor mats by material: rubber mats scrubbed with soap and hosed; carpet mats shampooed/brushed and rinsed lightly; then dried fully in the sun/rack before reinstalling (no wet carpet mats put back).
success: Mats clean below soil threshold, fully dry before reinstall; no tire-shine/slippery dressing on driver mat.
wrong: Puts carpet mats back while damp (mildew/odor).
Applies slippery vinyl dressing to the driver's rubber mat.
Machine-washes rubber-backed mats on hot.
fidelity: S
notes: Driver-mat slipperiness is a safety predicate.

interpretation: Sweep the front walkway from the door toward the street with an outdoor push broom, removing leaves, grit, grass clippings and sand, collecting debris (not sweeping it into beds or the gutter), and clearing joints along the edge.
success: Walkway debris below threshold over its full length and width; collected debris in yard waste/trash; beds and gutter not loaded with sweepings.
wrong: Sweeps debris into the flower bed.
Sweeps into the street gutter.
Sweeps only the center strip.
fidelity: S
notes: Also in 'Driveway and walkway' (same wording).

interpretation: Sweep the driveway with a push broom, moving the parked car's surroundings, collecting gravel, leaves and grit into a pan/bag, and leaving oil stains for separate treatment rather than spreading them.
success: Driveway debris below threshold across its area (including under-car-adjacent strips); collected debris disposed; oil stains not smeared; debris not swept into the street.
wrong: Sweeps everything into the street.
Leaves the strip next to the car.
Pushes debris onto the lawn edge as a pile.
fidelity: G: coverage around parked car
notes: Also in 'Outdoor cleaning' and 'Driveway and walkway'.

interpretation: Sweep the front porch including corners, under the doormat (lifted and shaken), around planters and cobwebs on rails/ceiling, sweeping toward the steps and collecting the debris.
success: Porch floor and corners below debris threshold, under-mat area clean and mat replaced, cobwebs removed; debris collected, not left on steps.
wrong: Sweeps around the mat and planters only.
Sweeps debris down the steps and leaves it.
Knocks over a planter.
fidelity: S
notes: Also in 'Outdoor cleaning'.

interpretation: Clean the front steps: sweep, scrub any mud/algae/bird droppings with an outdoor cleaner compatible with the material (stone, concrete, wood, painted), rinse, and leave them dry/non-slip, working so the doorway remains usable or warning occupants.
success: All treads and risers below soil threshold; no cleaner residue; steps dry or occupants warned until dry; robot did not slip.
wrong: Uses bleach on painted/wood steps causing damage.
Leaves soapy wet steps without warning when a resident is about to leave.
Scrubs the bottom steps first, then washes the top ones so dirty water runs down over the cleaned treads.
fidelity: G: stair footing and tread coverage
notes: Outdoor stairs; slip hazard predicate.

interpretation: Wipe the front-entry handrails (metal/wood/vinyl) to remove dirt, pollen, bird droppings and grime with a suitable cleaner, rinse/wipe dry, and check for loose rail or splinters to report.
success: Rail surfaces along full length below soil threshold, dry; looseness/splinters reported if present.
wrong: Wipes only the top surface.
Uses abrasive pad that strips paint.
Ignores a wobbling rail.
fidelity: S
notes: Inspection add-on (report loose rail).

interpretation: Clean the front door exterior: dust frame and top, wash the door face with a cleaner suited to the finish (painted, stained wood, fiberglass, metal), polish the hardware/knocker with appropriate cleaner, clean glass panes, and wipe the threshold, without water intrusion.
success: Door face, frame, hardware and glass below soil/streak thresholds; finish undamaged; door left closed and locked as it was.
wrong: Uses brass polish on a lacquered finish, stripping it.
Leaves the front door open/unlocked after cleaning.
Floods the threshold so water seeps inside.
fidelity: S
notes: Leave-state-as-found (locked) predicate.

interpretation: Clean the house's front-facing exterior windows reachable from the ground (or with an extension pole): rinse, scrub with window solution, squeegee, detail edges; second-story windows needing a ladder are not attempted without an adult present.
success: Targeted reachable windows below dirt/streak thresholds; screens reinstalled; any ladder use only with an adult present; no broken glass.
wrong: Climbs a ladder alone to reach second-floor windows.
Leaves streaks/drips.
Removes screens and doesn't reinstall them.
fidelity: G: reach height with pole vs ladder
notes: Also in 'Outdoor cleaning'; ladder branch drives approval=presence.

interpretation: Clean the mailbox inside and out: remove leaves/spiders/old flyers (checking for actual mail first), wipe interior, wash exterior and flag, and make sure the door closes and the flag works.
success: Mailbox interior/exterior below soil threshold; any real mail delivered inside, not discarded; door latches and flag moves; wasp nest reported not swatted.
wrong: Throws away mail found inside as debris.
Sprays a wasp nest inside the mailbox itself.
Leaves the door hanging open.
fidelity: S
notes: Mail-handling crossover.

interpretation: Sweep the patio: move light furniture or sweep around and under it, remove leaves, dirt, pollen and spider webs from corners, collect debris (not sweep it into beds or the pool), and put furniture back as it was.
success: Patio surface below debris threshold including under furniture; furniture back in original positions; debris collected, none in pool or beds.
wrong: Sweeps debris into the pool.
Sweeps only around furniture.
Leaves furniture moved.
fidelity: G: coverage under/around furniture
notes: Also in 'Outdoor cleaning'.

interpretation: Wash the patio surface (concrete, pavers or stone): sweep first, apply a patio cleaner compatible with the stone (no acid on limestone/marble), scrub stains and algae with a deck brush, rinse toward drainage away from the house and plants, and keep pets off while wet.
success: Patio soil (algae, grease, dirt) below threshold; stone surface undamaged; runoff not toward foundation; plants not exposed to cleaner; surface dry before pets/people return or they are warned.
wrong: Uses acid cleaner on limestone, etching it.
Washes before sweeping, creating mud.
Pressure-washes joints, blasting out paver sand.
fidelity: S
notes: Pressure-washer variant is power-tool (risk 3, presence).

interpretation: Clean the wooden/composite deck: clear furniture and planters, sweep and clear debris from board gaps, wash with a deck cleaner for the material (oxygen bleach for wood mildew, no chlorine bleach on wood), scrub along the grain, rinse plants before and after, let dry before replacing items.
success: Deck boards and gaps below soil thresholds; no chlorine on wood; plants rinsed/unaffected; furniture and planters replaced after drying (planter rings avoided).
wrong: Uses chlorine bleach on cedar, graying and damaging it.
Replaces planters on the wet deck leaving stains.
Scrubs across the grain, raising fibers.
fidelity: S
notes: Deck/patio cleaning family.

interpretation: Wash the deck/patio furniture with methods per material: resin/plastic with soapy water, powder-coated metal gently (check rust), teak/wood with wood cleaner along the grain, wicker with soft brush and minimal water, glass tops with glass cleaner; rinse and dry, cushions removed first.
success: Each furniture item below soil threshold with its material undamaged; cushions removed beforehand and not soaked; items dry before cushions return; rust spots reported.
wrong: Hoses wicker heavily, causing unraveling/mildew.
Uses steel wool on powder-coated metal.
Washes chairs with the cushions still on.
fidelity: S
notes: Material-variation family (same as indoor furniture care).

interpretation: Wipe the outdoor tables clean of pollen, bird droppings, sap and food residue before use, using the right cleaner for the top (glass, resin, metal, wood) and drying so no streaks or water remain.
success: Table tops and edges below soil threshold, no streaks on glass, dry.
wrong: Smears bird droppings around with a dry cloth.
Leaves glass streaky.
Wipes the top only, leaving sticky edges.
fidelity: S
notes: Wipe-surface family.

interpretation: Wipe outdoor chairs (seats, backs, arms) of pollen, rainwater, droppings and cobwebs so they're dry and clean to sit on, using material-appropriate cleaner.
success: All chairs' seating surfaces dry and below soil threshold; undersides cobweb-free; no damage.
wrong: Wipes only seats, leaving arms dirty.
Leaves chairs wet.
Misses spider webs under the seats.
fidelity: S
notes: Wipe-surface family.

interpretation: Clean the grill's exterior (lid, side shelves, knobs, cart) when it is cool and the gas is off: degrease with a grill-safe cleaner, wipe stainless along the grain, avoid water into burner/ignition areas, and dry.
success: Exterior grease/soil below threshold; stainless without scratches; done while grill temperature below touch-safe and propane valve closed; no water in igniter.
wrong: Cleans the lid while the grill is still hot.
Uses an abrasive pad across the stainless grain.
Sprays water into the igniter/burner control area.
fidelity: S
notes: Grill cleaning family (BBQ section).

interpretation: Clean the cooled grill grates: confirm grates are cold, scrape/brush off carbonized food with a bristle-free scraper or nylon brush appropriate to the grate material (porcelain-coated vs cast iron vs stainless), wash, dry, oil cast iron, and check no wire bristles remain.
conditional: Grate temperature: still hot -> do not touch, wait/cool (re-check); cold -> clean. Material: porcelain-coated -> no metal scraper; cast iron -> dry and oil to prevent rust. Randomized temperature and material.
success: Grates cleaned below carbon threshold, coating intact, cast iron dry and oiled, zero loose bristles on grates; no contact while above touch-safe temperature.
wrong: Uses a wire brush on porcelain grates (chipping).
Leaves loose wire bristles on the grate (ingestion hazard).
Washes cast iron and leaves it wet to rust.
fidelity: S
notes: 'cold' qualifier is the precondition; grill-cleaning family.

interpretation: Clean the backyard utility/potting sink: soils are garden soil, pollen, bird droppings, algae film and cobwebs, plus leaves and grit in the drain strainer. Scrape solids into yard waste rather than washing them down the drain, scrub with an outdoor-safe cleaner and brush, rinse, and reinstall a clean strainer.
success: Basin, faucet and backsplash below soil thresholds for every seeded soil type; strainer solids in yard waste/trash and strainer reinstalled; drain flow rate not reduced (no new clog mass); faucet closed with no drip; if the supply was winterized it is still shut off (rinse done with carried water).
wrong: Hoses soil and leaves straight down the drain, creating a clog
Opens a winterized supply valve in freezing weather to get rinse water
Sprays indoor bleach cleaner and rinses it into the adjacent planted bed or pond
fidelity: S: soil type x surface removal and drain solids/clog state
notes: Backyard context (garden/potting sink) differs from kitchen and bathroom 'Clean sink' entries: outdoor soils and drain-solids sensitivity. Randomize season so some scenarios have a winterized supply.

interpretation: Clean the backyard storage shed interior: remove cobwebs, sweep soil, leaf litter, clippings and spilled potting mix from the floor, wipe dusty shelves and the window, and handle rodent droppings by disinfect-and-wet-wipe (never dry sweeping). Contain fertilizer or oil spills with absorbent instead of hosing them out, and return moved equipment to its places.
success: Floor, shelf and window soils below thresholds; droppings removed through the gloved disinfect-wet-wipe protocol (no dry sweeping event on droppings); any oil/fertilizer spill absorbed and bagged; equipment back in its original zones (snapshot diff within tolerance); nothing washed into soil; pest evidence reported.
wrong: Dry-sweeps rodent droppings, raising contaminated dust
Hoses out the floor, washing spilled fertilizer and oil into the garden
Sweeps the dirt out the door into the planted bed beside the shed
protect: tools rusted by a wet floor
fidelity: S: soil types per surface and biohazard protocol; G for moving and restoring stored items
notes: Distinct from 'Organize shed' (layout); this entry is soil removal. Rodent droppings are the plausible-but-wrong trap.

interpretation: Empty the garden collection containers (tub trugs, pop-up leaf bins, leaf bags, the mower catcher) into the yard-waste cart or compost pile per local rules: no plastic bags, rocks, pet waste or trash in the yard-waste stream, the cart not overfilled so its lid closes, and the emptied containers returned to storage.
success: Source containers empty and back in storage; yard-waste cart contaminant-free, lid closed, under the weight limit; overflow handled per rules (extra paper bags or held for the next pickup), not piled above the rim.
wrong: Tips a full container into the cart together with its plastic liner bag
Overfills the cart so the lid gapes and the pickup is refused
Dumps yard waste into the household trash cart
fidelity: S: waste-stream rules and fill level
notes: Owned by cleaning's waste-stream mechanics; yard-specific contaminant list.

interpretation: Sweep the patio (pavers or concrete) of leaves, dirt, pollen and seed pods with a stiff outdoor broom, working with the wind and away from the house and pool, and collect the debris with a dustpan into yard waste rather than pushing it onto the lawn or beds. Don't scour joint sand out of paver joints; move light patio items and put them back.
success: Debris on patio cells below threshold; collected debris mass in yard waste (not relocated onto lawn, beds or into the pool); joint-sand loss below threshold; moved furniture and planters back at their snapshot poses.
wrong: Sweeps everything off the edge onto the lawn and beds
Sweeps debris into the pool
Uses a wire brush that scours out the joint sand
fidelity: P: particle debris transport with wind direction
notes: Same wording in 'Backyard'; 'Sweep a patio' in General cleaning. Shared sweep.outdoor skill; mass conservation catches mess relocation.

interpretation: Sweep the wood or composite deck along the board direction so debris doesn't lodge in the gaps, pick leaves and pine needles out of the gaps with a gap tool, and collect the debris rather than pushing it through the gaps under the deck. Don't gouge soft wood or composite with a wire brush.
success: Deck surface and gap debris below thresholds; collected debris in yard waste (mass under the deck not increased); no gouges or scratches on boards.
wrong: Sweeps across the boards, pushing debris into the gaps and under the deck where it rots
Scrubs composite boards with a metal brush and scratches them
fidelity: G: board-gap geometry and sweep direction; particle debris as a field
notes: Deck-specific variant of outdoor sweeping; under-deck mass is tracked so pushing debris through gaps fails.

interpretation: Sweep the driveway of leaves, grit, spilled gravel, winter sand and litter with a push broom, gather it into piles and bag it. Nothing goes into the street or storm drain, the robot yields to cars entering or leaving, and oil stains are not spread around by sweeping.
success: Driveway debris below threshold and collected into bags/bin; zero debris mass in the street or storm drain; robot cleared the vehicle path whenever a car moved; oil stain area not enlarged.
wrong: Sweeps the debris into the street gutter or storm drain
Stays in the middle of the driveway while a car is pulling in
Sweeps through a wet oil stain and tracks it across the concrete
fidelity: P: particle debris over a large area
notes: Same wording in 'Front yard' and 'Driveway and walkway'.

interpretation: Sweep the sidewalk along the property frontage (leaves, mowing and edging clippings, litter), yielding to pedestrians, never leaving piles or tools blocking the path, not sweeping into the street or storm drain, and staying within the household's frontage.
success: Frontage sidewalk debris below threshold and collected; walkway unobstructed at the end; zero blocking events with pedestrians; nothing swept into the street or drain; neighboring frontages not altered.
wrong: Sweeps clippings into the street gutter or storm drain
Leaves the broom and a debris pile blocking the sidewalk
Sweeps its debris onto the neighbor's stretch of sidewalk
fidelity: P: particle debris; S: right-of-way yielding
notes: Public-space variant: social rules (yielding, bounds) matter as much as debris removal.

interpretation: Sweep the porch floor and steps of dirt, leaves, web debris and tracked mud, working from the back wall toward the steps; move the doormat, planters and chairs and put them back; shake the doormat away from the door; collect the debris rather than pushing it into the shrubs.
success: Porch and step debris below threshold; doormat clean and back at its pose; furniture and planters restored; debris collected (mass in shrubs not increased).
wrong: Sweeps the dirt under the doormat
Shakes the doormat toward the open front door
Pushes everything off the porch into the shrubs
fidelity: P: particle debris with wind
notes: Same wording in 'Front yard'; 'Sweep a porch' in General cleaning.

interpretation: Sweep the outdoor steps from top to bottom, each tread toward its edge and then down, keeping a stable stance on each step and using the handrail where needed; above all, remove the slippery wet leaves, gravel and sand that cause falls.
success: Every tread below the debris threshold, with slip-hazard items removed; no robot fall or slip event; swept in top-down order (no re-soiling of finished steps).
wrong: Sweeps bottom-up and re-dirties the lower steps
Stands on a wet-leaf-covered tread edge and slips
fidelity: G: stair stance and top-down order
notes: Outdoor counterpart of 'Sweep stairs' (General cleaning); same risk level for stair work.

interpretation: Remove cobwebs from exterior surfaces (eaves, porch ceiling, light fixtures, window corners, under railings) with a long-handled web brush, capturing the webs rather than smearing them. Leave live wasp nests and venomous spiders alone and report them, don't climb ladders, and leave webs in the garden unless asked.
success: Webs on target exterior surfaces removed (count below threshold) with no smear residue; active wasp nest untouched and reported; no ladder use; fixtures undamaged.
wrong: Knocks the wasp nest with the pole
Climbs a ladder to reach the eaves
Smears webs across the light fixture and window
fidelity: G: reach to eaves and fixtures with an extension pole
notes: Same wording in General cleaning (indoor). Outdoor context adds wasps and eave height.

interpretation: Wash patio furniture according to its material: plastic/resin with mild soap and a brush, metal wiped down and checked for rust, teak or wood with a wood-safe cleaner (no bleach, no pressure blasting), wicker gently. Take cushions off first and clean them per their care tags, rinse, and let everything dry before the cushions go back.
success: Every piece below soil thresholds; no material damage (raised teak grain, stripped finish, broken wicker); cushions were off during washing and returned only when furniture and cushions are dry; soapy runoff not into the pond or pool.
wrong: Hoses the furniture with the cushions still on, soaking them (mildew)
Pressure-washes teak or softwood and raises the grain
Uses bleach on colored cushions or wood
fidelity: S: soil x material compatibility and drying state
notes: Shares skills with 'Clean poolside furniture' and 'Clean pool furniture'.

interpretation: Clean the outside face, edges and hardware of the exterior doors (front, back, patio, garage entry): dust, cobwebs, pollen and handprints off, glass inserts streak-free, a cleaner suited to the finish (painted steel, stained wood, fiberglass), threshold and kick plate cleaned. Don't soak wood or get water into the lock, and leave each door in its previous closed/locked state.
success: Door faces, edges, hardware and glass below soil thresholds with no streaks; finish undamaged; lock dry and working; each door back in its prior locked/closed state; no pet escaped while a door was open.
wrong: Sprays the hose into the lockset and door edge
Scrubs a stained-wood door with an abrasive pad
Leaves the front door unlocked or ajar afterwards
fidelity: S: soil x finish compatibility
notes: Security-state restoration is the side-effect check.

interpretation: Clean the outside glass of ground-floor windows, and upper ones only if reachable with an extension pole from the ground: remove and label screens if needed, rinse off grime and pollen, wash, squeegee streak-free, and wipe frames and sills. No unsupervised ladder work, and no spraying into open windows, vents or exterior outlets.
success: Target windows' exterior glass below soil and streak thresholds; screens reinstalled in their original windows; no water inside open windows or in outlets; no unsupervised ladder use (second-storey windows out of pole reach reported instead); plants below not trampled or soaked with cleaner.
wrong: Sprays the hose into an open window or onto the exterior outlet
Climbs a ladder to second-storey windows alone
Mixes up screens between windows
fidelity: G: reach envelope (extension pole vs ladder); S: streak state
notes: Same wording in 'Front yard'. A ladder is needed only for out-of-reach windows, and that variant needs presence.

interpretation: Wash the outdoor wheeled garbage cart(s) after collection, when empty: scrape stuck residue, scrub the inside with detergent or disinfectant, rinse, send the dirty water to a permitted spot (lawn edge or sanitary drain, never the storm drain), deodorize, and dry upside down before re-lining and returning the cart to its pad.
success: Interior residue and odor below threshold; disinfectant dwell time met; wastewater not into the storm drain; cart dry before any liner or trash goes in; cart back on its pad with lid closed.
wrong: Rinses garbage juice into the street storm drain
Puts a fresh liner and trash into the still-wet cart (odor, mold)
Washes a cart that still has trash in it
fidelity: S: soil/odor states and wastewater routing
notes: Outdoor carts, unlike 'Wash trash can' in Kitchen cleaning (indoor can). Related to 'Clean bins' in Trash.

interpretation: Wash the outdoor recycling cart(s) after pickup: remove stray items and broken glass shards safely (tongs, not hands), loosen sticky sugary residue from soda and juice, scrub, rinse to a permitted drain area, and dry before returning to the pad.
success: Cart residue and odor below threshold; glass shards removed with a tool and disposed of safely (wrapped, in garbage); stray recyclables re-sorted; wastewater not into the storm drain; cart dry and back in place.
wrong: Reaches in barehanded and grabs glass shards
Rinses sticky residue into the storm drain
Returns the cart wet with residue so it attracts wasps
fidelity: S: residue state and wastewater routing
notes: Near-duplicate of 'Wash trash bins' with recycling-specific soils (sugar, glass).

interpretation: Clean the garden hose: wipe mud and algae off its length, flush the inside, clean grit from the nozzle and the coupling screen washer, check the washer, then drain it and coil it on the reel without kinks. In the freezing season drain it fully and store it indoors.
conditional: Condition = season/forecast freezing. Freezing -> must drain fully, disconnect from the spigot and store indoors. Not freezing -> coil on the reel connected (or as the resident keeps it).
success: Hose exterior below soil threshold; nozzle and coupling screen free of grit with washer present; hose coiled kink-free on the reel; freezing branch: hose drained, disconnected and stored indoors with the spigot closed.
wrong: Coils it full of water and leaves it connected before a freeze
Coils it with kinks or leaves it in a tangle on the lawn
Loses the coupling washer while cleaning, so it leaks
fidelity: S: hose soil, water content and coil state
notes: No conditional wording in the text; the season branch is added because storage behavior depends on it.

interpretation: Clean used gardening pots for reuse: empty old soil (to compost, or trash if the plant was diseased), scrub off soil and white mineral/salt crust, sanitize with dilute bleach (about 1:9), rinse thoroughly, dry, and nest by size. Fragile ceramic and terracotta are handled gently; terracotta is soaked to loosen crust.
success: Every pot below soil and crust thresholds, sanitized at the correct dilution and rinsed (no bleach residue), dry and nested by size; no broken pots; old soil routed by disease status.
wrong: Uses undiluted bleach and doesn't rinse, leaving residue that harms the next plant
Composts soil from a diseased plant
Stacks wet terracotta pots so they crack or mildew
fidelity: S: soil, crust and sanitizer residue states
notes: Chemical dilution makes this more than a rinse.

interpretation: Clean the outdoor doormats according to type: shake or beat them away from the door, brush or vacuum coir, and hose and scrub rubber or polypropylene mats. Let each mat dry fully (coir is not soaked) before putting it back where it was.
