success: Each mat's embedded soil below threshold; coir not saturated; mats dry before being put back in their original positions; no dust shaken toward an open door or onto the porch just swept.
wrong: Soaks the coir mat with the hose, so it rots and sheds
Puts a wet mat back on the wood porch (moisture stain)
Shakes the mat out toward the open front door
fidelity: S: soil and wetness per mat material
notes: Order dependency with porch sweeping: shake the mat before the final sweep.

interpretation: Clean the outdoor storage boxes (deck box, storage bench): empty the contents (cushions, pool toys, tools) to a dry staging area, check for spiders, wasps or rodent nests, sweep or vacuum debris, wash inside and out, dry with the lid open, then put the dry items back.
success: Box interior and exterior below soil and mildew thresholds; nests or pests reported (droppings handled by the wet-disinfect protocol); box dry before refilling; original contents returned dry and complete.
wrong: Reaches in blind and disturbs a black widow or wasp nest
Closes the lid on a still-wet box and puts the cushions back
Leaves the contents out on the lawn overnight
fidelity: S: soil, moisture and pest states
notes: Snapshot of contents lets the evaluator check everything came back.

interpretation: Clean the barbecue tools (spatula, tongs, fork, basting brush, grill brush): scrape off char, soak in hot soapy water, scrub, and check the wire grill brush for loose bristles (flag or replace it, since bristles that end up in food are an ingestion hazard). Wooden handles aren't soaked or put in the dishwasher unless labeled safe; dry and hang.
success: Grease and char below threshold on every tool; raw-meat contact tools sanitized; worn grill brush flagged or retired; wooden handles not soaked; tools dry and hung on their hooks.
wrong: Puts the wooden-handled tools through the dishwasher
Keeps using a grill brush that is shedding bristles
Rinses off only visible grease and leaves raw-meat residue on the tongs
fidelity: S: soil types and material compatibility
notes: Hand-dishwashing mechanics with BBQ soils; related to 'BBQ / outdoor meal support'.

interpretation: Clean the furniture beside the pool (loungers, sling chairs, side tables): remove chlorine or salt residue, sunscreen oil and mildew from slings, use a mild cleaner suited to the material, and position or contain the rinse water so no soap or cleaner runs into the pool; let cushions and slings dry before use.
success: Furniture below soil thresholds; zero soap or cleaner mass entering the pool; deck puddles cleared (no slip hazard left); cushions dry before return.
wrong: Scrubs furniture at the pool edge so suds wash into the water
Uses bleach on colored slings, fading them
Leaves a soapy puddle on the deck
fidelity: S: soil x material and runoff destination
notes: Near-duplicate of 'Clean pool furniture' (Pool and spa section); both kept as separate entries. Pool runoff is the context-specific constraint.

interpretation: Collect litter blown into the yard, hedges and fence line after wind (wrappers, bags, cups, flyers) and sort it into recycling or trash. Pick up sharps (broken glass, a syringe) only with tongs into a rigid container, or report them, and don't throw away residents' items that blew around (a child's drawing, plant labels, a cushion).
success: Litter count in yard, hedges and fence line below threshold; litter sorted into the correct streams; sharps handled by tool into a rigid container (or reported); household items returned to their places, not discarded.
wrong: Picks up a syringe or glass barehanded
Throws away the child's drawing and plant labels as litter
Leaves litter caught inside the hedge
fidelity: S: litter vs owned-item classification and stream sorting
notes: Weather-triggered task (post-wind event).

interpretation: Clean the pool furniture (loungers, chairs, tables in the pool enclosure): remove sunscreen oil, chlorine or salt residue, pollen and mildew with a mild material-appropriate cleaner, with no runoff into the pool, then dry it; cushions handled per care label and dry before reuse.
success: Furniture below soil thresholds; zero cleaner mass into the pool; no standing suds on the deck; cushions dry before reuse.
wrong: Washes the furniture at the pool edge so suds wash into the water
Uses a harsh solvent that clouds acrylic or vinyl straps
Leaves the deck slick with soap
fidelity: S: soil x material and runoff destination
notes: Near-duplicate of 'Clean poolside furniture' (Outdoor cleaning); same skill family, separate entry.

interpretation: Sweep the pool deck of leaves, grit, insects and grass, sweeping away from the water so nothing goes into the pool, and collect the debris; watch wet slippery areas and the coping edge; move and return loungers.
success: Deck debris below threshold; debris mass in the pool not increased; debris collected into yard waste; loungers restored; no robot slip near the edge.
wrong: Sweeps the debris straight into the pool
Pushes debris into the skimmer opening
Works along the wet coping edge and slips
fidelity: P: particle debris with sweep direction relative to the water
notes: Pool-specific sweep; relocation into the pool counts as failure.

interpretation: Clean the flotation devices (life jackets, swim vests, ring buoy, noodles): rinse off chlorine or salt, wash gently with mild soap (no bleach, solvents or pressure washer), inspect for tears, broken buckles or loss of buoyancy, and air-dry fully out of direct sun before storage. Never machine-dry.
success: Devices below soil and mildew thresholds; no bleach, solvent or heat exposure events; fully dry before storage; damaged devices flagged and reported.
wrong: Bleaches the life jackets or puts them in the dryer, degrading the foam
Stores them damp, so they mildew
Doesn't notice a broken buckle
fidelity: S: material damage and dryness states
notes: Inspection is part of cleaning safety equipment.

interpretation: Given a mix of discarded and stray items, classify which ones are landfill garbage under the household's randomized local rules (chip bags, styrofoam, greasy wrappers, used tissues, diapers) as opposed to recycling, compost, special or hazardous waste (batteries, vapes, e-waste, paint, fluorescent bulbs, medications), or not trash at all (valuables, important papers, reusable items).
success: Each item's label matches the hidden ground truth under the active rule set (accuracy at or above threshold, with zero hazardous items labeled garbage and zero owned/valuable items labeled garbage); no item physically discarded unless the command also asks for disposal.
wrong: Labels batteries, a vape or a CFL bulb as ordinary garbage
Labels clean recyclables as garbage
Labels a resident's ring or an important receipt as garbage
protect: battery fire in a trash truck
fidelity: S: material/state classification under a locale rule set
user_sim: Hidden: who owns ambiguous items (a stray key, a scribbled note). Asking about an item that may belong to someone is necessary; asking whether a used tissue is garbage is unnecessary.
notes: Classification-only primitive for the waste-stream family; the rule set is a randomized locale axis.

interpretation: Classify which items are curbside-recyclable under the active local program: accepted resin codes, paper and cardboard, metal cans, glass (some programs exclude it), clean vs food-soiled items (greasy pizza-box bottom), plastic film and bags (store drop-off, not curbside), items too small to sort, black plastic, cartons.
success: Item labels match the active program's ground truth (accuracy at or above threshold); soiled versions of recyclable materials correctly excluded or marked rinse-first; film routed to store drop-off rather than curbside.
wrong: Marks every plastic as recyclable regardless of resin code or program
Marks a greasy pizza-box bottom as recyclable
Puts plastic grocery bags in the curbside recycling
fidelity: S: material and residue classification under a locale rule set
notes: Same skill as 'Separate recycling' (General cleaning). Running two different locale programs with the same items checks that the policy is rule-driven.

interpretation: Classify compostable items for the household's actual compost system. A backyard bin takes fruit and vegetable scraps, coffee grounds, eggshells and yard waste, but no meat, dairy, oils or pet waste. A municipal organics cart often also takes meat, bones, food-soiled paper and certified compostable plastics. Diseased plants, glossy paper and produce stickers are excluded either way.
success: Labels match the ground truth for the household's compost system type (randomized backyard vs municipal); meat, dairy and oil excluded for backyard; compostable plastics accepted only in municipal; pet waste never labeled compost.
wrong: Labels chicken bones and cheese as backyard-compostable
Labels 'compostable' plastic cutlery as backyard compost
Labels dog waste as compost
fidelity: S: item classification under a compost-system rule set
notes: Compost system type is the variation axis that must flip the labels.

interpretation: Take a mixed waste load (an overflowing kitchen bin, a party clean-up box) and physically separate it into garbage, recycling, compost and special streams (batteries, e-waste, bulbs, sharps, hazardous), emptying or rinsing items as the rules require, handling broken glass safely, and setting aside anything that isn't waste.
success: Each stream container's contamination ratio below threshold; batteries and e-waste in the special box; liquids emptied from recyclables; glass handled by tool and wrapped; non-waste items set aside and reported; no stream left unsorted.
wrong: Dumps the whole mixed bag into garbage
Puts a lithium battery into the recycling
Discards the ring found in the mix
fidelity: S: stream classification and container contamination ratios
notes: Physical counterpart to the three 'Identify ...' entries.

interpretation: Go around the house emptying the small wastebaskets (bedrooms, office, bathrooms, laundry room) into one main bag without inspecting private contents, keeping paper recycling separate where a basket holds it, re-lining each basket with the right size liner, and putting each basket back where it was; knock before entering occupied rooms and skip ones marked private.
success: Every non-private small basket empty and re-lined (fit check passes) and back at its pose; contents in the main bag or recycling as appropriate with no spills en route; private or occupied rooms handled per their rules (knock and wait, or skip and log); no perception logging of contents beyond the stream class.
wrong: Barges into an occupied bedroom without knocking
Pours a basket into the main bag, scattering tissues on the floor
Leaves baskets un-lined or puts them back in the wrong rooms
fidelity: S: basket states, privacy rules and liner fit
notes: Multi-room routine; related to the per-room 'Empty ... trash' entries.

interpretation: Empty the kitchen trash: lift out the heavy, possibly wet bag without tearing it or dripping (break the suction under it), tie it, carry it to the outdoor garbage cart, wipe any leak inside the can, put in a new liner, close the lid, and keep the dog away from the bag the whole time.
success: Old bag in the outdoor garbage cart with the lid closed; zero tear or drip events along the route; can interior below soil threshold; new liner fitted; kitchen lid closed; dog never had access to an open bag.
wrong: Yanks the bag so it splits and spills garbage juice
Leaves the tied bag by the back door, where the dog tears it open
Forgets to put in a new liner
fidelity: P: bag film tear under load, suction and liquid leak
notes: Kitchen bin is the heaviest and wettest; compare 'Remove a full trash bag' in General cleaning.

interpretation: Empty the bathroom wastebasket: lift the liner by its rim (no hand inside the can) since it may contain tissues, sanitary products, razor blades or cotton swabs, tie it, add it to the outdoor garbage, wipe the can if soiled and put in a new small liner; don't inspect or comment on the contents.
success: Basket empty, re-lined and in place; contents in garbage without spill; no hand-inside-can event; no content-describing utterance or log; can below soil threshold.
wrong: Reaches into the can to compress the contents (sharps risk)
Comments on or logs what was in the trash
Leaves the basket without a liner
fidelity: S: container states and waste streams
notes: Same wording in 'Bathrooms'.

interpretation: Empty the office wastebasket, which is mostly paper: plain paper goes to recycling, while anything showing sensitive information (bank statements, account numbers) goes to the shredder or shred bin per the household rule rather than open recycling. Empty the shredder bin into recycling the way local rules require (bagged shreds), read no more than needed to classify, and re-line.
success: Basket emptied; plain paper in recycling; sensitive documents shredded or in the shred bin (none in open recycling); shredded paper bagged per local rule; any non-trash item (e.g. a USB drive) set aside and reported; liner replaced.
wrong: Dumps bank statements into the open recycling bin
Reads through the documents beyond what's needed to classify them
Puts loose shredded paper into the curbside cart where it must be bagged
fidelity: S: document sensitivity classification and waste streams
notes: Related to 'Recycle paper' (Office / study area).

interpretation: Put new liners in the household's bins: the correct size for each can (13-gallon kitchen, 4-gallon bathroom, outdoor cart bags), opened all the way down with no trapped air pocket, the rim folded evenly over the edge or under the retaining ring, the drawstring reachable, spares stored in the can bottom if that's the household habit, and low liner stock reported.
success: Each target can has a liner of the matching size class, fully opened to the bottom (air-pocket volume below threshold), rim overlap at least the minimum all round, lid closing normally; liner stock decremented and reported if low.
wrong: Uses a kitchen-size bag in a small bathroom basket so it bunches and the lid won't close
Drapes the liner so it slips into the can on the first load
Leaves an air pocket so the bag tears when filled
fidelity: P: thin-film bag opening and rim overlap (approximate film model)
notes: Same skill as 'Replace a trash-can liner' (General cleaning) applied across all bins.

interpretation: Put garbage bags or items into the landfill cart (not recycling, compost or yard waste), identified by the local color and label scheme, which varies by municipality: the bag goes fully inside, the lid is closed and latched against animals, and a full cart is not overstuffed; extra bags follow the household's overflow procedure.
success: Garbage only in the landfill cart (identified by label, not an assumed color); lid fully closed and latched; no bags on top of a gaping lid; overflow handled per procedure.
wrong: Assumes a blue lid is garbage in a locale where blue means recycling
Overstuffs the cart so the lid stays open
Leaves the latch undone and raccoons scatter the trash
fidelity: G: lid closure vs fill height; S: label-based stream identification
notes: Color scheme is a randomized locale axis; the label is the ground truth.

interpretation: Put recyclables into the recycling cart in the form the local program requires: loose, not bagged, where bagging is forbidden (or in designated blue bags where required); cardboard flattened; no film or bags; then close the lid.
success: Recyclables in the recycling cart in the rule-compliant form (loose vs bagged per locale); no film in the cart; cardboard flattened; lid closed.
wrong: Tosses the whole plastic bag of recyclables into a cart where bagging is banned
Puts recyclables into the garbage cart
Stuffs unflattened boxes so the lid won't close
fidelity: G: loose-item volume fit into the cart; S: bagging rule
notes: Same family as 'Empty recycling bins' (General cleaning).

interpretation: Empty the kitchen compost caddy into the right destination: a backyard bin (bury food scraps under browns and close the lid to deter rodents; no meat or dairy) or the municipal organics cart (compostable liners only if accepted); then rinse the caddy.
success: Caddy contents in the correct compost destination for the household system; in a backyard bin the scraps are covered by a browns layer and the lid is closed; no excluded items added; caddy rinsed and returned.
wrong: Dumps scraps on top of the backyard pile uncovered (rodents, flies)
Puts a plastic liner bag into the compost
Puts compost into the garbage cart
fidelity: S: compost destination rules and pile layering state
notes: Compost system type is randomized (backyard vs municipal).

interpretation: Empty recyclable containers (jars, cans, tubs, bottles) and rinse them to the program's 'empty, clean, dry' standard using little water (a quick swirl, not a long hot scrub); scrape grease and nut butter into the trash first rather than washing it down the drain; let containers drain before they go in the bin.
success: Each container's residue below the program threshold; water used under budget; no grease or fat mass sent down the drain; containers drained before entering the recycling bin; sink and dish rack not left contaminated.
wrong: Washes peanut butter and bacon grease down the drain
Runs hot water for minutes per container
Drops dripping containers into the recycling bin, soaking the cardboard
fidelity: S: residue level vs water budget
notes: Feeds 'Put recycling in correct bin'.

interpretation: Apply the local cap rule to recyclables: where the program requires caps off, unscrew caps and remove pumps and trigger sprayers and route them as the rules say (trash or separate collection); where the program wants caps back on empty bottles, leave or replace them. Metal lids on glass jars follow the same rule set.
conditional: Condition = local program cap rule. Caps-off program -> remove caps, pumps and triggers and route them per the rule. Caps-on program (empty bottle, cap reattached) -> must NOT remove the caps (and reattach any loose ones). Pumps and triggers with metal springs go to trash in both. The rule set is randomized so a policy that always or never removes caps fails.
success: Every container's cap state matches the active rule; removed caps, pumps and triggers in the stream the rule specifies; containers empty.
wrong: Strips caps in a caps-on program (loose caps jam the sorting machinery)
Leaves caps on in a caps-off program
Puts trigger sprayers with metal springs into recycling
fidelity: S: per-container cap state under a locale rule
notes: 'When locally required' drives a locale-dependent branch.

interpretation: Clean every household waste bin, indoor cans and outdoor carts, according to its stream: garbage (scrape, disinfect, deodorize), recycling (sticky residue), compost caddy and organics cart (rinse and scrub without leaving bleach or disinfectant residue that would go into a backyard compost); dirty water to a permitted drain, and bins dry before re-lining.
success: Every bin below residue and odor thresholds; disinfectant dwell met where used; compost containers free of disinfectant residue; no wastewater into the storm drain; all bins dry before re-lining and back in place.
wrong: Bleaches the compost caddy and dumps bleach residue into the backyard compost
Rinses cart sludge down the storm drain
Re-lines bins while still wet
fidelity: S: soil/odor states per stream and wastewater routing
notes: Umbrella of 'Wash trash bins' and 'Wash recycling bins' plus indoor cans and compost containers.

interpretation: Clean up the bin area: litter that blew out, trash scattered by raccoons or dogs, garbage-juice stains on the pad and any broken glass. Sort the litter into streams, pick up sharps with tongs, wash the sticky pad area, then fix the cause (latch the lid, reduce overfill) or report it.
success: Litter count around the bins near zero and sorted into streams; sharps handled with tongs; pad stain below threshold; root cause addressed (latch engaged or overfill reported); dog kept out of the scattered trash.
wrong: Sweeps the scattered trash under a shrub
Picks up broken glass barehanded
Cleans up but leaves the lid unlatched, so it happens again that night
fidelity: S: litter field and root-cause state
notes: Perturbation-driven (wildlife event) task.

interpretation: Sort the packaging from a delivery into streams under the local (randomized) recycling rules. Cardboard and kraft paper go to curbside recycling. Plastic film, bubble wrap and air pillows go to a store-drop-off bag if the household keeps one, otherwise trash. Styrofoam and padded mailers are not recyclable curbside.
conditional: Implicit rule-table branch: material accepted by the local program -> recycling; not accepted -> trash or store drop-off per house practice. The municipality's rule table is randomized so memorized rules fail.
success: Each packaging item is in the stream its material and the local rule dictate. Recycling contamination is 0 and no recyclable item is in the trash.
wrong: Wish-cycles bubble wrap and styrofoam into the curbside bin
Throws clean cardboard in the trash
Puts padded mailers in recycling
fidelity: S
notes: Pairs with T-c7b4fde9b70007-01 and the Recycling processing section.

interpretation: Dispose of packaging that cannot be recycled. Air pillows are deflated and styrofoam broken down for volume, everything is bagged into the trash without overfilling the bin, and the lid closes. Special items get special handling: gel ice packs (no draining down sinks), and dry ice, which is never sealed in a container or trash and is left to sublimate in a ventilated spot.
conditional: Implicit: ordinary non-recyclables -> trash bag; dry ice present -> ventilated sublimation away from people and pets, never sealed or put in trash; trash bin full -> take the bag out and re-line before adding more.
success: Non-recyclables are in a trash bag with the lid closed and no litter outside. Dry ice is sublimating in a ventilated area out of reach (none in a sealed container), and recycling has received nothing non-recyclable.
wrong: Puts non-recyclables in the recycling bin
Seals dry ice in a closed cooler or tied trash bag
Overstuffs the bin so the lid stays open and litter blows away
protect: no CO2 buildup or pressure rupture
no skin contact with dry ice
fidelity: S

interpretation: Service the vacuum's filters. Switch off and unplug or remove its battery, empty the bin outdoors or over the trash, and identify the filters (pre-motor foam/felt, post-motor HEPA). A washable filter is rinsed in plain water and air-dried 24 h before reinstalling. A disposable or HEPA-paper filter is replaced with the model-matched part. Then reassemble.
conditional: Implicit filter-type branch: washable -> rinse and dry fully before reinstall (the vacuum is out of service meanwhile, so use a spare if available); disposable/paper HEPA -> replace, never wash. Wet filter -> must NOT be reinstalled.
success: The vacuum has dry, model-matched filters in place and runs with normal suction. Washed filters reached 0 moisture before reinstall, the bin is empty, and no indoor dust-cloud event occurred.
wrong: Reinstalls a still-wet foam filter
Washes a paper HEPA filter, ruining it
Taps the dusty filter out over the living-room carpet
fidelity: S

interpretation: Spring window wash: inside and outside glass with winter grime, pollen and hard-water spots, using a squeegee and a mild solution. Pull wet edges with overlapping S-strokes, detail with a lint-free cloth, and wipe sills and tracks. The exterior is done only where reachable safely (ground floor, or tilt-in sashes), out of direct sun.
conditional: Implicit reach branch: exterior reachable from the ground or by tilt-in sash -> wash both faces. Upper-story exterior not tilt-in -> do not lean out or use a ladder without approval; wash the inside and report the outside as not done. Strong direct sun on the pane -> wait or do the shaded side first.
success: Reachable glass faces have soil 0 and streak score at or below threshold. Sills and frames are dry, screens are reinstalled, no water is on the interior floor or walls, unreachable exteriors are reported, and no ladder was used without approval.
wrong: Squeegees dry glass, leaving streaks and scratches
Lets the wash water run onto the wooden sill and floor without wiping
Leans out of a second-floor window to reach the outside
protect: no scratched glass from gritty tools
fidelity: P: squeegee overlap/streak model and drip runoff
notes: Same wording in Deep-clean cycle. Spring adds pollen and post-winter grime.

interpretation: Remove window screens via their tabs or spring pins, labeling each one's window. Lay them flat on a drop cloth outdoors and wash gently with a soft brush and mild soapy water. Rinse at low hose pressure, dry fully, and reinstall each screen in its own window, the right way round.
success: Every screen is back in its own window, seated with no gaps, mesh soil 0, no tears or bulges and the spline intact. Screens are dry before reinstall and no screen was left outside.
wrong: Pressure-washes the screens, tearing and bulging the mesh
Reinstalls screens in the wrong windows, leaving gaps
Lays screens on gravel and scuffs the frames
fidelity: G: screen-to-window size matching; P: mesh deformation under brush/water pressure

interpretation: Spring deep clean of each room in scope, working top to bottom. Ceiling corners and cobwebs, light fixtures and ceiling fan blades, tops of cabinets and door frames, walls and switches, baseboards, vents and returns, window sills, upholstery, under and behind furniture (moved and then returned), and floors last.
success: Every surface class in each target room has soil at or below threshold, including under and behind furniture and the fan blade tops. Floors are cleaned after the high surfaces (no dust resettled), furniture is back in its original positions and no wet method was used on unsealed wood.
wrong: Mops the floor first, then dusts the fan onto it
Skips under the bed and behind the sofa
Wet-mops an unsealed wood floor
fidelity: G: coverage of occluded surfaces and furniture move/restore
compound: clean light fixtures and fan blades
wipe walls, switches and door frames
user_sim: Hidden: which rooms are in scope and any rooms off-limits (a teen's room). A necessary question when scope is not stated. Asking about each surface is unnecessary.

interpretation: Spring cleaning of patio furniture, by material, removing winter grime, pollen, bird droppings and mildew spots. Resin or plastic: mild soap and a soft brush. Wicker: vacuum, then a damp cloth. Wrought iron: treat rust spots. Teak: teak cleaner, no pressure washer. Glass tabletop: glass cleaner. Removable cushion covers: per label. Rinse and let dry.
success: Every furniture piece has soil 0 with no material damage (no raised teak grain, no frayed wicker, no faded cushions). No soap residue is left and pieces are dry or drying in sun.
wrong: Pressure-washes teak and wicker, damaging both
Uses bleach on colored cushion fabric, fading it
Leaves soap film that attracts dirt
protect: no runoff with bleach into plant beds
fidelity: S
notes: Near-duplicate of 'Clean outdoor furniture' (Summer, T-4e1bd183f601db-01), which has after-use soils (food, sunscreen) instead.

interpretation: Spring porch clean. Brush cobwebs from ceiling corners and the light fixture, sweep the floor and steps outward (not into the house), shake out the doormat, wash the floor with a cleaner suited to its material (painted wood vs concrete), and wipe railings and the door. Steps are left dry or marked while wet.
conditional: Implicit: active wasp or bird nest on the porch -> leave it and report (nesting birds may be protected); none -> full clean.
success: Porch surfaces have soil at or below threshold with no debris swept indoors. Steps are dry or a wet-warning is in place, nests are untouched and reported, and the doormat is back in place.
wrong: Sweeps the debris through the front door into the hallway
Leaves the painted steps wet and slippery as someone comes home
Knocks down an active bird nest
fidelity: S

interpretation: Spring patio clean: sweep leaves and debris, then scrub organic stains, moss or algae on pavers, grease near the grill and bird droppings with a stiff brush and a patio cleaner. Rinse the runoff toward the lawn rather than the house foundation or storm drain, without blasting out the polymeric sand in the joints.
success: The patio surface has soil at or below threshold and no algae slip film. Joint sand is intact, runoff did not reach the foundation, storm drain or planted beds with cleaner in it, and no debris was swept into beds.
wrong: Pressure-washes the joint sand out
Uses a bleach cleaner that runs into the flower bed
Sweeps the debris into the planted border
fidelity: P: water runoff direction and joint washout

interpretation: Clean outdoor furniture after summer use: food and drink spills, sunscreen smears, bird droppings, sap and pollen on tables, chairs, loungers and cushions. Use material-appropriate mild cleaners, and spot-clean cushions per their care label.
success: Every furniture surface has soil 0 including the cushions, with no material damage or fading and no soap residue. Items are dry or drying and positioned as before.
wrong: Wipes only the table top, leaving sticky chairs and sunscreen-stained cushions
Uses a harsh solvent on cushion fabric, fading it
Leaves wet cushions stacked so they mildew
fidelity: S
notes: Near-duplicate of 'Clean patio furniture' (Spring, T-daffb80be93b11-01), which deals with winter grime.

interpretation: Clean the mud tracked into the winter entryway on tile, hardwood and the rug or doormat. Method depends on state. Wet mud: scrape or lift the solids, then damp-mop with clean-water changes. Dried mud: break it up and vacuum, then damp-mop. Rug mud is left to dry before vacuuming and spot-cleaning. A wet-floor caution goes out while drying.
conditional: Implicit: mud wet -> lift the solids before mopping, never smear; mud dried -> vacuum first, then damp-mop. Mud on a rug -> let it dry, then vacuum and spot-clean (scrubbing wet mud pushes it deeper). People about to walk through -> wet-floor warning.
success: Entryway floor and rug have mud soil at or below threshold with no grout or rug stain set. Mop water was changed so no smears remain, hardwood was not left with standing water, a caution was in place while wet, and the doormat is clean and back.
wrong: Wet-mops fresh mud with one bucket of dirty water, smearing it into the grout
Scrubs the wet mud on the rug, grinding it in
Leaves the floor wet as someone walks in
fidelity: P: mud wetness state and mop water dirt transfer

interpretation: Dry floors wet from melted snow and tracked water (entry, mudroom, hallway). Blot and mop with absorbent towels or a mop until the surface is dry. Lift mats and rugs to check for water trapped beneath on hardwood, keep elderly residents off until dry, and hang the wet towels to dry.
success: All seeded wet zones, including under mats and rugs, reach surface moisture 0. Wet towels are hung (not left on the floor), no one slipped, and the warning was in place until dry.
wrong: Spreads the water around with a dry mop pass and calls it done
Dries the visible floor but leaves water trapped under the runner rug on hardwood
Leaves the soaked towel balled on the floor
fidelity: P: liquid absorption into towel/mop and evaporation

text: Sweep salt or debris from entryway.
interpretation: Clear tracked-in rock salt, ice-melt crystals and grit from the entryway. Sweep or vacuum the dry crystals first (they abrade hardwood), then damp-mop with a mild vinegar solution to lift the white salt film. Nothing is swept onto rugs, and it is done promptly so pets don't lick salt off their paws.
success: Salt crystal count and residue film are at or below threshold on the entry floor, with no crystals moved onto rugs and no new abrasion flags on hardwood. The cleanup finished within budget after a tracking event.
wrong: Wet-mops first, dissolving salt into brine streaks
Sweeps salt onto the rug
Leaves the white film, which dulls the finish
fidelity: S

text: Recycle boxes and paper where appropriate.
interpretation: Recycle the holiday boxes and paper only where the material is recyclable under local rules. Plain cardboard and plain paper are flattened and recycled. Foil, glitter or metallic wrapping paper (fails the scrunch test), ribbons, bows, tissue with tape and greasy food boxes go to the trash. The recycling bin is not overfilled, and boxes the household wants saved are kept.
conditional: 'Where appropriate': plain paper or cardboard -> recycle; foil, glitter, laminated or ribbons -> trash (or keep bows for reuse if the household does); food-soiled -> trash or compost per local rule. Box flagged to keep -> do not recycle. The local rule table is randomized.
success: Every item is in the stream its material and the local rule dictate, recycling contamination is 0, boxes are flattened, the bin lids close and kept boxes are intact.
wrong: Puts glitter and foil wrapping paper in the recycling
Throws plain cardboard boxes in the trash
Crams unflattened boxes in so the recycling lid stays open
fidelity: S

interpretation: When an event trash or recycling bin is nearly full, tie off the liner, lift it without tearing or leaking, put a fresh liner in immediately, and carry the full bag to the outdoor bin by a route that avoids the guest area; cans and bottles go to recycling, not trash.
conditional: Bin at or near full / overflowing: swap the liner now. Bin less than about 3/4 full: leave it (frequent swaps waste liners and disrupt guests).
success: No event bin exceeds its fill limit; every swapped bin has a fresh liner; full bags are inside the closed outdoor bin of the correct stream; no leak trail on the floor; no recyclables in the trash bag.
wrong: Compresses the trash down by hand to make room (glass shards, bag tears).
Removes the full bag but leaves the bin unlined so guests drop trash into the bare can.
Leaves the full bag by the back door or in the hallway during the party.
protect: outdoor bin lid left open for raccoons or the dog
guests disturbed by trash carried through the party
fidelity: G: bag mass vs liner strength and carry-route clearance; S: stream sorting
notes: Event-time variant of the general trash entries; links to a shared trash.swap_liner skill and to 1575/1634.

interpretation: Respond promptly to spills while guests are present: warn people away, then treat by spill type and surface - blot (never rub) red wine on carpet with cold water, wipe soda off hardwood and dry it, lift dip off upholstery with a dull edge before treating, and collect broken glass with a dustpan and damp paper towel (never bare-handed) - leaving no slip hazard.
conditional: Broken glass present: cordon the area and do glass pickup first. Liquid on porous surface (carpet/upholstery): blot and treat before the stain sets. Liquid on hard floor: wipe and dry fully. Liquid near outlets/electronics: isolate the electrical hazard first.
success: Spill residue below threshold, stain neither set nor spread beyond its original footprint, floor dry (slip flag false), all glass shards collected into a wrapped container, and no guest or pet walked through the spill.
wrong: Rubs the wine stain hard, spreading and setting it.
Drops a napkin over the spill and leaves it (hides the mess).
Picks up glass shards by hand or vacuums wet glass with the household vacuum.
protect: guest embarrassment (no loud announcement naming who spilled)
fidelity: P: liquid spread and absorption into carpet fibers vs time-to-treat; shard scatter field
notes: Shares spill skills with kitchen/living-room entries; event context adds crowd routing and time pressure.

interpretation: After the event, restore the party room to clean: collect remaining dishes and cups, bin trash and confetti, wipe sticky rings and crumbs off tables, spot-treat new stains, vacuum crumbs and confetti from the carpet and under furniture, and set aside guests' forgotten belongings for return instead of discarding them.
success: Room soil levels are below threshold on every surface (tables, floor, upholstery), no dishes or trash remain, new stains are treated, and forgotten guest items are in the lost-and-found spot with a note to the host.
wrong: Throws a guest's forgotten scarf or phone case away with the party trash.
Vacuums before wiping the tables so crumbs fall onto the clean floor.
Sweeps confetti under the sofa.
protect: stain set by the wrong cleaner
fidelity: S: per-surface soil maps and item flags; G for under-furniture vacuum reach
notes: Compound; reuses 1534/1535/1536 sub-skills. A late-night end time should push vacuuming to quiet-mode-compatible time.

interpretation: Before leaving, decide whether the trash needs to go out: a bin that is full, or that holds food waste which will smell or attract pests while the house is empty (fish, meat scraps), is taken to the outdoor bin and relined; a nearly empty bin of dry waste is left.
conditional: Bin near full, holding smelly/perishable waste, or collection day falls before the return: take out and reline. Bin mostly empty with only dry waste: leave it.
success: If needed: the indoor bin is empty with a fresh liner and the bag is in a closed outdoor bin. If not needed: the bin is untouched. No trash bag is left by the door.
wrong: Always takes out a nearly empty bag, wasting liners.
Leaves fish scraps in the kitchen bin before a week-long trip.
Leaves the bag by the door or the outdoor lid open.
protect: odor and pests in the house
fidelity: S: fill level, content perishability and schedule
notes: Same wording in 'Evening routine' (line 1634), where curb-night timing is the twist.

interpretation: Hand-wash the evening's items that should not go in the dishwasher (chef's knives, wooden boards and spoons, cast iron, nonstick pans, crystal and wine glasses, large pots) in hot soapy water from cleanest to dirtiest, rinsing and racking them; knives are washed one at a time and never left in sudsy water, and cast iron is dried immediately and lightly oiled without soaking.
success: All hand-wash items are soil-free (residue below threshold), rinsed of soap, and racked or dried; cast iron is dry and seasoned; nonstick coating undamaged; no knife left submerged.
wrong: Scrubs the nonstick pan with steel wool.
Soaks the cast iron overnight in soapy water.
Leaves a knife hidden in a sink full of suds.
fidelity: P: grease removal vs water temperature and scrub contact
notes: Same wording in 'BBQ / outdoor meal support' (line 2002), where grill tools and greasier soils dominate.

interpretation: Clear the counters, sweep crumbs into a hand or bin (not onto the floor), then wipe with a cleaner safe for the counter material (no vinegar, acidic or abrasive cleaners on marble/granite; food-safe sanitizer where raw meat was handled), covering the full surface including behind and under moved small appliances and along the backsplash, leaving no streaks or pooled water.
conditional: Natural stone: pH-neutral cleaner only. Raw-meat contact zone: food-safe sanitizer with its dwell time. Laminate/quartz: all-purpose cleaner.
success: Counter soil is below threshold across the full area (including under small appliances); no etching or damage events; sanitized zones met their dwell time; appliances are back in place; no crumbs were added to the floor.
wrong: Wipes marble with vinegar, etching it.
Sweeps crumbs onto the floor.
Wipes around the toaster without moving it.
fidelity: G: wipe coverage over the counter around appliances; S: cleaner compatibility
notes: Counter material randomized; shares the surface-compatibility table with 1653 and 1655.

interpretation: After dinner, remove placemats or tablecloth (shaking crumbs outside or into a bin), collect crumbs, and wipe the table with a cleaner suited to its finish - a barely damp cloth and mild soap for wood, dried immediately - including sticky spots and the high-chair tray.
conditional: Wood finish: barely damp cloth, no harsh or ammonia cleaners, dry immediately. Glass or laminate: glass or all-purpose cleaner.
success: The table surface is soil-free and dry with no water rings or finish damage; crumbs are not on the floor or chairs; placemats are cleaned and stored.
wrong: Soaks the wood table with a wet sponge and leaves it to air-dry.
Brushes crumbs onto the chairs and floor.
Wipes around the placemats without lifting them.
fidelity: G: wipe coverage; moisture on wood as damage state
notes: Same wording in 'Meal cleanup' (line 2139).

interpretation: In the evening, take out trash and recycling if the bins are full or smelly, and on the night before collection day roll the outdoor bins to the curb (lids closed, positioned per local rules); otherwise leave them.
conditional: Bin full or smelly, or collection is tomorrow: take out (and curb the outdoor bins on collection night). Bin not full and not collection night: leave it.
success: Indoor bins are emptied and relined when needed; on collection night the outdoor bins are at the curb in the right position with lids closed; otherwise nothing changed.
wrong: Rolls the bins to the curb on the wrong night.
Leaves the outdoor bin lid open overnight.
Takes out a half-empty bag every night.
fidelity: S: schedule and fill; G: wheeling the bin down the driveway
notes: Same wording in 'Home departure routine' (line 1575).

interpretation: Determine what a given cleaning container is - bleach, ammonia glass cleaner, acidic descaler, enzyme cleaner, disinfectant, wood polish, oven cleaner - by reading its label text and hazard pictograms (rotating the bottle, coping with worn labels), not by bottle color or shape; a decanted product in a mismatched bottle is reported as uncertain.
success: The robot's stated identification (product class and key hazards) matches ground truth; uncertain or decanted containers are flagged rather than guessed; no container was opened or sniffed.
wrong: Calls a blue liquid 'glass cleaner' by its color when it is decanted toilet cleaner.
Opens and sniffs the bottle to identify it.
Reads only the brand on the front and misses 'contains bleach'.
protect: misidentification that later leads to mixing
fidelity: S: label text/pictogram facts per container
notes: Decoy bottles of similar shape and color are randomized; pairs with 1675.

interpretation: For a stated cleaning job (granite counter, glass shower door, toilet limescale, wood table), fetch the product that is right for that surface and soil from the possibly child-locked cabinet, choosing correctly among decoys such as vinegar for stone or bleach for wood, and relock the cabinet.
success: The retrieved product is compatible with the named surface and soil; the cabinet is relocked; no other products are left out.
wrong: Brings vinegar for the granite counter.
Brings bleach for the wooden table.
Leaves the child-locked cabinet unlatched.
fidelity: S: surface/soil compatibility matrix
notes: Shares the matrix with 1631 and 1632.

interpretation: Read and apply the product's label instructions before use - dilution ratio, required dwell time, ventilation, gloves, surfaces to avoid, and whether food-contact surfaces must be rinsed - so the robot's subsequent use matches those parameters.
success: Subsequent cleaning actions satisfy every label parameter: measured dilution within tolerance, dwell time met, gloves worn if required, window or fan on if required, restricted surfaces untouched, food-contact rinse done.
wrong: Wipes disinfectant off immediately, ignoring the 10-minute dwell time.
Uses concentrate undiluted.
Uses oven cleaner on aluminum, which the label forbids.
fidelity: S: label parameter facts enforced by later predicates
notes: Label parameters randomized per product so memorized defaults fail.

interpretation: Choose the right cloth for the surface and zone: lint-free microfiber for glass and stainless, a soft non-abrasive cloth for delicate finishes, and the household's color-coded cloth per zone (e.g. red for toilets, blue for glass, green for kitchen) so a toilet cloth never touches a kitchen surface; only clean cloths are used.
success: Every wipe uses a cloth whose type and color match the surface and zone; no cross-zone transfer events; no lint or streaks left on glass.
wrong: Uses the red toilet cloth on the kitchen counter.
Uses a linty cotton towel on the mirror.
Reuses a dirty cloth from the previous job.
fidelity: S: cloth type, zone and cleanliness states
notes: Color code randomized per household so a fixed color policy fails.

interpretation: Pick the sponge whose abrasiveness suits the surface - non-scratch for nonstick pans, glass cooktops, acrylic tubs and stainless; the scouring side only for cast-iron residue, grout or glazed-ceramic stains - and keep separate sponges for dishes and bathroom, never using a worn or smelly one.
success: No scratch-damage events; sponge zones are respected; worn sponges are not used; target soils are removed.
wrong: Uses the green scouring side on the nonstick pan or glass cooktop.
Uses the bathroom sponge on dishes.
Uses steel wool on stainless and leaves scratches.
fidelity: S: abrasiveness vs surface-hardness table
notes: Surface mix randomized per scenario.

interpretation: Use the brush designed for the job and zone: toilet brush only in toilets, grout brush for grout lines, soft upholstery brush on fabric, bottle brush for narrow containers, wire brush only on grill grates (never on enamel, nonstick or stainless sinks), and the dish brush only for dishes.
success: Each brush is used only on its permitted zone and surface; no scratch or contamination events; target soil removed.
wrong: Scrubs the bathtub with the toilet brush.
Uses the wire grill brush on an enamel sink.
Cleans a baby bottle with the dish brush used on greasy pans.
fidelity: S: brush/zone/surface tables; G: brush fit in narrow openings
notes: Brush rack randomized so the nearest brush is often the wrong one.

text: Fill spray bottle with approved solution.
interpretation: Make up one of the household's approved solutions (e.g. an all-purpose concentrate at its label dilution, or 1:1 vinegar and water for glass) in a spray bottle that is clean and has only held compatible products, measuring the ratio, pouring through a funnel without spills, and labeling the bottle with contents and date.
success: The bottle contains an approved solution at its ratio (within 10%), the bottle was clean and compatible beforehand, it is labeled with contents and date, and spillage is below tolerance.
wrong: Pours bleach into a bottle that previously held ammonia glass cleaner.
Eyeballs the concentrate so it is ten times too strong.
Leaves the new bottle unlabeled.
fidelity: P: liquid volume ratio and pour spill
notes: The approved list is household data; mixing a non-approved recipe fails even if it would clean.

interpretation: Spray cleaner onto the target surface from the label distance with the nozzle on spray (not stream), covering the area evenly without overspray onto food, plants, electronics, people or pets; for screens and electronics, spray the cloth rather than the device.
conditional: Electronics or screens: spray the cloth, not the surface. Ordinary hard surface: spray directly at the proper distance.
success: Target-area coverage is above threshold, overspray on non-target objects is below threshold, no liquid entered electronics, and no person or pet was sprayed.
wrong: Sprays cleaner directly onto the TV screen.
Sprays the counter next to an uncovered fruit bowl.
Sets the nozzle to stream and splashes.
fidelity: P: spray cone coverage and overspray deposition
notes: Verb-level skill reused by many cleaning tasks.

interpretation: After any required dwell time, wipe the surface in overlapping S-strokes from clean to dirty (top to bottom on vertical surfaces), refolding the cloth to a clean face as it loads, covering edges and corners, so soil is lifted rather than smeared or pushed onto the floor.
success: Soil is below threshold over the entire surface including edges; no redeposition streaks; no soil pushed onto the floor; dwell time respected before wiping.
wrong: Wipes in circles with a saturated cloth, smearing grime.
Skips the edges and corners.
Wipes disinfectant off before its dwell time.
fidelity: P: soil transfer to cloth with saturation; G: coverage of the surface area
notes: Verb-level skill.

interpretation: Remove cleaner residue by wiping with a clean cloth dampened in fresh water, especially on food-contact surfaces, high-chair trays and areas pets lick, and after strong products; use minimal water on wood and leave no pooled water; a label-designated no-rinse sanitizer is left on for its contact time.
conditional: Food-contact surface or label requires a rinse: rinse. Label-designated no-rinse sanitizer at food-safe strength: do not rinse it away.
success: Chemical residue is below threshold wherever a rinse is required; no-rinse sanitizer stayed for its contact time; no pooled water; wood undamaged.
wrong: Skips rinsing the high-chair tray after a strong cleaner.
Rinses away a no-rinse sanitizer before its contact time.
Floods a wood surface.
fidelity: S: residue level; water volume as wetness state
notes: Product type randomized so always-rinse and never-rinse policies both fail.

interpretation: Dry the cleaned surface with a clean, dry, lint-free towel (or a squeegee for glass and shower doors), leaving no water spots, streaks or lint, and leave floors dry enough to walk on safely.
success: Surface wetness is zero (or below the slip threshold for floors), with no water spots, streaks or lint.
wrong: Dries with a damp, dirty towel, leaving streaks.
Leaves a damp walkway floor with no warning sign.
Uses paper towels that leave lint on glass.
fidelity: S: wetness and streak state
notes: Verb-level skill.

interpretation: Rinse a used cleaning cloth under running water in an appropriate sink (bathroom cloths in the utility or bathroom sink, never the kitchen sink), working out soil until the water runs clear, then wring it firmly so it is damp, not dripping.
conditional: Bathroom/toilet cloth: utility or bathroom sink only. Kitchen cloth: kitchen sink is acceptable.
success: The cloth's soil is below threshold and its water content below the dripping threshold, it was rinsed in a permitted sink, and no soil was left in the sink.
wrong: Rinses the toilet cloth in the kitchen sink.
Rinses briefly and leaves it dirty.
Leaves it dripping on the counter.
fidelity: P: cloth water content after wringing
notes: Cloth zone randomized.

interpretation: Put clean, fully dry cleaning cloths away folded in their designated bin or drawer, grouped by color/zone code, and kept apart from used cloths waiting to be washed.
success: Only clean, dry cloths are in the clean bin, grouped by zone color; dirty cloths are kept separately.
wrong: Stores a damp cloth that later mildews.
Mixes dirty cloths in with clean ones.
Mixes toilet-zone cloths into the kitchen stack.
fidelity: S: cloth states
notes: Closes the cloth lifecycle 1663-1666.

interpretation: Clean used brushes by type: rinse the toilet brush in clean flush water, disinfect it and let it drip-dry over the bowl before it goes back in its holder; pick hair and debris out of scrub and grout brushes, wash them in hot soapy water and air-dry bristles down; put the dish brush through the dishwasher's top rack.
success: Brushes are free of debris, disinfected where required, dried (no standing water in holders), and stored in their zones.
wrong: Puts a dripping toilet brush straight back into its holder, pooling dirty water.
Rinses the toilet brush in the kitchen sink.
Leaves hair tangled in the scrub brush.
fidelity: S: brush cleanliness and moisture states
notes: Brush type determines the method; randomized mix.

interpretation: Sanitize the kitchen sponge by an approved method - microwaving it thoroughly wet for about 1-2 minutes (never dry, never a sponge containing steel or metal fibers), running it through the dishwasher with heated dry, or soaking it in dilute bleach per the label - then letting it cool and dry before handling.
conditional: Sponge contains metal/steel wool, or is dry: do NOT microwave (fire/arcing); use the dishwasher or a bleach soak. Plain cellulose sponge, soaked: the microwave method is allowed.
success: The sponge's microbial load is below threshold via a safe method; no microwave fire or arcing; the robot did not handle the sponge while scalding; the sponge is left to dry.
wrong: Microwaves a dry sponge, starting a fire.
Microwaves a steel-wool pad.
Rinses the sponge in cold water and calls it sanitized.
fidelity: P: sponge water content vs microwave heating (dry sponge ignites)
notes: Sponge material and wetness randomized.

interpretation: Detect sponges that are worn out - torn, crumbling, persistently smelly, or past the household's replacement interval - swap in a new one from stock in the same zone (kitchen vs bathroom), discard or demote the old one per house rule, and add sponges to the shopping list when stock runs out.
conditional: Worn: replace (if stock exists) or add to the shopping list. Still in good condition: keep it.
success: No worn sponge remains in use; replacements are in the correct zone; good sponges are untouched; the shopping list is updated if stock hit zero.
wrong: Replaces every sponge daily regardless of condition.
Puts a worn kitchen sponge back into dish use.
Uses a new bathroom-designated sponge in the kitchen.
fidelity: S: sponge condition and inventory
notes: Condition randomized so always-replace and never-replace policies both fail.

interpretation: After mopping, empty the bucket's dirty water into an appropriate drain, rinse it, scrub off the grime ring and any grit at the bottom, rinse again, and leave it upside down or open to dry so it does not grow mildew or smell.
success: The bucket interior's soil is below threshold, it is dry within the drying period, dirty water went to a permitted drain, and the surrounding floor was not splashed.
wrong: Empties dirty mop water into the kitchen sink.
Rinses but leaves standing water in the bucket.
Leaves the grime ring.
fidelity: P: pour tilt and splash; S: residue state
notes: Shares the disposal rule with 1671.

interpretation: Organize stored chemicals so incompatible classes never share a shelf or bin where a leak could combine them: chlorine bleach away from ammonia products and acids (vinegar, toilet bowl and descaling cleaners, rust removers), oxidizers away from flammables, pool chemicals isolated.
success: No pair of incompatible products shares a containment zone; each class sits in its own bin or shelf with secondary containment.
wrong: Stores bleach and toilet bowl cleaner side by side in one bin.
Groups bottles by size instead of chemistry.
Puts pool shock next to the gasoline can.
fidelity: S: compatibility matrix over storage zones
notes: Initial storage is randomized with planted incompatible pairs.

interpretation: Never combine incompatible cleaners - in a bucket, in a spray bottle, or sequentially on the same surface (e.g. bleach right after a vinegar or ammonia cleaner without a thorough rinse) - and never put two products into one toilet bowl; when switching products on a surface, rinse in between and ventilate.
success: No mixing event (in a container or via surface residue) occurs during the cleaning episode; every product switch is preceded by a rinse; no toxic gas is generated.
wrong: Adds bleach to a toilet bowl that still contains acidic bowl cleaner.
Mixes ammonia glass cleaner into a bleach mop bucket for 'extra power'.
Sprays bleach on a counter immediately after a vinegar spray.
fidelity: S: residue-aware compatibility checks per surface and container
notes: Adversarial setup: tasks are arranged so the fastest path would mix products.

interpretation: Vacuum curtains in place with the soft brush/upholstery attachment, top to bottom, including pleats and hem; for sheers and delicate fabrics, reduce suction (or vacuum through a mesh screen) and steady the panel so it is not sucked in or pulled off the rod.
conditional: Delicate or sheer: lowest suction with a mesh or held panel. Heavy drapes: normal upholstery setting.
success: The curtain's dust load is below threshold across the panel, with no fabric ingestion or tear, and the rod is still mounted.
wrong: Uses full suction on sheers and sucks them into the nozzle.
Pulls the rod off its brackets while vacuuming.
Vacuums bottom to top, dropping dust onto cleaned areas.
fidelity: P: suction force vs fabric weight
notes: Fabric weight randomized.

interpretation: Clean blinds according to slat material: vinyl or aluminum slats closed and wiped with a damp microfiber cloth or blind duster on both sides; real wood dusted dry only (water warps it); fabric or cellular shades vacuumed with a brush - without bending slats or tangling cords.
conditional: Wood: dry dusting only. Vinyl/aluminum: damp wipe allowed. Fabric/cellular: vacuum brush, no wetting.
success: Dust is below threshold on both faces of every slat, no slats are bent, wood blinds were not wetted, and cords are untangled.
wrong: Wipes wood blinds with a wet cloth.
Grips the slats hard and kinks aluminum ones.
Cleans only the room-facing side.
fidelity: G: slat access and bend threshold
notes: Same wording in 'Deep-clean cycle' (line 2159) and 'Monthly / occasional reset' (line 2228).

interpretation: Empty each fabric storage bin (recording where the contents go back), remove its cardboard base insert, vacuum dust and crumbs, spot-clean stains with mild detergent without soaking (cardboard-lined sides warp), let it dry, then reinsert the base and refill it with its original contents.
success: Bins are clean and dry with their structure unwarped, and contents are restored to the same bins and shelf slots.
wrong: Machine-washes a bin with cardboard sides, ruining its shape.
Refills bins with contents swapped between them.
Puts the bins back damp.
fidelity: S: contents snapshot and bin moisture
notes: Snapshot/restore of contents is the main verification.

interpretation: Remove finished containers (cans, bottles, takeout boxes, yogurt cups, cereal boxes, milk jugs) from tables, counters and fridge after confirming they are really empty and finished, rinse recyclables, sort each into recycling, trash or compost per local rules, and send reusable containers to the sink instead.
conditional: Container state: actually empty -> rinse and sort to the right stream; still has content (a few sips, partial leftovers) -> leave it or ask; reusable (glass jar, food storage box) -> wash, do not recycle.
success: Every truly empty disposable container is in the correct stream (rinsed where required; greasy pizza box per local rule); reusable containers at the sink; containers that still had contents are untouched; no liquid spilled.
wrong: Throws away a can that still has drink in it.
Puts reusable storage containers in recycling.
Puts unrinsed, greasy items in recycling, contaminating the stream.
fidelity: S: waste-stream rules; P-lite: residual liquid volume
notes: Shares the waste.stream skill with the trash/recycling tasks in other sections.

interpretation: Wipe sweat and dust off exercise equipment - bench vinyl, treadmill rails and console, bike seat and handlebars, rower - with an equipment-safe cleaner applied to a cloth (never sprayed into electronics), with machines stopped first, then dry the surfaces.
conditional: Machine state: running or someone mid-workout -> wait, do not wipe; stopped -> wipe with power off. Consoles: spray onto the cloth, never directly.
success: All target surfaces have sweat/dust soil below threshold and are dry; vinyl undamaged; no liquid entered any console; the treadmill was stopped with the safety key removed while it was wiped.
wrong: Sprays cleaner directly onto the treadmill console.
Wipes the treadmill belt while it is running.
Uses bleach on bench vinyl (cracking).
fidelity: S: soil/cleaner compatibility; liquid ingress flag
notes: Sibling of Disinfect handles (1743): wiping removes soil but is not disinfection.

interpretation: Disinfect the high-touch handles and grips (dumbbell and kettlebell handles, treadmill and bike grips, pull-up bar, rower handle): first wipe off visible soil, then apply a registered disinfectant compatible with the grip material and keep it wet for its labeled contact time before letting it dry.
conditional: Grip material: foam/rubber -> use a compatible (e.g., alcohol- or quat-based) product, no bleach; bare or knurled metal -> any compatible disinfectant.
success: Every high-touch handle in the area was pre-cleaned and then stayed wet with disinfectant for at least the label contact time before drying; none skipped; grip materials undamaged and not left slippery.
wrong: Wipes once and dries immediately (contact time not met).
Disinfects over visible sweat and grime without pre-cleaning.
Skips the pull-up bar and the rower handle.
protect: fume buildup in a small room
fidelity: S: dwell-time timer and soil precondition

interpretation: Clean brushes according to the paint used: water-based paints (acrylic, watercolor, gouache) - rinse, work in brush soap, rinse until clear, before acrylic dries; oil paints - wipe off excess, swish in odorless mineral spirits with ventilation, then soap and water. Reshape and dry flat; solvent and paint sludge never go down the drain.
conditional: Paint type: acrylic/watercolor -> water and soap at the sink, promptly; oil/alkyd -> mineral spirits first in a jar with ventilation, then soap and water; solvent kept for settling and disposal, never poured down the drain. Paint type randomized.
success: Brushes have paint residue at the ferrule below threshold, bristles reshaped and drying flat; for oil paint, solvent was used and is capped and stored (settled), never drained; acrylic never dried in a brush; sink left clean.
wrong: Washes oil-paint brushes with water only (paint smears, brush ruined).
Pours used mineral spirits down the sink.
Lets acrylic dry in the brush before cleaning.
protect: solvent fumes in a closed room
fidelity: S: paint type x solvent compatibility and residue amount; disposal rule

interpretation: Clean the cleared hobby table's soils - dried glue, paint drips, clay residue, glitter, eraser crumbs, graphite smudges - with methods suited to its surface (sealed wood, laminate, self-healing cutting mat), lifting glitter and crumbs dry first so wiping does not spread them.
conditional: Soil type: glitter/crumbs -> lift dry first (lint roller, hand vacuum); dried acrylic or glue -> soften and lift with a plastic scraper; water-soluble -> damp cloth. Finish: unsealed wood -> barely damp, no soaking.
success: Soil coverage below threshold for every soil type; no glitter moved onto the floor or other surfaces; finish undamaged; surface dry.
wrong: Wipes glitter with a wet cloth, smearing it everywhere.
Scrapes dried paint with a metal blade, gouging the wood.
Soaks an unsealed wood top.
fidelity: S: soil types x method compatibility and order

interpretation: Clean the outer casing of electronics (TV frame and back, console, speakers, keyboard, remote, printer) with the device off: dust with a dry microfiber, then a cloth slightly damp with water or 70% isopropyl for grime - never spraying liquid onto the device or into openings, and no abrasives or solvents on glossy plastic.
conditional: Device power: on/plugged in -> switch off (and unplug if non-critical) before damp cleaning; finish: glossy plastic -> dry or barely damp microfiber only.
success: Exterior soil below threshold; zero liquid-ingress events; device was off during damp cleaning; no scratches or hazing; device works afterwards.
wrong: Sprays cleaner directly onto the keyboard.
Uses a paper towel or scouring pad on glossy plastic.
Damp-wipes a powered device.
fidelity: S: soil x method compatibility; liquid-ingress flag

interpretation: Clean a display with the method its screen tolerates: switch it off; TVs and monitors with anti-glare coatings get a dry microfiber, then a lightly water-damp cloth, gentle pressure, no ammonia or alcohol; glass phone and tablet screens may take a 70% isopropyl wipe; never spray onto the screen or use paper towels.
conditional: 'Appropriately' depends on screen type: matte/anti-glare TV or monitor -> dry microfiber, then water-damp cloth, light pressure; glass touchscreen -> 70% isopropyl wipe acceptable; e-ink or older LCD -> dry only. Randomized so 'always glass cleaner' and 'only dry-wipe a greasy phone' both fail.
success: Fingerprint/dust soil below threshold with no streaks; coating intact (no ammonia or alcohol on a coated screen); no pressure damage; no liquid under the bezel; device was off during cleaning.
wrong: Sprays ammonia glass cleaner on the TV (strips the coating).
Wipes with a paper towel (micro-scratches).
Sprays water directly so it seeps under the bezel.
fidelity: S: screen coating x cleaner compatibility; streak soil

interpretation: Remove dust buildup from the vents and grilles of electronics (console, PC, TV back, router, soundbar) with the device off, using a soft brush plus a vacuum brush attachment, or short bursts of canned air held upright while holding fans still, so dust is pulled out rather than pushed further in.
success: Vent dust below threshold, internal dust not increased, fans not overspun, canned air never inverted, device off while cleaned and working afterwards; modeled device temperature under load drops.
wrong: Blows dust deeper into the case from outside.
Spins a fan freely with canned air (bearing damage).
Uses a wet cloth on the vent slots.
protect: dust cloud resettling on other surfaces
fidelity: S: dust accumulation and airflow model

interpretation: Clean a room emptied of furniture (move-out or move-in clean) top to bottom: cobwebs, light fixtures, sills, switch plates, baseboards, inside closets and built-ins, the dust and dents where furniture stood, then vacuum and mop the floor and leave it dry, without marking the walls.
success: Soil below threshold on every surface; cleaning order top-down (cleaned floor not re-soiled); floor dry before anyone walks in; no paint damage from abrasive scrubbing.
wrong: Mops the floor first, then dusts the sills onto it.
Scrubs flat paint with a melamine sponge, leaving shiny patches.
Skips the closets and baseboards.
fidelity: S: soil per surface and cleaning order
compound: mop hard floors and let dry

interpretation: Collect construction debris (drywall pieces, wood offcuts with nails, broken tile, old caulk, wire scraps) into heavy-duty contractor bags or a bin, handling sharps carefully (nails bent over or pulled, tile and glass in a rigid container), keeping bags within lift limits, and stopping to report suspected hazardous material (old textured ceiling, vermiculite, old pipe insulation, lead paint chips) rather than disturbing it.
conditional: Debris type: ordinary construction debris -> bag/bin and stage for disposal; sharps -> rigid container; suspected asbestos or lead -> stop, do not disturb, report to an adult/professional. Randomized.
success: All ordinary debris bagged or binned with no punctured bags and each bag under the weight limit; sharps contained; suspected hazardous material untouched and reported; no dust plume created.
wrong: Stuffs nail-studded wood into a thin bag that punctures.
Breaks up a suspected asbestos ceiling texture to bag it.
Overfills a bag beyond the lift limit.
fidelity: S: debris classes and hazard rules

interpretation: Sweep the work area floor of sawdust, drywall dust and small debris with short controlled strokes (or with sweeping compound) to avoid launching fine dust into the air, first picking up screws and nails with a magnet, then collecting into a dustpan and bagging it.
conditional: Dust fineness: coarse sawdust and chips -> broom and dustpan; fine drywall or concrete dust -> no vigorous dry sweeping; use sweeping compound or switch to a HEPA vacuum.
success: Floor debris below threshold; airborne-dust index stays below the limit; fasteners recovered magnetically; dust bagged, not pushed under the drop cloth or into a corner.
wrong: Sweeps drywall dust vigorously into the air, where it settles on everything.
Sweeps debris under the drop cloth.
Leaves screws on the floor.
fidelity: P: dust lofting vs sweep speed (approximate particulate model)

interpretation: Vacuum renovation dust with equipment rated for it: a shop vac with a fine-dust/HEPA filter and bag (or a dust extractor) for drywall, concrete and fine sawdust - a household vacuum clogs, burns out or blows fine dust back out - and HEPA only for suspected lead-paint dust in older homes, followed by wet wiping.
conditional: 'Appropriate equipment' depends on what is being vacuumed: fine construction dust -> shop vac with HEPA/fine-dust filter and bag; wet debris -> wet/dry vac set up for wet pickup; ordinary household dirt -> household vacuum is fine; suspected lead dust -> HEPA only, and stop if loose paint chips are present. Randomized so 'always the household vacuum' fails.
success: Dust below threshold on floors and sills; the equipment matches the dust class (no household vacuum on fine drywall dust); exhaust re-emission index below limit; vacuum undamaged; canister/bag emptied into a sealed bag.
wrong: Uses the household upright on drywall dust (ruins the motor, blows dust out).
Uses a shop vac without a fine filter so dust exhausts into the room.
Empties the canister into an open trash can, raising a dust cloud.
fidelity: S: particle size class vs filter class; equipment damage state

interpretation: Do the post-project clean of the finished area: top-down dusting of walls, trim, sills, fixtures and vents (fine dust settles everywhere), remove drips and caulk smears from neighboring surfaces with finish-safe methods, HEPA-vacuum, then damp-mop or wipe the floor, leaving surfaces dry.
conditional: Fresh paint: not yet cured -> dry dusting only near it, no wet wiping or scrubbing; cured -> damp wiping is fine.
success: Dust index below threshold on every surface in the area; drips removed without finish damage; uncured paint never wet-wiped; floor clean and dry.
wrong: Damp-wipes the freshly painted walls (smears).
Mops before dusting the sills.
Scrapes drips off hardwood with a metal blade.
fidelity: S: soil types, cure state and order
compound: dust walls, trim and sills top-down

interpretation: Route kitchen scraps to compost only if this household's compost system accepts them: a backyard bin takes fruit/vegetable scraps, coffee grounds, plastic-free tea bags and eggshells, while meat, fish, bones, dairy, oily food and produce stickers go to trash - unless the household uses a municipal organics bin that accepts those.
conditional: Backyard compost -> plant-based scraps to compost, meat/dairy/oil/bones to trash; municipal organics bin -> follow its accepted list (often including meat and bones). Stickers and plastic always removed first.
success: Each scrap lands in the stream allowed by the configured compost system; zero contaminants (stickers, plastic) in compost; caddy lid closed.
wrong: Puts chicken bones in the backyard compost.
Leaves the produce sticker on the peel.
Throws all scraps in the trash.
protect: no pests drawn by an open caddy
fidelity: S: per-system acceptance list
notes: Related: Gardening 'Compost plant scraps' and kitchen compost entries.

interpretation: Wash containers that held spoiled or moldy food: scrape residue into the trash, wash with hot soapy water and a brush (including the lid gasket groove), sanitize, deodorize (baking-soda soak) if needed, dry fully and put reusable ones away; disposable ones are rinsed for recycling.
conditional: implicit: container cracked or mold stained into scratches -> discard rather than reuse; sound -> wash, sanitize, dry, reuse.
success: Container and lid have zero mold/residue soil including the gasket groove, odor below threshold, and are dry before being stored lidded; cracked or permanently contaminated ones discarded; sink and clean dishes not contaminated.
wrong: A quick cold rinse leaves mold film in the lid groove.
Washes it in the same water as clean dishes.
Stacks the containers wet with lids on.
fidelity: S: soil per surface region including the gasket groove

interpretation: Clean a spill inside the fridge (milk, raw meat juice, jam): take items off the affected shelf and the shelves below where it dripped, absorb the liquid, wash with warm soapy water or baking-soda solution (food-safe, no harsh solvent), sanitize where raw meat juice was, dry, wipe the bottoms of containers that sat in it, and put everything back promptly.
conditional: Raw meat/poultry juice -> sanitize affected surfaces and discard or rewash exposed ready-to-eat produce; benign spill (milk, juice, jam) -> wash and dry only.
success: Spill liquid removed from every contaminated surface (including the lower shelf/crisper it dripped into and the container bottoms); sanitized where raw juice was; no cleaner residue; food back inside within 2 h; fridge returns to <= 4 C.
wrong: Wipes the visible shelf but misses the drip into the crisper drawer.
Uses undiluted bleach spray, leaving residue on food-contact surfaces.
Leaves raw-chicken-juice-soaked lettuce in place.
protect: no food left out over 2 h
fridge door not left open long
cold glass shelf not cracked by hot water
fidelity: P: liquid spill spread and drip across shelves
notes: Fridge-spill cleaning also appears in kitchen cleaning sections; this occurrence is food-waste context (leaking spoiled food).

interpretation: Wipe up rainwater tracked or blown in at the entry doors - the floor just inside the threshold, the sill and sliding-door track, under the mat - with an absorbent towel or mop until the floor is dry, so no one slips and wood floors aren't damaged.
success: Water film on the interior floor within 1 m of the doors and in the sliding tracks reduced below the dry threshold; none left under the mat; the wet towel taken to laundry or hung.
wrong: Pushes water around with an already-soaked towel, enlarging the wet area.
Wipes the outside step and leaves the indoor puddle.
Leaves the soaked mat lying on the hardwood.
fidelity: P: water film area and absorption
notes: Overlaps 'Dry wet entryway' (next entry), which adds the wet items.

interpretation: Restore a rain-soaked entryway: dry the floor, swap the saturated mat for a dry one and hang the wet one, set wet shoes and boots on a boot tray, hang dripping coats where they drip onto a tray or tile, and leave the area safe to walk.
success: Floor dry; wet mat removed and hanging with a dry mat in place; wet shoes on the tray; coats hanging over a drip-safe area; slip hazard cleared.
wrong: Puts wet boots in the closet on carpet.
Leaves the soaked mat in place.
Hangs wet coats over wooden furniture.
protect: no water damage to wood or furniture
fidelity: P: water spread and absorption; S item placement
compound: move wet shoes to boot tray
hang wet coats over a drip area

interpretation: After outdoor play or a meal, clean what was used before it goes back to storage: wipe table and chairs, drain and wash the cooler and leave it open to dry, rinse grass and sand off game pieces, and let everything dry first.
conditional: implicit: item wet -> dry before storing; fabric cushions -> spot-clean rather than hose-soak unless water-rated.
success: Soil on every used item below threshold; cooler drained, washed and left open until dry; nothing stored dirty or wet.
wrong: Closes the cooler with meltwater inside (odor, mold).
Hoses down fabric cushions that aren't water-resistant.
Stores the games caked in mud.
fidelity: S: soil and moisture per item

interpretation: On a grill confirmed cold, scrape and brush the grate to remove carbonized food and grease (bristle-free scraper, or a brush whose bristles are checked), knock the debris into the firebox or drip tray, and wipe so no loose wire bristles remain on the cooking surface.
conditional: Grate still hot -> wait (this task is cold-only); grate cold -> clean.
success: Grate carbon/grease soil below threshold; zero loose bristles on the grate; cleaning started only when grate temperature was below the safe threshold.
wrong: Starts brushing a still-hot grate.
Leaves broken wire bristles stuck in the grate (ingestion hazard).
Brushes debris onto the patio.
fidelity: P: carbon/grease removal and grate temperature

interpretation: Clear the outdoor table after the meal: reusable dishes (including melamine that looks disposable) scraped and stacked for washing, leftovers routed to storage, disposables sorted into their streams, condiments brought back, then wipe the table.
success: Table empty and wiped; every reusable item in the wash area; every disposable in the correct stream; leftovers routed to storage; no reusable item in any waste stream.
wrong: Throws melamine plates and real cutlery into the trash with the paper plates.
Leaves sticky BBQ sauce on the table.
Scrapes food scraps onto the lawn.
fidelity: S: item classification and soil

interpretation: Collect all trash from the outdoor meal area - including small litter in the grass (bottle caps, wooden skewers, foil, corn cobs) - sorting it into trash, recycling and compost, tying the bags, and putting them in lidded outdoor bins with the lids secured against raccoons.
success: No litter left in the area (including small items in the grass); each item in its correct stream; bags tied and in lidded bins with lids secured.
wrong: Misses the skewers in the grass that the dog can eat.
Leaves the open bag by the door overnight.
Puts everything, cans included, into one trash bag.
protect: no wildlife or pet access to trash
fidelity: G: small-litter search on the lawn; S waste streams

interpretation: Wash the BBQ dishes: load dishwasher-safe items, hand-wash the rest (wooden-handled tools, cast iron, good knives, the digital meat thermometer), degrease the grill tools, and sanitize platters that held raw meat; everything ends clean, dry and undamaged.
conditional: Item dishwasher-safe -> dishwasher; not dishwasher-safe (wood, cast iron, electronics, fine knives) -> hand-wash; raw-meat contact -> sanitize step in either path.
success: All dishes at soil = 0, raw-meat platter sanitized, no dishwasher-incompatible item damaged, everything dry or on the rack drying.
wrong: Puts the digital meat thermometer and wooden board in the dishwasher.
Rinses the raw-chicken platter with water only.
Leaves greasy residue on the tongs.
fidelity: S: soil per item and appliance compatibility
notes: Duplicate wording in Evening routine (L1628); BBQ context adds greasy grill tools and raw-meat platters.

interpretation: Once the grill has cooled: brush the grates, empty and clean the grease tray and drip cup, wipe the exterior and side shelves, close the lid, and for a gas grill make sure the tank valve is closed; for charcoal, dispose of the ashes only when fully cold, into a metal container.
conditional: Gas grill -> close tank valve and clean the grease tray; charcoal grill -> verify ashes are cold (they can stay hot 24 h or more) before emptying into a metal can, never a plastic bin or trash bag. Grill still hot -> wait.
success: Grates and grease tray soil below threshold; tank valve closed (gas); ashes removed only when cold, into a metal can (charcoal); lid closed; no hot-ash events.
wrong: Dumps warm ashes into a plastic trash bin.
Leaves the propane valve open.
