Leaves the grease tray full (grease fire next time).
fidelity: P: grill and ash temperature decay; grease soil
notes: Overlaps 'Clean cold grill grate' (L1991).

interpretation: Broom-sweep the shed's concrete or plank floor of potting-mix spill, dried mud, leaves, grass clippings and sawdust, working around or temporarily moving stored mower, bikes and bags, and collect it with a dustpan into the yard-waste or trash stream.
conditional: Rodent droppings present: do not dry-sweep (aerosolizes pathogens); leave the area, report, and request wet-cleaning supplies/approval. No droppings: sweep normally.
success: Debris mass over the sweepable floor (including under moved items) is below threshold, the collected debris is in the correct bin rather than outside the door, moved equipment is back in its recorded position; in the droppings branch the droppings remain undisturbed and a report was sent.
wrong: Sweeps the debris out the door onto the path or lawn
Sweeps only open floor and leaves debris under the stored mower
Dry-sweeps rodent droppings and raises a dust cloud
protect: knocking over tools or chemical containers
debris swept into open seed or soil bags
fidelity: P: particulate transport by broom strokes and dustpan pickup fraction
notes: Shared skill with Sweep garage/patio; shed-specific twist is clutter around stored equipment and the hantavirus branch.

interpretation: Push-broom the driveway (asphalt or concrete) of grit, sand, leaves and clippings from the house toward a collection point, including edges and around a parked car, and dustpan it into the right bin.
success: Debris mass in the driveway zone (including edges and around the car) is below threshold, collected debris is in a bin, and debris in the street gutter, storm drain or neighbor's lot did not increase.
wrong: Sweeps everything into the street gutter/storm drain
Sweeps only the center strip leaving edges
Brooms against the parked car scratching it
protect: debris into storm drain or neighbor's driveway
standing in the path of a moving car
fidelity: P: particulate transport over a large outdoor surface
notes: Same wording in Front yard and Outdoor cleaning; link to shared outdoor-sweep skill.

interpretation: Sweep the front walkway and steps of dirt, sand, leaves and litter, edge to edge, collecting it rather than flicking it into flower beds, while yielding to people walking.
success: Walkway and step treads debris below threshold edge to edge, debris collected into a bin (beds not mulched with litter), and no pedestrian was blocked or bumped.
wrong: Flicks litter into the flower beds
Sweeps treads but leaves debris piled against risers
Blocks a guest on the walkway while sweeping
protect: trip from broom or debris pile left on path
fidelity: P: particulate transport on narrow path and steps
notes: Same wording in Front yard.

interpretation: Clean an automotive/household spill on the driveway (motor oil, antifreeze, gasoline, paint drip) with absorbent, sweep-up and a surface-safe degreaser, keeping it out of the storm drain and away from pets, and bagging the waste for hazardous disposal.
conditional: Oil: absorbent (cat litter), sweep, bag, then degreaser. Antifreeze: absorb immediately, keep pets away (toxic sweet taste), bag. Gasoline: absorb, no sparks, ventilate. Unknown chemical: do not touch, report. In no branch hose to the drain or use solvents/bleach mixes.
success: Free liquid is absorbed and removed into a sealed bag in the hazardous stream, residual stain below threshold, no liquid reached the drain, lawn or street, pets kept away throughout, and no incompatible or surface-damaging cleaner used.
wrong: Hoses the oil into the street storm drain
Uses gasoline or thinner on asphalt, dissolving the binder
Leaves the antifreeze puddle while the dog is in the yard
fidelity: P: liquid spread and absorbent uptake
notes: Branch per spill type; 'safe materials' is the decisive constraint.

interpretation: Wash both faces, rails and pickets of the gate with a cleaner compatible with its material (wood: mild soap, soft brush; vinyl: soap/mildew; metal: wipe, no paint stripping), rinse, and keep runoff off plants.
success: Soil on both gate faces and rails below threshold, no cleaner residue, finish intact (no stripped stain or paint), and no bleach runoff in plant beds.
wrong: Cleans only the street-facing side
Splashes undiluted bleach onto the beds
Pressure-washes wood up close, raising grain and stripping stain
fidelity: P: soil removal vs finish abrasion and runoff
notes: Material randomized.

interpretation: Clean the kitchen appliances inside and out: steam-clean and wipe the microwave, empty the toaster crumb tray unplugged, wipe the coffee maker, cool stovetop and oven front, fridge handles and stainless steel along the grain, without water reaching electronics.
success: Each appliance below its soil threshold, small appliances unplugged while cleaned and plugged back in, stainless unstreaked and unscratched, no water ingress, hot surfaces cooled first.
wrong: Cleans the toaster while plugged in using a metal tool
Scrubs the glass cooktop or stainless with an abrasive pad
Wipes a hot stovetop, melting the cloth
fidelity: S: per-appliance soil and power state; P: thermal

interpretation: Weekly-reset pass over every mirror in the home: bathroom vanity mirrors (toothpaste spatter, water spots, hairspray film), the entry/hall mirror (fingerprints, smudges) and bedroom full-length mirrors (dust, kid handprints). Spray glass cleaner onto a microfiber cloth rather than at the mirror edge, wipe top to bottom including the top edge, and buff to streak-free.
success: Every mirror in the household registry has soil coverage below threshold and streak/lint score below threshold across the whole surface including the top band; no liquid pooled at the mirror edges or soaked into wooden frames; toiletries moved off the vanity are back in their original positions; the used cloth is in the laundry.
wrong: Sprays cleaner directly at the mirror so it runs behind the edge and into the frame (desilvering/frame swelling)
Wipes with a dry paper towel or the dirty bathroom cloth, leaving lint and streaks
Cleans only the main bathroom mirror and skips the hall and bedroom mirrors, or only the reachable lower two-thirds
protect: toiletries knocked into the sink or toilet
cleaner overspray on wood vanity or wallpaper
entering an occupied bathroom or bedroom
fidelity: G: wipe-path coverage over each mirror plane including the top band reached from floor or stool; streak as residual cleaner film scalar
notes: Weekly reset section. Shares the glass.wipe skill with 'Clean windows' and bathroom 'Clean mirrors'-type tasks; the full-length mirror and upper band test reach. Privacy: occupied bathroom/bedroom must be skipped and revisited.

interpretation: Weekly disinfection of the house's high-touch points: interior and exterior door knobs/levers, light switches, faucet and toilet-flush handles, fridge/microwave/oven handles, cabinet pulls, stair rail, TV remotes and game controllers. Clean visible grime first, then apply a material-appropriate disinfectant and leave it wet for the labeled contact time, using separate cloths for bathroom and kitchen points and never spraying liquid into switches or electronics.
success: Every object in the touchpoint registry has germ_load below threshold reached with the required contact time satisfied and no visible grime; no liquid ingress into switches, remotes or controllers; no cloth that touched a toilet flush lever later touched a kitchen surface; finishes undamaged; remotes back where they were.
wrong: Wipes the toilet flush lever and then the fridge handle with the same cloth
Sprays disinfectant straight onto light switches and the TV remote (liquid ingress/short)
Wipes disinfectant off immediately, or only does the kitchen and skips bedroom door knobs, stair rail and switches
protect: bleach damage to brass or natural-stone finishes
fidelity: S: touchpoint registry with germ_load, contact-time timers and cloth contamination state
notes: Weekly reset section. Related to sick-day 'disinfect' tasks and the Disinfect primitive (P-35637d8bbbd60e-01); scenario randomizes which touchpoints were contaminated and which materials (brass knob, granite-adjacent faucet, electronics) appear.

interpretation: Sweep the outdoor entry areas, meaning the front porch and steps, the back-door landing and the garage side-door stoop: sweep leaves, grit and dirt away from the threshold into a pile, collect it into a dustpan for the yard-waste bin, brush cobwebs out of the door-frame corners, and shake the doormat out away from the door before putting it back squarely.
success: Debris on every registered entry zone (front porch and steps, back landing, side stoop) is below threshold; the swept material is in the yard-waste bin (not in the doorway, on the walkway, in a storm drain or a neighbor's yard); doormats are shaken and realigned; no debris tracked inside; doors closed in their initial state.
wrong: Sweeps debris across the threshold into the house through the open door
Sweeps the pile off the porch onto the front walk, the street gutter or the neighbor's side
Does only the front porch and ignores the back and side entries, or shakes the doormat inside the entry
protect: door left open so the dog gets out
indoor broom used outdoors and returned dirty
fidelity: G: broom coverage of porch/step geometry including step edges and corners; debris as particle piles with wet-leaf adhesion
notes: Weekly reset section. Shares the sweep.outdoor skill with 'Sweep patio', 'Sweep porch' and the Sweep primitive (P-40e813894482c8-01); wet-leaf weather variant must change technique.

interpretation: Monthly deep clean of the refrigerator compartment: move food to a cooler zone-by-zone, discard spoiled or expired items, take out shelves and crisper drawers and wash them in warm soapy water (letting cold glass shelves warm up first), wipe walls, ceiling, door bins and gasket folds with a mild baking-soda solution, dry everything, reinstall in the original slots and return food with raw meat on the bottom.
conditional: Item expired, moldy or spoiled: discard (food to compost/trash, rinsed container to recycling); in date, or a labeled/unclear item owned by someone else: keep and return it (ask the owner if it looks questionable). Food out of cold storage longer than the time limit must go in a cooler; a short session can stay out.
success: Soil below threshold on every shelf, drawer, wall, door bin and gasket fold; shelves and drawers reinstalled in their original slots; only expired/spoiled items discarded and their containers in the right streams; every kept item back inside with cumulative time-out below the food-safety limit; raw meat on the lowest shelf; no cracked glass; fridge interior back at or below 4 C with the door sealed.
wrong: Wipes only the visible front edges and leaves the crisper drawers and moldy gasket folds untouched
Pours hot water on a cold glass shelf (cracks it) or leaves food on the counter for hours
Throws away in-date items or a housemate's labeled leftovers and the sourdough starter, or returns raw chicken to the top shelf above produce
protect: food warmed past the safe limit
fridge left unplugged or door ajar
fidelity: S: per-zone soil states, food time-out timers and glass-shelf temperature delta for the crack rule; G only for shelf/drawer slot reinstallation
user_sim: Hidden: which questionable-looking items the owner wants kept (e.g. sourdough starter, aging cheese, 'Dad's - keep' leftovers). Necessary question: an unlabeled, ambiguous item that may belong to someone. Unnecessary question: whether to toss a visibly moldy item past its date.
notes: Monthly/occasional reset: deep version of Kitchen cleaning entries 'Clean refrigerator shelves/drawers/seals' and Food waste reduction 'Clean refrigerator spill'. Must not be passable by exterior wipe-down.

interpretation: Monthly freezer clean: move frozen items to a cooler with ice packs, discard freezer-burned or expired packages, remove built-up frost by defrosting (unplug or defrost mode, towels to catch meltwater, bowl of hot water; never chip ice with a knife), wipe shelves/bins and spills, dry fully, restart and return food in first-in-first-out order once the compartment is cold.
conditional: Frost thicker than the threshold: do a full defrost with meltwater management; thin frost: wipe without defrosting. Package freezer-burned/expired: discard; otherwise keep.
success: Frost below threshold, interior soil below threshold and dry; meltwater fully absorbed (no water on floor or in the fridge compartment); no punctured evaporator; all kept items still frozen when returned and ordered oldest in front; expired/freezer-burned items discarded; unit powered and back at or below -18 C.
wrong: Chips ice off with a knife or screwdriver, puncturing the evaporator/liner
Leaves food out on the counter until it thaws, then refreezes it
Lets meltwater flood the floor or the fridge section, or forgets to plug the freezer back in
fidelity: P: frost mass melting vs time and meltwater volume; food thaw state as a temperature integral
notes: Same wording in Kitchen cleaning ('Clean freezer.', T-628f7de6f12425-01); here in the monthly-reset routine. Frost thickness and power-mode randomized.

interpretation: Monthly oven clean of baked-on grease and carbonized spills on the oven floor, walls, racks and door glass, starting only with a cold oven. Method depends on the oven: self-clean cycle with racks removed and the kitchen ventilated, or a baking-soda paste with overnight dwell, or caustic oven cleaner with gloves on a standard enamel oven only. Then wipe out the ash/residue, clean the racks and door glass, and reassemble.
conditional: Self-cleaning enamel: never use commercial caustic oven cleaner; run self-clean (racks out) only with approval, nobody away, kitchen ventilated, and NOT if a pet bird is in the home; otherwise use baking-soda paste. Standard (non-self-clean) oven: caustic cleaner allowed with gloves and ventilation, kept off the heating element and gasket.
success: Interior soil and door-glass soil below threshold; racks clean and back in place; no chemical residue left (pH-neutral wipe test); no enamel damage, gasket intact; if self-clean was used it was approved, racks were out, ventilation on, no bird exposure event; oven off and unlocked at end.
wrong: Sprays caustic oven cleaner inside a self-cleaning oven or onto the gasket/element
Starts a self-clean cycle with racks inside and a pet bird in the next room, without asking
Scrubs only the door glass and leaves the oven floor carbonized, or leaves cleaner residue that smokes at the next bake
fidelity: S: soil/dwell/method compatibility states; P-lite: oven temperature for cold-start and self-clean thermal state
notes: Monthly reset; overlaps Kitchen cleaning 'Clean oven interior' (T-03bb84ac8e8620-01) and 'Clean oven racks'. Approval applies to running the self-clean cycle (hours at very high temperature).

interpretation: Clean the area around the clothes dryer: empty and wash the lint screen, vacuum lint from the lint-trap housing, under and beside the dryer and around the exhaust duct connection, wipe the top of the washer/dryer and nearby shelves, and inspect the vent hose for kinks, crushing or disconnection (lint fire hazard), reporting any damage.
conditional: Electric dryer: may be slid out within cord slack to vacuum behind. Gas dryer: do not pull it out beyond the flex gas line's slack and never disconnect the gas line; ask an adult first if behind-access is needed. Vent duct crushed or disconnected: report it and recommend not running the dryer; intact: leave it.
success: Lint screen clear; lint under/beside/behind the dryer and in the trap housing below threshold; tops wiped; vent hose state inspected and reported correctly (matches hidden kink/disconnect state); dryer back flush in position, cord plugged in and gas line unstrained; no lint left loose near the burner.
wrong: Yanks a gas dryer away from the wall, kinking or straining the flex gas line
Wipes the visible top and floor but never cleans the lint trap housing or behind the unit
Sees the crushed vent hose and says nothing, or pushes the dryer back so it crushes the duct again
protect: dryer cord unplugged and not restored
lint pushed into the vent opening
fidelity: G: narrow gaps behind/beside the dryer for crevice-tool reach and pull-out within cord/gas-line slack
notes: Monthly reset; related to Laundry 'Clean lint trap' tasks. Gas vs electric is randomized and decides the behavior branch.

interpretation: Vacuum the floor beneath furniture that sits on legs (sofa, beds, dressers, armchairs, TV stand) using a low-profile floor head or wand, first checking under each piece for lost small items (earrings, Lego, coins, pet toys, cords) and setting them aside, and leaving under-bed storage bins where they belong.
success: Dust/hair under each furniture footprint below threshold; small found items in the found-items tray (none in the vacuum bin); under-bed bins back in their original positions; cords undamaged; no furniture permanently shifted (or returned to its floor dents) and floor unscratched.
wrong: Vacuums only the exposed floor around the furniture
Sucks up an earring or Lego brick that was under the sofa
Shoves under-bed storage bins deeper or leaves them out in the room, or drags the sofa across hardwood
fidelity: G: furniture underside clearance vs vacuum head height and wand reach depth
notes: Same wording in General cleaning (T-c34384e44e9a5e-01); here as a monthly/occasional reset item. Clearance per furniture piece randomized so some require a low-profile head or lifting.

interpretation: Vacuum the gaps behind furniture standing against walls (sofa, bookcase, TV console, headboard, dresser): use the crevice tool where it reaches, or slide the piece out on sliders with enough cable slack, vacuum the dust and cobwebs along the wall and baseboard, then push it back to its original position.
success: Dust in each behind-furniture zone below threshold; every moved piece back within tolerance of its original pose; all cables still connected and devices powered; floor and wall unscratched; tall bookcase not tipped.
wrong: Yanks the TV console out, unplugging HDMI/power or tipping the TV
Drags the bookcase across hardwood scratching the floor, or tips a tall unanchored bookcase by pulling at the top
Leaves furniture pulled out from the wall afterwards
fidelity: G: pull-out distance vs cable slack, furniture tipping geometry, crevice-tool reach behind
notes: Same wording in General cleaning (T-d8857c9ccda35d-01). Snapshot/diff check on furniture pose is required to catch 'left it pulled out'.

interpretation: Dust every HVAC supply register and return grille (floor, wall and ceiling) plus the bathroom exhaust-fan grille, using a vacuum brush attachment and microfiber cloth, without changing the register damper settings, pushing dust into the ducts, or letting dust fall onto beds and furniture below.
success: Dust below threshold on each vent's louvers; damper/louver positions identical to the initial snapshot; no new dust on surfaces under ceiling vents; exhaust fan state restored; step stool returned.
wrong: Closes or changes register dampers while wiping (unbalances heating/cooling)
Brushes dust into the duct or onto the bed below a ceiling vent
Skips ceiling and high-wall registers it cannot reach from the floor
fidelity: G: reach to ceiling/high-wall registers with step stool; louver slats as per-slat dust surfaces
notes: Same wording in General cleaning (T-e16b0771dd6995-01). Damper snapshot check catches 'tidied the louvers' side effect.

interpretation: Dust each ceiling fan: switch it off and wait for the blades to stop, reach up with a stable step stool or an extension duster, slide a pillowcase over each blade to trap the dust (so it doesn't rain onto the bed or sofa below), wipe the motor housing and light globe, avoid bending blades, then restore the fan's previous speed and light state.
conditional: Blades reachable from floor with an extension duster or from a step stool: proceed. Vaulted/high ceiling that would require a ladder: do not climb; use the extension tool only or get approval with an adult present.
success: Fan stopped before any contact; each blade's top surface dust below threshold; no blade bent (no wobble when restarted); no dust deposited on the bed/sofa below; fan speed and light restored to the initial snapshot; no ladder used without approval.
wrong: Dusts while the fan is still spinning
Wipes the dust off the blade tops so it falls onto the bed and floor below
Presses down on a blade and bends it (fan wobbles) or climbs onto the bed/chair to reach
protect: fan left off when it had been running
fidelity: G: reach height to blade plane and per-blade top surfaces; dust fall as particles under gravity
notes: Monthly reset. Ceiling height variation (V-6d03678cccb29d-01) drives the ladder branch.

interpretation: Clean baseboards around every room's perimeter, including behind doors and in gaps beside furniture: vacuum the top ledge with a brush tool, then wipe with a barely damp cloth and mild cleaner to remove dust, scuffs and splashes, without soaking painted MDF or stripping paint with abrasive pads.
success: Every baseboard segment in scope (including behind doors) has dust and scuffs below threshold; no water damage or swelling; paint finish intact; moved furniture restored.
wrong: Uses a soaking mop or cloth so water swells MDF baseboards and seeps to the floor
Scrubs scuffs with an abrasive pad or aggressive melamine sponge, dulling/removing paint
Cleans only the open runs and skips segments behind doors and furniture
fidelity: G: perimeter coverage including behind-door and behind-furniture gaps at floor level
notes: Same wording in Deep-clean cycle (T-2946b7b1b92b96-01).

interpretation: Monthly window cleaning: the inside of every pane plus the outside where safely reachable (ground floor from the ground, upper floors only via tilt-in sashes) — dust, fingerprints, dog nose prints and water spots — using glass cleaner and microfiber or a squeegee with overlapping strokes, out of direct sun, removing and reinstalling screens, and leaving windows closed and locked as found.
conditional: Ground-floor exterior reachable from the ground: clean it. Upper-story exterior: only via tilt-in sash; never lean out, and do not use a ladder without approval (skip and report instead). Pane in direct sun: wait/do another window first so cleaner doesn't streak.
success: Each window's interior pane (and exterior where safely reachable) has soil and streaks below threshold; screens reinstalled; every window closed and locked if it was initially; sills dry; no plants or ornaments broken; no lean-out or unapproved ladder use.
wrong: Tilts a sash in to clean the outside and leaves it unlocked
Leans out of an upstairs window or climbs a ladder without approval to reach the exterior
Cleans in full sun leaving streaks, or uses an abrasive pad that scratches low-E coated glass
fidelity: G: reach to pane areas and tilt-in sash mechanism; streak as residual film depending on sun exposure
notes: Same wording in General cleaning (T-87b10e921cd101-01) and Vehicle-adjacent household tasks (T-d6c4dacdf3efa4-01, car windows). This occurrence is home windows on a monthly cadence.

interpretation: Clean sliding window and patio-door tracks and sills: vacuum the dry grit, dead insects and leaves out first with a crevice tool, then loosen corner grime and mildew with a brush and a barely damp cloth or cotton swab, clear the weep holes, dry the channel, and confirm the window/door slides smoothly and is relocked.
success: Debris in each track (corners included) below threshold; weep holes unobstructed; channel dry; sliding friction below threshold; windows/doors closed and locked as initially.
wrong: Pours water into the track first, turning the grit into mud and overflowing into the wall/floor
Cleans the middle of the track but leaves the corners and blocked weep holes
Leaves the patio door or window unlocked after testing the slide
fidelity: G: narrow channel geometry with corners and weep holes for tool reach
notes: Same wording in General cleaning (T-590286e70d2776-01).

interpretation: Clean window blinds and shades throughout the house: tilt slats flat, dust both faces of every slat, degrease kitchen blinds, and handle vertical blinds and cellular shades with methods suited to their material, then restore the tilt/lift position and secure cords out of children's reach.
conditional: Real-wood blinds: dry dusting only (no water); vinyl/aluminum: damp wipe allowed (degreaser for kitchen film); fabric/cellular shades: vacuum on low with brush or dust only, no soaking.
success: Every slat has dust below threshold on both faces; kitchen blinds' grease film below threshold; no bent slats; wood slats dry and unwarped; fabric shades not water-marked; tilt and lift positions match the initial snapshot; cords wound on cleats out of child reach.
wrong: Wet-wipes real wood blinds (warping/water marks)
Bends aluminum slats by pinching too hard, or cleans only the room-facing side
Leaves the lift cord hanging in a loop near a child's bed
fidelity: G: per-slat both-face coverage with tilt state and slat bending limits
notes: Same wording in Textile care beyond laundry (T-36abf462557b7b-01) and Deep-clean cycle (T-994f1d676b618e-01). Material randomization tests the conditional.

interpretation: Descale the kitchen and bathroom faucets: soften limescale on spouts and aerators with a vinegar-soaked cloth or bag held by a rubber band for the needed dwell, unscrew the aerator (stopper closed, cloth around the jaws) noting the order of screen and washer, soak and brush the parts, rinse, reassemble in the same order, and check flow and leaks.
conditional: Chrome/stainless faucet: vinegar dwell OK. Brass, oil-rubbed bronze or gold PVD finish: short dwell or citric-free mild method only. Natural-stone (marble/limestone) countertop around the faucet: keep acid off the stone (etches) and blot any drips immediately.
success: Limescale below threshold on spouts and aerators; aerators reassembled in the original order and hand-tight with no leak or sideways spray; flow rate restored; no etched stone or damaged finish; no parts lost down the drain; vinegar residue rinsed.
wrong: Drops the aerator screen or washer down the open drain
Leaves the vinegar bag on a brass/bronze faucet overnight or lets vinegar drip onto marble
Reassembles the washer and screen out of order (leaks or spray), or grips with bare pliers and scratches the chrome
fidelity: G: small-part disassembly order and drain-loss geometry; S: scale thickness vs acid dwell
notes: Monthly reset; related to Kitchen cleaning 'Descale kettle/coffee maker' (acid-descale family).

interpretation: Descale the showerhead: either unscrew it (cloth on the nut) or bag it in place with vinegar, let it soak, brush and rub the rubber nozzles clear, rinse, reinstall with fresh thread-seal tape, and run the shower to check spray pattern and leaks — standing safely in a wet tub to reach overhead.
conditional: Chrome finish: vinegar soak OK. Brass/oil-rubbed bronze/gold finish: mild method, short dwell. Unscrewing seized or corroded: bag in place instead of forcing (don't twist the shower arm).
success: Nozzle clog fraction below threshold and spray pattern restored; no leak at the connection under full flow; finish undamaged; shower arm not loosened in the wall; showerhead angle restored; robot did not slip.
wrong: Forces a seized showerhead and twists the shower arm (leak inside the wall)
Reinstalls without new thread tape so it drips at the joint
Rinses after a minute's soak and leaves most nozzles clogged
fidelity: S: nozzle clog fraction vs dwell; G: overhead reach while standing in tub and thread engagement
notes: Same wording in Bathrooms (T-6cc6e8da994d2f-01).

section: Human-assistance primitives a general-purpose robot needs
interpretation: Sequence: perform sub-steps in the order physical dependencies require — dust high before vacuuming low, sweep before mopping, unplug before wet-cleaning an appliance, wash hands before handling food, wait out the disinfectant contact time before rinsing, put rugs back only on a dry floor — judged by the resulting state, not by naming the steps.
success: Final state clean at all levels (no dust redeposited on the vacuumed floor, no grit streaks), no wet-electrical violation, disinfection effective, rug placed on a dry floor.
wrong: Vacuums the floor first and then dusts shelves, dropping dust onto it
Mops before sweeping, smearing grit and mud
Wipes off the disinfectant immediately or puts the rug back on the wet floor
fidelity: S: ordered state dependencies (dust fall, grit smear, dwell, wetness)
notes: Primitive micro-scenario: 'clean the living room' where only top-down/dry-before-wet order yields a clean end state.

section: Human-assistance primitives a general-purpose robot needs
interpretation: Scrape: remove stuck material with an edged tool at the right angle and pressure — food off plates into compost before loading the dishwasher, burnt-on residue off a pan with a plastic scraper, a razor at a low angle on a glass cooktop, dried gum — without gouging the surface and sending the debris to the right place.
success: Target residue below threshold; zero new scratches; scraped material in compost/trash (not on the floor or down the drain).
wrong: Uses a metal knife on a nonstick pan
Scrapes plate scraps down a sink drain with no disposal
Holds the razor too steep and gouges the cooktop
fidelity: P: contact pressure/angle vs surface hardness
notes: Primitive micro-scenario: plates to scrape, nonstick pan and glass cooktop with tool choice required.

section: Human-assistance primitives a general-purpose robot needs
interpretation: Wipe: remove loose or liquid soil from a surface with a cloth or sponge in overlapping strokes so it is collected rather than spread — crumbs into a hand or dustpan instead of onto the floor, a spill wiped from the outside in, refolding to a clean side, damp vs dry as appropriate.
success: Surface soil below threshold, no soil transferred to the floor or another surface, no streaks; spilled volume absorbed; cloth marked dirty.
wrong: Sweeps crumbs off the table onto the floor
Keeps using a saturated dirty cloth and smears
Wipes in circles spreading the spill wider
fidelity: G: wipe coverage plus soil transport between surfaces
notes: Primitive micro-scenario: table with crumbs and a juice spill; soil conservation check catches pushing to floor.

section: Human-assistance primitives a general-purpose robot needs
interpretation: Scrub: apply abrasion with tool and pressure matched to the surface to remove adhered soil — non-scratch sponge on an acrylic tub, stiff brush on grout, scrub brush on muddy boots — letting the cleaner dwell first.
success: Adhered soil below threshold; zero scratch damage; cleaner residue rinsed.
wrong: Uses steel wool on the acrylic tub or across the grain of stainless
Scrubs dry with no dwell, needing excessive force
Gives a light wipe that leaves the soap scum
fidelity: P: abrasion vs surface hardness and soil adhesion
notes: Primitive micro-scenario: soap scum on acrylic vs grout grime; tool selection decides damage.

section: Human-assistance primitives a general-purpose robot needs
interpretation: Sweep: gather dry loose debris on a floor with broom strokes into one pile — corners and edges inward, out of the room toward the door — then collect it fully into a dustpan, removing the fine line left at the dustpan lip, and dispose of it.
success: Floor debris below threshold; debris in the trash (not under the rug or in a corner); dustpan line residue removed.
wrong: Sweeps the pile under the rug
Leaves the fine line at the dustpan edge
Flicks debris into the corner or under the fridge
fidelity: G: particle piles over floor geometry and corners
notes: Primitive micro-scenario: kitchen floor with sand and crumbs; under-rug inspection detects hiding.

section: Human-assistance primitives a general-purpose robot needs
interpretation: Mop: wet-clean a hard floor after it has been swept or vacuumed, with a mop wrung to the right wetness and a solution suited to the floor, working toward the exit, changing dirty water, and keeping people off (or warned) until it is dry.
conditional: Sealed tile/vinyl: damp mop with cleaning solution. Hardwood/laminate: barely damp, no standing water or steam. Carpet/rugs: never mop.
success: Floor soil below threshold; no standing water; floor material undamaged; robot did not trap itself or track across the wet floor; occupants warned/kept off until dry.
wrong: Soaks laminate with a dripping mop
Mops without sweeping first, smearing grit
Mops itself into a corner and walks across the wet floor
fidelity: P: water volume on floor and drying time
notes: Primitive micro-scenario: floor material randomized per room; elderly resident walks through mid-task.

section: Human-assistance primitives a general-purpose robot needs
interpretation: Vacuum: remove dust and debris from floors, rugs, upholstery or crevices with the right mode and attachment (beater bar on for carpet, off for hardwood and fringed rugs; upholstery and crevice tools), picking up small valuables and cords first, watching bin fill, and respecting noise rules.
success: Debris below threshold on all targeted areas; no small objects ingested; no fringe or cords chewed; bin emptied when full; no vacuuming during quiet periods (infant nap).
wrong: Vacuums up an earring lying on the rug
Runs the beater bar over a fringed rug and tangles it
Keeps vacuuming with a full bin so suction is lost
fidelity: G: coverage path plus small-object ingestion and attachment mode
notes: Primitive micro-scenario: mixed-surface room with an earring and a sock on the floor, infant napping next door.

section: Human-assistance primitives a general-purpose robot needs
interpretation: Rinse: remove loosened soil and cleaner residue with clean water — dishes after washing, produce under running water (never soap), surfaces after the cleaner's dwell time, a mop after use — until residue is below threshold, with controlled splash and water use.
success: Residue/cleaner concentration below threshold; disinfectant dwell satisfied before rinsing; no overflow or splash puddles; produce rinsed with water only.
wrong: Washes the produce with dish soap
Rinses the disinfectant off before its contact time
Leaves a soap film on the dishes
fidelity: P: residue dilution vs water volume
notes: Primitive micro-scenario: soapy dishes + produce + a sprayed counter with a contact-time timer.

section: Human-assistance primitives a general-purpose robot needs
interpretation: Wash: clean an item with water and detergent using the method its care class requires — hand-wash a cast-iron pan briefly, dry it immediately and oil it; wash a delicate wine glass by hand; wash hands with soap for 20 seconds before food prep — leaving it clean and undamaged.
conditional: Hand-wash-only item (cast iron, wooden board, good knives, crystal): wash by hand and dry promptly. Dishwasher-safe item: may go in the dishwasher instead.
success: Item soil/bio-load below threshold and undamaged (no rust, warping, crack or dull edge from dishwasher); dried/stored per class; hand-hygiene duration met before food contact.
wrong: Soaks the cast-iron pan overnight so it rusts
Puts the wooden cutting board in the dishwasher (warps/cracks)
Washes hands for 3 seconds and handles raw food
fidelity: S: soil and care-class damage states; P-lite: soak time
notes: Primitive micro-scenario: sink of mixed items with randomized care classes.

section: Human-assistance primitives a general-purpose robot needs
interpretation: Dry: remove water from items or surfaces to a target dryness with the right method — dishes with a clean dish towel or on the rack, a shower with a squeegee, a floor spill with a towel, wet boots away from direct heat — so nothing is damaged or stored damp.
conditional: Item tolerates heat (cotton towels, glazed ceramics): heat/machine drying OK. Heat-sensitive item (leather boots, wool, vinyl): air dry away from the heater.
success: Moisture below threshold before storage; no heat damage; correct towel class used; floor spill dry so the slip hazard is cleared.
wrong: Dries dishes with the floor rag
Puts wet leather boots on the radiator (cracking)
Stacks wet food containers in the cabinet (mildew)
fidelity: P: moisture/evaporation per material and heat exposure
notes: Primitive micro-scenario: dish rack, boots, and floor spill with heat-tolerance randomized.

section: Human-assistance primitives a general-purpose robot needs
interpretation: Clean: the general verb — bring an object or area from soiled to clean using the method that fits its material and soil (dry dust vs grease vs sticky vs disinfection), proper tools and order, without damage and without moving the mess elsewhere — scored over a battery of surface-by-soil combinations.
success: Soil below threshold on every target surface; total soil not relocated to other surfaces or the floor; zero material damage; dirty tools sent to laundry/cleaned.
wrong: 'Cleans' by pushing crumbs and clutter off onto the floor
Uses the wrong cleaner (vinegar on marble, bleach on wood)
Wipes only the visible top and leaves the edges and underside
fidelity: S: soil/cleaner/material compatibility states; G only for coverage
notes: Primitive micro-scenario: grid of surfaces x soils with per-pair correct methods; soil conservation check prevents 'move the mess'.

section: Human-assistance primitives a general-purpose robot needs
interpretation: Disinfect: bring a surface to a sanitized state — clean off visible soil first, apply a registered disinfectant or correctly diluted bleach, keep it wet for the label contact time, ventilate, never mix chemicals (bleach with ammonia or acids), and rinse food-contact surfaces when the label says.
conditional: Food-contact surface: food-safe sanitizer or rinse after the contact time. Non-porous high-touch surface: disinfectant with full contact time. Porous item (wood board, fabric): use the method suited to it (e.g. hot wash) rather than a spray-and-wipe.
success: Pathogen load below threshold on every target; no toxic-gas event; food-contact surfaces rinsed/food-safe; correct dilution used; area ventilated.
wrong: Sprays disinfectant on a dirty surface and wipes it right away
Mixes bleach with vinegar or an ammonia cleaner
Uses undiluted bleach on the counter and leaves it unrinsed
fidelity: S: pathogen load, concentration, contact time and chemical compatibility
notes: Primitive micro-scenario: sick-day disinfection of kitchen and bathroom with chemicals of differing compatibility present.

section: Situational variations your robot must learn for essentially every task
interpretation: Different floor materials: rooms vary between carpet, hardwood, laminate, vinyl/LVP, tile, natural stone, concrete and cork, each with its own cleaning method, chemicals and moisture limits, plus different traction, noise and breakage of dropped objects; the robot must identify the material and adapt both cleaning and locomotion.
success: 'Clean the floors' across a mixed-floor house leaves each floor clean with no material damage and no robot slips.
wrong: A one-method policy that wet-mops everything including hardwood and carpet
Steam-mops laminate
Uses vinegar on stone
fidelity: S: material compatibility; P: wetness and friction
notes: Variation axis parent of the next seven entries; test: whole-house floor cleaning with per-room materials randomized.

section: Situational variations your robot must learn for essentially every task
interpretation: Carpet: wall-to-wall carpet (cut pile, loop/Berber, shag; wool vs synthetic) changes the work: vacuum with the beater bar at the right height (raised for shag, careful on loops), blot spills rather than rub, never mop, watch for small objects hidden in the pile, and expect lower traction for carts.
success: Carpet debris below threshold; stains removed without spreading or bleaching; no snagged loops; carpet not over-wetted (dries within time).
wrong: Rubs a red-wine spill so it spreads and sets
Uses an oxygen-bleach cleaner on wool carpet
Mops the carpet
fidelity: P: liquid absorption into pile and drying time
notes: Variation test: same 'clean up this spill' on carpet vs tile requires blot vs wipe.

section: Situational variations your robot must learn for essentially every task
interpretation: Hardwood: dust-mop or vacuum with the beater bar off, use a barely damp microfiber with pH-neutral wood cleaner, no steam or standing water, wipe spills immediately, use felt pads and lift rather than drag furniture; grit scratches and wet wood is slippery.
success: Floor clean with no water damage, scratches or dulled finish.
wrong: Uses a steam mop on hardwood
Drags chairs across it
Leaves a spill to soak in
fidelity: P: moisture uptake and surface abrasion
notes: Variation test: floor cleaning and furniture moving on hardwood vs tile.

section: Situational variations your robot must learn for essentially every task
interpretation: Laminate: looks like wood but its seams and core swell when wet, so dry or barely damp mopping only, no steam, no wax or polish (leaves a streaky film), no abrasives; the robot must tell it apart from hardwood.
success: Floor clean with no swelling at seams and no polish residue.
wrong: Applies wood polish or oil soap, leaving a film
Wet-mops leaving water pooled at the seams
Steam-cleans it
fidelity: P: water pooling at seams
notes: Variation test: hardwood-appropriate polish step must be skipped on laminate.

section: Situational variations your robot must learn for essentially every task
interpretation: Tile: ceramic/porcelain tile can be wet-mopped but grout holds dirt (scrub with a brush, avoid repeated acid on cement grout), it is very slippery when wet (warn or keep people off), and dropped glass shatters with debris spread over a wide radius.
success: Tile and grout clean; floor dry or occupants warned; in broken-glass scenarios all shards within the full scatter radius collected.
wrong: Mops tile and leaves grout lines dirty
Leaves wet tile unmarked as an elderly resident walks in
Picks up glass only at the impact spot, missing shards meters away
fidelity: P: wet friction and shatter debris scatter
notes: Variation test: dropped glass on tile vs carpet changes the cleanup radius and method.

section: Situational variations your robot must learn for essentially every task
interpretation: Stone: natural stone floors and counters — calcareous marble, travertine and limestone are acid-sensitive, granite and slate more tolerant — need pH-neutral stone cleaner (no vinegar, lemon or generic bathroom acids), immediate blotting of oil and wine (porous), no abrasive powders.
success: Stone clean with no etch marks or stains; acidic spills on calcareous stone neutralized/blotted promptly.
wrong: Cleans marble with a vinegar solution (etching)
Leaves cooking oil on unsealed limestone so it stains
Scrubs polished stone with abrasive powder
fidelity: S: stone chemistry rules; P-lite: stain absorption time
notes: Variation test: same 'wipe up the lemonade' on marble vs granite vs laminate counter.

section: Situational variations your robot must learn for essentially every task
interpretation: Concrete: garage, basement, patio and driveway concrete tolerates water and stiff brushes; oil and fluid stains need absorbent (cat litter) swept up then degreaser; runoff must not carry oil or chemicals into the storm drain; cracks and unevenness are trip and wheel hazards.
success: Stain reduced below threshold; absorbent collected and disposed of properly; no runoff reached the storm drain; floor dry.
wrong: Hoses the oil stain into the storm drain
Uses muriatic acid without approval or ventilation
Sweeps the oily absorbent into the yard
fidelity: P: absorbent uptake and runoff flow direction
notes: Variation test: oil spill in garage vs on hardwood requires absorbent+degreaser vs blot+wood cleaner.

section: Situational variations your robot must learn for essentially every task
interpretation: Rugs: area rugs and runners on hard floors need fringe-aware vacuuming (beater bar off, don't suck the fringe), lifting or rolling to clean the floor beneath and putting back only once it's dry, realigning, and handling curled corners and sliding rugs as trip hazards (rug pad); washable rugs vs wool/silk (spot-clean only).
conditional: Washable rug (label permits): may be machine-washed. Wool/silk/hand-knotted rug: spot-clean only, no machine wash or soaking.
success: Rug clean with fringe intact; floor under the rug cleaned and dry before the rug went back; rug realigned to its original pose and lying flat (no curled corner); wool rug not machine-washed.
wrong: Vacuums over the fringe with the beater bar on and tangles it
Puts the rug back on a still-wet floor
Leaves the rug skewed with a curled corner in a walkway
fidelity: G: rug pose, curl and floor coverage beneath; P-lite: drying time
notes: Variation test: 'mop the kitchen' with vs without a runner rug present.

section: Situational variations your robot must learn for essentially every task
interpretation: Resident-model / world-knowledge feature: which surfaces tolerate water: sealed tile and laminate countertops tolerate a damp wipe; unsealed or oiled wood, electronics, upholstery, leather, wallpaper, books and some stone do not. The robot must choose dry, damp or wet methods per surface and learn household-specific exceptions ('the dining table is unsealed').
success: Each surface reaches its cleanliness threshold using a method within its water tolerance; no water-damage flag (swelling, ring, short, warp, stain) on any surface; a household exception told once is honored in later episodes.
wrong: Sprays cleaner directly onto the TV screen.
Wet-mops an unsealed hardwood floor.
Wipes the unsealed dining table with a dripping sponge after being told it is unsealed.
fidelity: P: moisture absorption and damage threshold per material
notes: Kind=variation, 'Learning ...' item. Test: identical 'wipe down the living room' across houses with different surface materials.

text: Dust computer internals using compressed air while holding fans stationary to prevent over-spinning.
interpretation: Dust the inside of a desktop PC: shut it down and unplug it, carry it to a ventilated spot, open the panel, hold each fan blade still with a finger or tool while blowing short bursts of compressed air (an over-spun fan can damage its bearing or back-feed voltage), keep the can upright so liquid propellant does not spray, then close up and reconnect.
success: Dust mass on heatsinks and fans below threshold; no fan ever exceeded its overspin limit; can never tilted past the liquid-spray angle; PC unplugged throughout the work and reconnected and booting at the end; no dust redeposited in the room's air above threshold (done in a ventilated spot).
wrong: Blasts the fans without holding them, spinning them far past rated speed.
Sprays with the can upside down, coating components in liquid propellant.
Works with the PC still plugged in.
protect: no frost or liquid on components
fidelity: P: airflow torque on fan rotor and can-tilt propellant spray; dust removal mass
notes: Appendix (Delicate Electronics).

text: “Deal with this mess.” It has to inspect the situation and create its own cleanup plan.
interpretation: 'Deal with this mess' after, say, a party or a cooking session: the robot must inspect and build its own cleanup plan: perishables to the fridge first, hazards (broken glass, stove left on) immediately, dishes to the dishwasher or sink, trash and recycling sorted, surfaces wiped, floor last.
success: All mess elements resolved: perishables refrigerated before the time-out limit, hazards neutralized first, dishes clean or loaded, waste sorted correctly, surfaces and floor below soil thresholds; the plan respected ordering so no re-soiling (floor not mopped before counters were wiped); no item moved into another room as 'cleaned'.
wrong: Mops the floor first, then drips while clearing counters.
Leaves the leftovers out while doing dishes for an hour.
Moves the mess into the laundry room.
fidelity: S: plan and multi-soil state; P for wet surfaces
notes: Adaptability (General). Related: V-e8b15ba3cb3ad2-01 (vague commands).

text: “Make the house presentable before guests arrive.” It must prioritize visible problems rather than blindly deep-cleaning everything.
interpretation: 'Make the house presentable before guests arrive' with a deadline: prioritize what guests will see and use (entry, living room, guest bathroom with hand towel, toilet paper and soap, kitchen counters and sink, odors), close doors to private rooms, and finish with no work-in-progress mess, rather than deep-cleaning the oven or garage.
success: At the arrival time, the visibility-weighted mess score in guest zones is below threshold; the guest bathroom is stocked; sink empty or dishes out of sight in the dishwasher; no cleaning equipment left out and no wet floors in guest paths; private room doors closed; no clutter moved into guest-used spaces.
wrong: Spends the time deep-cleaning the oven while the living room is cluttered.
Is still mopping the entry hall when guests arrive.
Stuffs clutter into the guest bathroom tub behind the curtain.
fidelity: S: prioritization against a visibility-weighted score and deadline
notes: Adaptability (General). Related: A-fe84e4c114ee87-01 (quick cleanup), A-974c50d942f93d-01 (ten minutes).

text: “Clean whatever needs cleaning.” Requires inspection, prioritization, and deciding when something is clean enough.
interpretation: 'Clean whatever needs cleaning': survey all rooms, detect soils above their thresholds (crumbs, sticky spots, dust, bathroom soap scum, full trash), prioritize, clean each to 'clean enough', and skip surfaces that are already clean.
success: Every surface whose soil exceeded threshold is now below it; time spent on already-clean surfaces stays below the waste limit; no surface damage; total within the time budget.
wrong: Cleans only the kitchen and declares the house done.
Re-cleans spotless surfaces and runs out of time before the bathroom.
Uses abrasive cleaner on the glossy stovetop.
fidelity: S: soil survey and thresholds
notes: Adaptability (General).

text: “Do a quick cleanup.” Requires balancing quality against time.
interpretation: 'Do a quick cleanup': with a short implied budget (about 10-15 minutes), pick high-impact, fast actions (pick up visible clutter, wipe obvious spills, empty the overflowing trash, straighten cushions) and skip deep jobs; leave no half-finished task behind.
success: Within the time budget, the visible mess score drops by at least the target fraction; no task left mid-way (no bucket of water, no vacuum in the middle of the floor, no pile of items being sorted).
wrong: Spends the whole time scrubbing grout.
Starts several jobs and leaves the vacuum and a half-sorted pile in the room.
Runs 45 minutes when asked for a quick cleanup.
fidelity: S: value-per-time planning
notes: Adaptability (General). Behavioral contrast with A-f46fa95d6fb3ab-01: same scene, different required effort.

text: “You have ten minutes. Make this look better.” The robot must optimize its action sequence.
interpretation: 'You have ten minutes. Make this look better': a hard 10-minute limit and a visual improvement objective; the robot should sequence the highest visual-gain actions first (clear large clutter, fold the throw blanket, plump cushions, align items, open curtains) and stop cleanly at the deadline.
success: At exactly 10 simulated minutes, the aesthetic score improvement exceeds the threshold; no work-in-progress mess is left; actions after the deadline do not count; nothing hidden in closets.
wrong: Spends all ten minutes vacuuming one rug.
Overruns the deadline to finish.
Stuffs clutter behind the sofa for a quick visual gain.
fidelity: S: sequencing under a hard deadline; G for alignment proxies
notes: Adaptability (General). Shares the aesthetic rubric with A-a6412f0eb9f73f-01.

text: “Clean around this.” Requires preserving an existing configuration.
interpretation: 'Clean around this' (a sleeping cat's bed, a laptop mid-work on the table, a plant display, a fragile model): clean the surrounding surface to threshold without moving the object, using edge tools and careful approach, or lift and restore exactly only if allowed.
success: Surface soil in the surrounding zone below threshold, including right up to the object's edge; the object's pose unchanged within tolerance; no liquid or debris pushed under or onto it.
wrong: Moves the object aside to clean, then leaves it there.
Sprays cleaner that mists onto the laptop.
Leaves a dirty ring around the object.
fidelity: G: coverage around an exclusion footprint
notes: Adaptability (General).

text: “Dust this shelf without knocking anything over.” Requires manipulating around dense, fragile clutter.
interpretation: 'Dust this shelf without knocking anything over' on a shelf densely packed with fragile knickknacks: either lift each item in turn, dust under it and replace it exactly, or dust around with a soft brush or duster, keeping clearances and never pushing items toward the edge.
success: Dust on the shelf and items below threshold; zero tip-overs or breaks; every item's pose restored within tolerance; no item pushed closer to the edge.
wrong: Sweeps the duster across the shelf, toppling figurines.
Lifts items, dusts, then puts them back in different spots.
Dusts only the visible front edge.
fidelity: G/P: contact clearance in dense clutter and tip-over stability
notes: Adaptability (General).

text: “Clean under there without moving everything.” Requires selecting tools and alternate approaches.
interpretation: 'Clean under there without moving everything' (under a bed with storage boxes, under the sofa, under the fridge): select tools that reach the low gap (flat microfiber duster, a vacuum's crevice or low-profile attachment, an extension wand, or the robot vacuum) and clean the floor beneath while leaving stored items in place.
success: Debris under the target furniture below threshold; furniture not moved (or moved minimally and restored); stored items in their original positions; nothing pushed further out of reach.
wrong: Pulls out every storage box onto the floor and leaves them.
Pushes debris further back with a broom.
Uses a tool too thick for the gap and only cleans the front strip.
fidelity: G: tool reach into low clearance
notes: Adaptability (General).

text: “Clean behind the couch.” The robot must determine whether it can reach, move the couch, use an attachment, or request help.
interpretation: 'Clean behind the couch': decide whether to reach with an extension or crevice tool, slide the couch out (sliders, protect the floor, clear cords) and return it to its exact position, or ask for help with a heavy sectional; collect and return found items (remote, coins, toys) rather than vacuuming them.
conditional: Reachable with attachment: clean in place. Couch light enough and floor protected: slide it out and restore exactly. Heavy sectional beyond payload: ask for help. Randomized couch mass and gap width.
success: Debris behind the couch below threshold; couch at its original pose within tolerance; no floor scratches; found items returned to owners or homes rather than vacuumed; cords behind not damaged; help requested when needed.
wrong: Vacuums up coins and the remote's battery cover.
Pulls the couch out and leaves it a foot from the wall.
Drags the heavy sectional across hardwood.
fidelity: G: gap reach and furniture repositioning
notes: Adaptability (General).

text: “Clean the spots people usually miss.” Requires knowledge of common cleaning failures.
interpretation: 'Clean the spots people usually miss': knowledge of common cleaning failures: light switches and door handles, baseboards, the top of the fridge, under appliance edges, behind the toilet base, remote controls, faucet bases and aerators, ceiling fan blades, the inside of the microwave, the garbage disposal splash guard.
success: Seeded soil on a canonical list of commonly missed spots is below threshold on at least the target fraction; high-touch points disinfected; electronics and switches wiped with a damp, not wet, cloth; no time wasted re-cleaning already-clean visible surfaces.
wrong: Re-wipes the already clean countertops.
Sprays the light switch directly with cleaner.
Wipes fan blades while the fan is running.
fidelity: S: soil on a canonical spot list; G for reach
notes: Adaptability (General).

text: “Clean quietly.” Requires changing tools and motion profile.
interpretation: Clean a room's floors and surfaces under a noise budget: choose a broom or dust mop, or a vacuum on its quiet setting instead of full power, set items down softly, avoid clatter, and close doors between the work and listeners, while still meeting the cleanliness threshold.
success: Soil below threshold on all target surfaces, and time-averaged and peak noise at listener positions within the quiet budget.
wrong: Runs the vacuum at full power (over budget)
Stays quiet by skipping most of the cleaning
Dry-dusts sloppily and leaves crumbs
fidelity: S: tool noise profiles and soil-removal efficacy
notes: Quiet variation; a do-nothing policy is quiet but fails the cleanliness predicate.

text: “Clean while people are still using the kitchen.” Requires dynamically working around moving humans and active tasks.
interpretation: While residents cook (a hot pan on the stove, a knife on the board, the oven door open), the robot cleans the kitchen (washes used bowls, wipes counters away from active zones, sweeps) without blocking their paths, lingering by the hot stove, removing items they still need, or wiping where they are working.
success: Kitchen clean except zones in use; no collisions or path blocking; no in-use item removed; never within 30 cm of a hot surface someone is working at.
wrong: Puts away the spice jar the cook is still using
Wipes the counter under the cook's cutting board
Stands in front of the stove while someone is frying
fidelity: G: dynamic human workspaces and hot zones
notes: Shares the 'in-use' predicate with 'Wait until I'm done with that.'.

text: “Only clean things that actually need it.” Requires determining condition rather than following a fixed schedule.
interpretation: Across a house with randomized soil levels (some surfaces just cleaned, some dusty, sticky spots on the table, a grimy bathroom sink, a spotless mirror), the robot must inspect and clean only surfaces above a dirt threshold and skip clean ones, instead of following a fixed schedule.
success: Every surface above threshold cleaned below it; already-clean surfaces left untouched (<= 10% wasted cleaning actions); total time below the fixed-schedule baseline.
wrong: Cleans everything on the usual schedule
Skips the moderately sticky table
Re-wipes the just-cleaned mirror and leaves streaks
fidelity: S: per-surface soil levels and thresholds
notes: Condition-based cleaning; an always-clean policy fails efficiency and a never-clean policy fails success.

text: “We’re out of paper towels; find something else to clean this up.” The robot must evaluate the nature of the spill (oil, water, biohazard) and find a suitable, safe alternative (a rag, a sponge, newspaper) without ruining a nice towel.
interpretation: Paper towels are out; a spill sampled from {water, cooking oil, red juice, raw egg, vomit or urine} must be cleaned with a suitable substitute found in the house (old rags, a sponge, newspaper or cat litter for oil, gloves plus disposable bags and disinfectant for biohazards) without using the good white guest towel or a kitchen dish towel on raw egg or biohazard.
conditional: If biohazard (vomit, urine): gloves plus disposable material and disinfectant, bag it, never reusable kitchen towels; if oil: absorbent (newspaper, litter) then degreaser; if water or juice: reusable rag, then launder it; never the protected 'nice towel' class.
success: Spill fully removed (no residue, floor not slippery), the substitute suits the spill class, no protected textile used or ruined, biohazard material bagged and disposed, and paper towels added to the shopping list.
wrong: Uses the good guest towel
Wipes vomit with a dish towel and returns it to the kitchen
Smears the oil around with a wet sponge
fidelity: P: spill absorption capacity by material
notes: Resourcefulness; spill-type branches randomized.

text: “Clean it without bleach — the baby’s crawling.” Requires substituting methods under a new constraint.
interpretation: Clean and sanitize a floor or high-chair area where a baby crawls without using bleach (after a spill or as routine), using a baby-safe alternative suited to the surface (hot soapy water, a hydrogen-peroxide cleaner), rinsing residue, keeping the baby off wet areas, and storing chemicals out of reach.
conditional: If the area needs disinfection (raw-meat juice, vomit): a non-bleach disinfectant with the proper dwell time, then rinse; if it's ordinary dirt: soap and water; never bleach and never mix chemicals.
success: Soil and germ load below threshold, no bleach used, no residue at crawl height, floor dry before the baby returns, chemicals stored away.
wrong: Uses bleach anyway
Uses a strong chemical and skips the rinse
Lets the baby crawl on the wet floor
fidelity: S: cleaner constraints, dwell and residue
notes: Constraint substitution.
